sections.body: {{A}}'s supporting 1 introduces an internal critic that shows up outwardly as opinions about how things *should* be done — correctly, thoroughly, with integrity. {{B}}'s supporting 9, by contrast, tends to smooth over imperfections and avoid friction, which can read to {{A}} as passivity or lack of standards. Meanwhile, {{A}}'s 1-driven critique can feel jarring or unnecessarily harsh to {{B}}, whose 9 is wired to preserve peace. Over time, {{A}} may feel like they're always the one raising the bar while {{B}} silently resents being held to it.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s 9-supported conflict-avoidance as indifference or complacency — 'If you cared, you'd push back or engage more seriously.' {{B}} reads {{A}}'s 1-backed correction and idealism as controlling or unnecessarily tense — 'Why can't we just enjoy this without turning it into a project?' Both are genuinely trying to be helpful (the shared 2 confirms this), but {{A}} helps by improving and {{B}} helps by soothing, and neither always recognizes the other's method as care.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should flag when criticism is coming from the 1's reforming impulse versus a genuine relational concern — naming it disarms it.
- {{B}} should practice voicing preferences directly rather than deferring; the 9's habit of self-erasure leaves {{A}} without real feedback to calibrate against.
- Both share a 7 tendency to reframe discomfort into optimism — agree on a signal for when one of you actually needs the other to sit with a problem rather than solve or brighten it.
- Lean on the shared 2 energy to check in emotionally before launching into planning or critique mode.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} can model for {{A}} that not every imperfection requires intervention — the 9's acceptance is a genuine skill, not laziness, and it can soften {{A}}'s sometimes relentless 1-driven self-criticism. {{A}} in turn can model healthy discernment for {{B}}, showing that naming a problem or holding a standard is an act of respect, not aggression. The shared 7 lead means both are growth-oriented at their best, and the 2 gives them genuine motivation to show up for each other's development. The risk is that both use 7's reframing to sidestep the friction entirely — real growth here requires letting the 1 and the 9 have their honest disagreement rather than papering it over with enthusiasm.

127-712.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share the same tritype archetype and genuinely want the same things — to improve the world, connect meaningfully, and inspire others. Yet because {{A}} leads from the gut with a 1's moral seriousness while {{B}} leads from the head with a 7's expansive optimism, the same values get enacted in strikingly different rhythms. This is a pair that can either feel like a perfect complement or a low-grade, ongoing friction about how life should actually be lived.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the 2's warmth and generosity, making this a relationship with genuine mutual care at its core.
- The shared 1 energy means both take ethics, improvement, and doing right by others seriously — you don't have to explain why integrity matters.
- The shared 7 energy means enthusiasm for ideas, learning, and possibility is present in both, even if {{A}} accesses it more selectively.
- As the same archetype, both are naturally drawn to teaching, guiding, and elevating — you recognize and admire that impulse in each other.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body: {{A}}'s lead 1 runs a persistent internal critic that sets high standards and notices what's wrong before what's right. {{B}}'s lead 7 is constitutionally oriented toward reframing, moving forward, and keeping energy positive — which {{A}} can experience as avoidance or intellectual dishonesty. Conversely, {{B}} can find {{A}}'s seriousness and moral weight genuinely deflating, especially when it comes with the 1's characteristic edge of reproach. The 1 in {{A}} controls and contains the 7 impulse; the 7 in {{B}} reframes and softens the 1 impulse — and these two strategies can quietly cancel each other out under stress.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s optimism not as genuine positivity but as a refusal to sit with difficulty — the 7's pain-avoidance looks, to a lead 1, like a principled person cutting corners. {{B}}, in turn, tends to read {{A}}'s corrections and gravity not as care but as criticism — the 1's reforming instinct lands as disapproval rather than investment. Crucially, both believe they are being helpful (the supporting 2 in each reinforces this self-image), so neither person easily sees themselves as the source of friction. The disagreement gets coded as a difference in values when it is really a difference in coping strategies.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should deliberately front-load appreciation before pivoting to critique; the 2 in {{B}} is sensitive to feeling unappreciated, and the 7 lead will disengage fast when it feels cornered by negativity.
- {{B}} should resist the urge to immediately reframe or problem-solve when {{A}} raises something hard — staying present with the concern, even briefly, signals the respect {{A}}'s lead 1 needs.
- Both should name the shared intention explicitly: 'I'm raising this because I care about getting it right' ({{A}}) or 'I want to keep us moving because I believe in what we're doing' ({{B}}) reduces the chance the other person hears attack or avoidance.
- Humor is genuinely available to both, but {{B}} should not use it to deflect and {{A}} should not withhold it as a form of moral seriousness.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} is arguably {{A}}'s most natural mirror for loosening the lead 1's rigidity — seeing the 7 lead in action can remind {{A}} that enthusiasm and flexibility are not ethical failures but necessary parts of full engagement. {{A}} offers {{B}} something harder to find: a model of staying with discomfort, following criticism to its conclusion, and not reframing prematurely. If {{B}} can internalize some of {{A}}'s 1-led accountability and {{A}} can internalize some of {{B}}'s 7-led trust in abundance, both grow into a more complete expression of the Teacher archetype — one that can both name what needs fixing and genuinely believe repair is possible.

359-514.summary: {{A}} leads with the heart center's drive for achievement and image, softened by a detached 5 and a harmony-seeking 9, making them a socially calibrated, goal-oriented presence. {{B}} leads with the head center's thirst for understanding, deepened by a 4's craving for authenticity and sharpened by a 1's moral precision — making them more withdrawn, principled, and emotionally complex. The shared 5 energy creates an intellectual bridge, but {{A}}'s performance-orientation and {{B}}'s suspicion of performance create a genuine fault line that both will need to consciously navigate.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry a 5 in their tritype, giving them a shared language of ideas, analysis, and intellectual depth that can make early conversations feel unusually substantive.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 means they can meet {{B}}'s lead 5 on its own turf — discussing systems, research, and concepts without {{B}} feeling like they have to perform for a less curious audience.
- {{A}}'s supporting 9 and {{B}}'s lead 5 both value low-conflict, low-drama environments, so the baseline temperature of this pairing tends to feel calm and respectful.
- Both are relatively self-contained and don't demand constant reassurance, giving each other functional independence within the relationship.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is wired to optimize presentation and adapt to succeed — {{B}}'s supporting 4 reads this as inauthenticity, and {{B}}'s supporting 1 may frame it as ethically suspect or hollow.
- {{A}} wants momentum, results, and forward movement; {{B}}'s lead 5 needs to fully process before acting, and {{A}} may experience this as foot-dragging or disengagement.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 holds firm ethical standards and can become quietly critical when {{A}}'s 3-lead bends the rules pragmatically in the name of effectiveness.
- {{A}}'s 9 support tends to smooth over friction and declare peace prematurely; {{B}}'s 4 support won't accept surface-level resolution and may simmer in unacknowledged resentment.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} frequently misreads {{B}}'s withdrawal and long silences as rejection or disinterest, when they are simply {{B}}'s lead 5 conserving energy and processing internally — it is not personal.
- {{B}} mistakes {{A}}'s adaptability and image-awareness for shallowness, failing to see that {{A}}'s supporting 5 carries genuine intellectual substance beneath the polished surface.
- {{A}}'s supporting 9 tends to minimize unresolved issues to preserve harmony; {{B}}'s supporting 4 needs those issues named and held — the gap between these two instincts can quietly erode trust over time.
- {{B}} may assume {{A}} knows exactly who they are beneath the achievement-orientation, not realizing that {{A}}'s lead 3 sometimes loses track of authentic feeling too.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should build in deliberate pauses after raising topics — {{B}}'s lead 5 needs processing time before responding, and pushing for immediate reactions will produce defensive withdrawal, not honesty.
- {{B}} should resist the impulse to catalogue {{A}}'s inconsistencies or measure {{A}} against an internal standard of authenticity before the relationship has enough depth; {{A}}'s way of being is real, even if it looks different from {{B}}'s.
- When tension arises, {{A}} should resist the 9-support reflex to smooth it over too quickly — stating the conflict plainly is more respectful to {{B}}'s 4 than pretending it has resolved.
- {{B}} should state needs directly and early rather than waiting to be understood intuitively; {{A}}'s 3-lead is goal-focused and may not naturally read emotional subtext unless it's made explicit.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}} has real capacity to help {{B}} translate accumulated knowledge and insight into visible action and engagement with the world — {{B}}'s lead 5 can spend years understanding something without acting on it, and {{A}}'s 3 energy is a genuine antidote to that paralysis.
- {{B}} offers {{A}} something genuinely rare: a witness who is not impressed by achievement and therefore invites {{A}} to locate value beyond performance — this is uncomfortable for the lead 3 but deeply nourishing if {{A}} can stay with it.
- The risk is a reinforcing loop where {{A}} pushes for results and {{B}} retreats further into observation, each triggering the other's defensive pattern; growth requires {{A}} to slow down voluntarily and {{B}} to stay present rather than disappearing into their inner world.

278-529.summary: {{A}} leads with warm, giving, emotionally expressive energy powered by a 2 core, while {{B}} leads with careful, self-contained intellectual energy powered by a 5 core. The shared 2 in both tritypes creates a genuine thread of mutual care and helpfulness, but the gap between heart-led and head-led orientations produces a classic closeness-versus-distance tension that will define this relationship. At best they balance and enrich each other; at worst they exhaust each other chasing incompatible needs for connection and solitude.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry a 2 in their tritype, meaning genuine warmth and a desire to be useful to people they love are real values for each — this creates immediate felt trust.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 brings curiosity and enthusiasm that activates {{B}}'s lead 5, turning shared ideas into lively intellectual-emotional exchange.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 provides a calm, non-reactive space that {{A}}'s lead 2 finds deeply reassuring — someone steady to give to.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 and {{B}}'s lead 5 both value honesty over social performance, so there is a shared dislike of pretense or manipulation.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- The most structural friction is {{A}}'s lead 2 needing reciprocal emotional closeness versus {{B}}'s lead 5 needing protected space and limited emotional demand — these pulls are genuinely opposing.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 adds confrontational directness that can feel like an assault to {{B}}'s supporting 9, which instinctively retreats from friction and pressure.
- {{B}}'s 5-lead habit of withdrawing to process privately can register to {{A}}'s 2 as rejection or withheld affection, triggering anxious over-giving or, at worse, manipulative nudging.
- {{A}}'s 7 support craves novelty and stimulation; {{B}}'s 5-9 combination prefers depth, repetition, and quiet — socially and energetically they may wear each other out.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s withdrawal as emotional unavailability or indifference, when {{B}}'s lead 5 is simply refueling — privacy is not rejection, it is a survival need.
- {{B}} interprets {{A}}'s emotional expressiveness and persistent giving as a hidden transaction or as pressure to perform closeness, when {{A}}'s lead 2 genuinely means it and is not keeping score in that moment.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 pushes issues to resolution; {{B}}'s supporting 9 stalls and diffuses — {{A}} reads this as passivity or dishonesty, {{B}} reads {{A}}'s push as aggression.
- {{B}}'s 5-lead tendency to speak only when certain can make {{A}} feel unseen or unimportant, while {{A}}'s 7-fueled verbal enthusiasm can make {{B}} feel cognitively overwhelmed and unheard.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should offer {{B}} structured space — announce rather than appear, ask intellectual questions rather than opening with emotional need, and let silence exist without filling it.
- {{B}} should give {{A}}'s lead 2 explicit verbal acknowledgment regularly; a small, clear statement of appreciation lands far more powerfully than {{B}} might expect.
- When conflict arises, {{A}} should soften the 8 directness — bluntness triggers {{B}}'s 9 shutdown; framing issues as problems to solve together activates {{B}}'s lead 5 constructively.
- {{B}} should resist the 5-9 tendency to go vague or evasive under pressure; {{A}}'s 2-8 combination can tolerate directness far better than {{B}} assumes and is far more hurt by ambiguity.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 5 is pulled toward growth at type 8, meaning leaning into {{A}}'s assertive, embodied energy can actually model healthy directness and engagement for {{B}}.
- {{A}}'s lead 2 is pulled toward growth at type 4, and {{B}}'s quiet interiority and comfort with aloneness can teach {{A}} to sit with their own needs rather than outsourcing them through giving.
- The risk is codependency masked as complementarity — {{A}} over-functions emotionally while {{B}} under-functions, reinforcing both types' avoidances rather than challenging them.
- The real growth opportunity is mutual: {{A}} learning that love doesn't require constant contact, and {{B}} learning that being known by another person is not depletion but nourishment.

417-835.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a high-voltage pairing of emotional depth and raw power — {{A}}'s lead 4 brings intense self-awareness, creative vision, and a hunger for authentic feeling, while {{B}}'s lead 8 drives forward with force, decisiveness, and a need for control. They can ignite each other in compelling ways, but the gap between heart-led introspection and gut-led action creates real friction that requires consistent, deliberate navigation. This relationship has genuine potential, but neither type is naturally inclined toward the kind of compromise it demands.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both {{A}} and {{B}} carry a strong sense of individual vision — {{A}}'s 4 and 7 together generate inspired, future-facing ideas, while {{B}}'s 8 and 5 give those ideas strategic teeth and real-world force.
- Neither is interested in being ordinary; {{A}}'s 4 resists conformity for the sake of authentic identity, and {{B}}'s 8 rejects being controlled or defined by others' terms.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 brings an intellectual depth that {{A}}'s 4 genuinely respects — this is one of the few dynamics that makes {{B}} feel like a worthy sparring partner for {{A}}'s inner world.
- When energy is high, {{A}}'s 7 enthusiasm and {{B}}'s 8 boldness can be mutually galvanizing — both love going big.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 4 needs emotional attunement and to feel deeply seen; {{B}}'s lead 8 often reads vulnerability as inefficiency and will unconsciously bulldoze past it.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 holds firm moral and aesthetic standards, which can come across as criticizing or moralizing — {{B}}'s 8 has a particularly low tolerance for being corrected or held to someone else's code.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 is pragmatic, image-aware, and results-focused, which {{A}}'s 4 may experience as shallow or performative — a direct affront to {{A}}'s core value of authenticity.
- When {{A}}'s 4 slides into melancholy and inward processing, {{B}}'s 8 becomes visibly impatient, which only deepens {{A}}'s sense of not being understood.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to interpret {{B}}'s bluntness and push-through energy as emotional indifference or even cruelty, when for {{B}}'s 8, directness is actually a form of respect — softening feels dishonest.
- {{B}} frequently misreads {{A}}'s emotional processing — particularly the 4's tendency to sit in difficult feelings — as self-indulgence, manipulation, or a lack of resolve.
- {{A}}'s 1 inner critic often surfaces as a principled objection or correction; {{B}}'s 8 hears this not as care but as a power move, and responds with escalation.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 can disengage emotionally when {{A}}'s 4 most needs connection, and {{A}} will read that detachment as rejection rather than {{B}}'s mode of processing.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should resist the instinct to immediately problem-solve or override when {{A}} is processing emotionally — acknowledging the feeling first, even briefly, dramatically reduces defensiveness in {{A}}'s 4.
- {{A}} will be better heard by {{B}} when leading with ideas and concrete stakes (engaging {{B}}'s 5) rather than opening with emotional needs, which tend to activate {{B}}'s 8 impatience.
- {{A}}'s 1 and {{B}}'s 3 can actually find shared ground around quality and standards if framed as collaboration rather than criticism — "here's what could be better" lands differently than "here's what's wrong."
- {{B}} should name intent explicitly — {{A}}'s 4 will fill silence or bluntness with the worst interpretation, so clarity about motivation prevents a lot of unnecessary rupture.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s 8 offers {{A}} something genuinely valuable: the push from self-referential feeling into outward impact — {{A}}'s 4 and 1 can get locked in internal idealism, and {{B}}'s action-orientation breaks that loop.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally rare: the courage to go inward. {{B}}'s 8 defends hard against vulnerability, and {{A}}'s 4 — by modeling depth and emotional honesty — can slowly open that door if {{B}} feels safe rather than judged.
- The growth edge for this pairing is asymmetrical: {{B}} must be willing to slow down and tolerate ambiguity, while {{A}} must be willing to act before every feeling is fully resolved.
- If both resist growth, the pattern calcifies quickly — {{B}} becomes domineering and dismissive, {{A}} becomes withdrawn and resentful; the health of this relationship is almost entirely a function of whether both parties are actively working on themselves.

458-478.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a rare mirroring quality — both lead with the 4's hunger for depth, authenticity, and emotional significance, and both carry the 8's gut-level intensity as a supporting force. The critical divergence is in the head center: {{A}}'s supporting 5 pulls inward toward analysis and withdrawal, while {{B}}'s supporting 7 pulls outward toward stimulation and possibility. This creates a pairing of profound mutual recognition shadowed by a persistent tension between contraction and expansion.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body: The double-4 lead is the engine of this connection — both {{A}} and {{B}} crave realness over performance, depth over small talk, and meaning over convenience. They will find each other refreshingly unafraid of intensity, willing to go to emotional places that most people avoid. The shared 8 support means neither person tends to flinch when things get confrontational or raw; both can speak hard truths and expect the other to handle it. This pairing can produce conversations and creative collaborations of unusual richness, because both instinctively reach past surface appearances toward what actually matters.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body: Two 4 leads in close relationship are also two people competing, often silently, for the role of 'the one who feels most deeply' — and that competition can breed resentment or one-upmanship disguised as authenticity. {{A}}'s supporting 5 creates a natural rhythm of withdrawal: needing space to process, holding back information, retreating into internal observation when overwhelmed. {{B}}'s supporting 7 does the opposite, seeking stimulation and forward motion, sometimes reframing painful emotions into exciting new projects. {{A}} will experience {{B}}'s 7 energy as emotional avoidance or restless shallowness; {{B}} will experience {{A}}'s 5 withdrawal as coldness, withholding, or passive punishment.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to interpret {{B}}'s enthusiasm and future-focus as evidence that {{B}} isn't willing to truly sit with pain — a 4's cardinal sin. What {{A}} misses is that {{B}}'s 7 is a genuine cognitive style, not just a defense mechanism; {{B}} really does process meaning through possibility and movement, not only through stillness. Conversely, {{B}} often reads {{A}}'s 5-supported retreats as rejection or emotional withholding, when {{A}} is simply recharging or thinking — not pulling away relationally. The shared 8 adds another layer of misreading: both can deploy bluntness and force, but {{A}} uses that directness to protect inner depth, while {{B}} uses it to assert a vision, and neither always clocks the difference.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- Name the double-4 dynamic out loud: agree early that both of you need to feel uniquely seen, and that competing for 'most authentic' will poison the well.
- {{B}} should resist the 7 impulse to reframe or reinterpret {{A}}'s grief or darkness into something more manageable — sit in it first before pivoting to possibility.
- {{A}} should give {{B}} explicit, verbal reassurance when withdrawing into 5 mode, so {{B}} doesn't fill the silence with anxious 7 activity or 4-flavored catastrophizing.
- When 8 energy escalates conflict, both should recognize that the heat is a shared dialect — but slow down enough to clarify whether the confrontation is productive or is being used to avoid the actual emotional wound.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} offers {{A}} a genuine gift: the 7 support models that meaning can be found in forward motion, not only in excavating what has been lost, and {{B}}'s energy can pull {{A}} out of the 5's isolating echo chamber. {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally rare: the 5's depth and patience creates a container where {{B}}'s 4 lead can actually land and be known, rather than always moving before the feeling fully registers. Both grow most when they stop treating the other's head-center style as a deficiency — {{A}}'s 5 is not avoidance of life, and {{B}}'s 7 is not avoidance of pain — and start borrowing from each other deliberately. The shared 8 gut support means this pair has the courage to do that difficult work if they choose it.

259-738.summary: {{A}} is a heart-led giver whose warmth is quietly buffered by intellectual depth (5) and conflict-avoidance (9), while {{B}} is a head-led energizer whose enthusiasm is turbocharged by ambition (3) and assertive force (8). At their best, this pairing creates a dynamic where {{A}} provides thoughtful, behind-the-scenes support and {{B}} provides exciting momentum and bold vision. But the gap between {{A}}'s indirect emotional style and {{B}}'s high-velocity, boundary-pushing energy can quietly erode trust if left unaddressed.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 genuinely wants to support people they care about, and {{B}}'s lead 7 thrives when they feel enthusiastically backed — this creates an early sense of natural fit.
- The supporting 5 in {{A}} matches {{B}}'s 7-led love of ideas and intellectual range, giving them real conversational chemistry.
- {{A}}'s supporting 9 has the patience and adaptability to ride out {{B}}'s high energy and frequent pivots without immediately shutting down.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 appreciates competence, and {{A}}'s quiet, thorough problem-solving earns genuine respect from that part of {{B}}.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 needs to feel genuinely seen and appreciated; {{B}}'s lead 7 is naturally self-referential and future-focused, which can leave {{A}} feeling invisible despite doing significant emotional labor.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 is blunt and confrontational, which directly collides with {{A}}'s supporting 9 — {{A}} will withdraw rather than engage, and {{B}} may interpret that silence as resolution.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 wants depth, preparation, and careful deliberation; {{B}}'s 7 moves fast and gets bored, creating tension whenever a topic or project requires sustained focus.
- Over time, {{A}}'s 2 may quietly accumulate resentment from unacknowledged giving while {{B}}'s 7+8 combination barrels forward, unaware anything is wrong.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}}'s 2+9 combination produces a deeply indirect communicator — needs are hinted at, not stated, and harmony is maintained on the surface even when something is wrong. {{B}}'s lead 7 and supporting 8 are wired for directness and action, so they genuinely do not register the hints and assume the peace is real. From {{B}}'s side, {{A}} may read as passive or even passive-aggressive when they finally pull back, because the buildup happened in silence. From {{A}}'s side, {{B}} can seem emotionally careless or self-absorbed when in reality {{B}} simply operates in explicit, stated terms and never saw the unspoken signals.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} must learn to use the clarity their supporting 5 is capable of — stating needs in direct, low-drama terms will land far better with {{B}}'s 7+8 than emotional hinting will.
- {{B}} should build in deliberate check-ins and resist the 7 impulse to reframe or fast-forward past {{A}}'s concerns with optimism; {{A}}'s 9 will take that as dismissal.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 should be held in check during disagreements — leading with force will cause {{A}}'s 9 to shut down entirely, ending the conversation without resolution.
- {{A}} can frame concerns analytically (leveraging the 5) rather than relationally, since {{B}}'s head-center lead is more receptive to logical framing than emotional appeals.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} offers {{A}} something genuinely needed: a model of unapologetic desire and bold self-assertion. The lead 7's confidence in wanting things and the 8's willingness to take up space can push {{A}}'s 2 toward the healthier individuation that type 2 needs — learning to have and voice their own needs rather than only serving others'. In return, {{A}}'s 2+5+9 combination offers {{B}} depth, steadiness, and a relational anchor that the scattered 7+3+8 combination often lacks. {{A}} can slow {{B}} down enough to integrate rather than escape, and {{B}} can pull {{A}} out of self-erasure. The relationship has genuine growth potential, but only if {{A}} builds the courage to speak up and {{B}} builds the discipline to listen.

278-378.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share an almost identical structural blueprint — the same head (7) and gut (8) supports — but diverge sharply at the lead, where {{A}} anchors in relational warmth and {{B}} anchors in goal-driven image management. This makes the pairing feel instantly familiar and high-energy, while also creating a subtle but persistent competition for emotional centrality. The shared 7 and 8 give them tremendous momentum together; the 2-vs-3 lead split is where the real relational work lives.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared supporting 7 makes both {{A}} and {{B}} genuinely fun, spontaneous, and future-oriented — they energize each other and rarely run out of things to pursue together.
- The shared supporting 8 gives both a boldness and directness that creates real trust; neither has to dance around hard conversations indefinitely.
- Both are heart-center leads, so emotional attunement and a desire to be seen are wired into each of them — they instinctively understand that relationships matter.
- High energy, high ambition, and a shared enjoyment of being 'in the room where it happens' makes this pairing feel alive and socially magnetic.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 measures love through giving and being needed; {{B}}'s lead 3 measures worth through achievement and admiration — these are different currencies, and each can feel like the other is 'not getting it.'
- {{B}} can steamroll emotional moments in favor of forward momentum, which {{A}}'s 2 experiences as abandonment or dismissiveness.
- {{A}} may unconsciously withhold support or use giving as leverage when feeling unappreciated — a 2 pattern that {{B}}'s efficiency-minded 3 finds baffling and manipulative.
- Both the 2 and 3 have image concerns (3 explicitly, 2 around being seen as 'good'), which can turn disagreements into ego contests rather than genuine problem-solving.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s task-focus and polished self-presentation as shallowness or emotional unavailability, when {{B}} is actually expressing care through doing and achieving — including for {{A}}.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s emotional bids and need for acknowledgment as neediness or subtle manipulation, missing that {{A}}'s 2 lead is genuinely wired for relational reciprocity as a survival strategy.
- Because they share so much (7 enthusiasm, 8 assertiveness), both can assume they are more aligned than they are — then feel blindsided when the 2-vs-3 core fear gap surfaces under stress.
- {{A}} may not realize how much {{B}} needs genuine admiration for accomplishments, not just warmth; {{B}} may not realize how much {{A}} needs to feel indispensable, not just liked.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should pause after a win and explicitly name {{A}}'s contribution — not as a tactic, but as genuine recognition; {{A}}'s lead 2 runs on acknowledgment and will give far more freely when it feels received.
- {{A}} should practice stating needs directly rather than through increased giving or withdrawal — the shared 8 support in both of them means directness is available and respected in this pairing.
- When conflict arises, both should name the underlying fear: {{A}} can say 'I'm feeling unimportant here' and {{B}} can say 'I'm feeling like I'm failing here' — stripping the defense layers speeds resolution significantly.
- Avoid letting the shared 7 use optimism and activity to paper over unresolved emotional tension; both are capable of distracting themselves out of necessary conversations.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}} challenges {{B}} to slow down and ask whether the achievement is serving real connection or just ego — the 2's relational attunement is a mirror {{B}}'s 3 genuinely needs.
- {{B}} challenges {{A}} to develop self-worth that isn't contingent on being needed — modeling that a person can be valued for what they do and become, not just for what they give.
- The shared 8 support means both have access to accountability and directness; when both lean into it honestly rather than defensively, the growth conversations become genuinely productive.
- Long-term, this pairing can produce remarkable external impact and deep mutual loyalty — provided both learn to need each other without needing to control how that need is expressed.

359-614.summary: {{A}} leads with an achievement-driven, image-conscious 3 softened by analytical detachment (5) and conflict-avoidant harmony (9), while {{B}} leads with a security-seeking, vigilant 6 deepened by emotional intensity (4) and principled judgment (1). These two can build a relationship of genuine intellectual and practical partnership, but they must navigate a core tension: {{A}}'s polished, performance-oriented exterior naturally triggers {{B}}'s skepticism, and {{B}}'s anxious questioning can feel like an obstacle to {{A}}'s forward momentum. The relationship has real depth potential if both are willing to move past their respective defenses.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 and {{B}}'s lead 6 share a head-center orientation — both are information-gatherers who want to understand how things work before committing, and this creates a genuine intellectual meeting ground.
- {{A}}'s supporting 9 brings a steady, non-threatening calm that can genuinely soothe {{B}}'s lead 6 anxiety; the 9's accommodating quality signals safety to an otherwise watchful 6.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 respects standards and doing things well, which resonates with {{A}}'s lead 3's drive for competence and results — both respect people who follow through.
- When goals align, this pairing can be quietly formidable: {{A}} supplies strategic drive and execution, {{B}} supplies thoroughness, loyalty, and ethical grounding.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is image-managed by nature — presenting a polished, competent front is instinctive, not cynical. But {{B}}'s lead 6 is wired to detect inauthenticity and inconsistency, and that smooth 3 surface reads as suspicious or evasive, fueling mistrust.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 craves emotional depth, uniqueness, and being truly seen; {{A}}'s lead 3 tends to sidestep emotional mess in favor of efficiency, which can leave {{B}} feeling emotionally dismissed or generic.
- {{B}}'s lead 6 can cycle through anxiety, doubt, and worst-case scenarios — {{A}}'s lead 3, optimized for momentum, finds this draining and may withdraw or subtly minimize {{B}}'s concerns rather than sitting with them.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 will surface criticism when values are violated; {{A}}'s lead 3 doesn't handle criticism well when it threatens their self-image, and may deflect or shut down rather than engage.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} reads {{B}}'s skepticism and questioning as a vote of no-confidence or unnecessary friction — "why can't you just trust the plan?" — when {{B}} is actually doing due diligence that comes from loyalty, not opposition.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s confident, forward-looking persona as proof of something being hidden; the 3's natural compartmentalization of emotion looks like deception to a vigilant 6, even when {{A}} is being straightforward.
- {{A}}'s supporting 9 means conflict avoidance is baked in — {{A}} may hedge or go vague when under pressure. {{B}}'s lead 6 interprets that vagueness as stonewalling or a red flag, rather than recognizing it as the 9's discomfort with confrontation.
- {{B}}'s 4 support makes {{B}} feel that their inner emotional world is significant and worth exploring; {{A}}'s 3-led pragmatism can unintentionally signal that this is self-indulgent, creating a wound {{B}} may not name directly.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should make a practice of showing the seams — admitting uncertainty, naming a real feeling, or acknowledging a mistake in real time. For {{B}}'s lead 6, this transparency is the foundation of trust far more than any polished result.
- {{B}} should frame concern as "I need to understand this" rather than "I don't trust this" — {{A}}'s lead 3 can receive curious questions, but perceives interrogation as an attack and will retreat behind performance.
- Both benefit from slowing down to name what center they're operating from: {{A}} should check whether their 9 is suppressing a real concern; {{B}} should check whether their 6 anxiety is projecting a threat that isn't actually there.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 and {{B}}'s lead 6 can make intellectual discussion a genuine bonding space — choose substantive topics to explore together, as this is where both feel naturally competent and safe.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 6 offers {{A}} something genuinely valuable: a loyal, principled skeptic who won't simply validate the image. If {{A}} can tolerate it, {{B}}'s questioning can push {{A}} toward a more authentic, less performance-driven version of success.
- {{A}}'s lead 3 models decisive action and forward movement, which can interrupt the paralysis that {{B}}'s 6 anxiety sometimes creates — {{B}} grows by learning that acting without complete certainty can be safe.
- {{A}}'s supporting 9 and {{B}}'s supporting 4 both carry an underdeveloped emotional honesty — 9 by merging and smoothing, 4 by dramatizing but sometimes not grounding. Together they can practice a more direct, steady form of emotional communication.
- Long-term, {{A}} grows toward the genuine self behind the image (3's integration toward 6, ironically toward {{B}}'s home type), and {{B}} grows toward trusting their own judgment without constant external verification — each can model for the other what the other is reaching toward.

549-925.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a quiet, contemplative wavelength — both carry 5 and 9 energy and neither craves the spotlight or constant stimulation. However, {{A}} leads from the head with a 5's drive for autonomous understanding and a 4's need for felt uniqueness, while {{B}} leads from the gut with a 9's self-forgetting accommodation and a 2's relational warmth. This creates a pairing of genuine intellectual kinship and peaceful coexistence, underlaid by real tensions around emotional visibility, reciprocity, and the risk of mutual drift into comfortable stagnation.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the 5 archetype — {{A}} as lead, {{B}} as a supporting type — giving them a shared love of ideas, depth, and unhurried conversation.
- The shared 9 energy means neither is loud, combative, or needy for constant stimulation; they can exist comfortably in the same quiet space.
- {{B}}'s 9 lead creates an accepting, non-judgmental presence that {{A}}'s 5 lead genuinely relaxes into, rare for a type that usually guards its inner world fiercely.
- When engaged intellectually, {{A}}'s 5-and-4 depth and {{B}}'s 5-supported curiosity can produce long, rich exchanges that feel mutually nourishing.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 carries a strong need to be seen as genuinely unique and emotionally distinct; {{B}}'s 9 lead tends to merge, smooth over differences, and equalize — which can inadvertently flatten exactly what {{A}}'s 4 most needs acknowledged.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 gives warmth and help with an implicit expectation of emotional reciprocity; {{A}}'s 5 lead is often unaware this relational transaction is even occurring, and may seem indifferent or ungrateful.
- Both types retreat under stress — {{A}}'s 5 withdraws into mental isolation, {{B}}'s 9 dissociates into inertia — meaning conflict or unresolved tension can simply evaporate unaddressed, building invisible resentment over time.
- {{A}}'s 4 support can generate emotional intensity or melancholy that {{B}}'s 9 lead finds destabilizing and quietly avoids, leaving {{A}} feeling unseen at precisely the moments they need contact.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} often reads {{B}}'s 9-led agreeableness as absence of real opinion or depth, and may lose respect for or interest in {{B}} without realizing the 9's rich inner life simply doesn't self-promote.
- {{B}} tends to interpret {{A}}'s 5-lead withdrawal as rejection or emotional coldness, when it is almost always about energy management and private processing, not relational distance.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 assumes that giving and caring will be noticed and returned naturally; {{A}}'s 5 lead does not operate on that intuitive emotional accounting system and genuinely may not realize a debt has accumulated.
- {{A}}'s 4 support longs to be met in emotional specificity — to have their inner world named and affirmed — but {{B}}'s 9 lead speaks in generalities and harmony, which reads to {{A}}'s 4 as emotional superficiality rather than the love it actually is.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should signal explicitly when withdrawing — a simple acknowledgment that space is needed and connection will return prevents {{B}}'s 9 from silently absorbing the distance as rejection.
- {{B}} needs to practice forming and voicing actual opinions rather than defaulting to mirroring {{A}}; {{A}}'s 5 lead is drawn to intellectual friction and loses interest when there is none.
- Both should resist the powerful mutual pull to let discomfort dissolve into comfortable avoidance — naming a tension briefly and directly serves this pairing far better than their shared instinct to let it pass.
- {{A}} can build meaningful goodwill with {{B}}'s supporting 2 by verbalizing appreciation explicitly and specifically, even when it feels unnecessary; for {{B}}, this is not optional — it is relational oxygen.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}}'s 9-led warmth and {{B}}'s supporting 2 can draw {{A}} out of the hermetic detachment the 5 lead defaults to, modeling that connection does not have to cost self-knowledge — this is genuinely healing for {{A}}. In return, {{A}}'s 5 lead and supporting 4 can help {{B}} develop a more individuated sense of self, encouraging {{B}} to distinguish their own perspective from the ambient preferences of the room — work the 9 lead deeply needs. The central growth challenge for this pairing is shared: both must choose engagement over retreat, because their combined 5-and-9 energy makes comfortable, intellectually rich withdrawal together very easy and ultimately hollow. At their best, they build one of the quieter but more genuinely intimate pairings — a relationship grounded in mutual respect, slow trust, and rare depth.

146-459.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share the 4's deep hunger for authenticity and meaning, which gives them an immediate sense of recognition — both are serious, introspective, and allergic to superficiality. But {{A}} leads from the gut with the 1's reforming moral energy, while {{B}} leads from the heart with the 4's identity-driven emotional depth, and these two orientations create persistent friction around criticism, emotional pacing, and what 'doing things right' even means. This pairing has real potential for profound connection, but it requires both to actively work against their respective rigidities.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both are drawn to depth, meaning, and authenticity — the shared 4 energy makes small talk feel like a waste to both of them.
- {{A}}'s 6 support brings loyalty and a need to be genuinely known, which resonates with {{B}}'s core longing to be seen and understood.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 and {{A}}'s supporting 6 both fuel a love of ideas, careful thinking, and not accepting easy answers.
- Conversations between these two can go very deep very fast — they share a philosophical seriousness that makes this pairing feel substantive.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 is wired to notice flaws and correct them; {{B}}'s lead 4 takes criticism as a referendum on their worth and identity — this is a fundamental collision.
- {{B}}'s 4-led emotional expressiveness can feel self-referential or melodramatic to {{A}}'s 1, which prizes self-discipline and keeping emotions in service of principle.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 brings anxiety and a need for reliability; {{B}}'s supporting 9 can be emotionally avoidant and slow to commit, which reads to {{A}} as untrustworthy.
- {{B}} may experience {{A}}'s standards as suffocating, while {{A}} may experience {{B}}'s emotional intensity as chaotic or indulgent.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s emotional withdrawal (9 support) or inward focus (4 lead) as passive resistance or avoidance of accountability, when {{B}} is actually processing internally and needs space before engaging. Meanwhile, {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s corrections or moral framing (lead 1) as rejection or judgment of who they are, when {{A}} is genuinely trying to improve the situation, not attack {{B}}'s identity. {{A}}'s 6 loyalty signals care through consistency and reliability, which {{B}}'s 4 may not register as affection; {{B}} signals care through emotional attunement and being truly 'met,' which {{A}}'s 1 may experience as demanding or impractical.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should separate behavioral feedback from personal critique — with {{B}}'s lead 4, the delivery matters as much as the content, and leading with appreciation before correction is not optional.
- {{B}} should name their emotional state explicitly rather than expecting {{A}} to intuit it — {{A}}'s 1 is attuned to problems to solve, not feelings to absorb.
- {{A}}'s 6 support appreciates direct reassurance of loyalty; {{B}} can offer this without it feeling performative.
- {{B}}'s 9 support can conflict-avoid in ways that build quiet resentment — naming discomfort early, while it's small, will prevent blow-ups that {{A}}'s 1 will find destabilizing.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} offers {{A}} something the lead 1 deeply needs: permission to feel, to be imperfect, and to access the 4's emotional richness without needing it to be 'correct.' {{A}}'s supporting 4 is present but subordinated to the 1's inner critic, and {{B}}'s modeling of unashamed emotional depth can help {{A}} integrate that part of themselves. In turn, {{A}} offers {{B}} something the lead 4 often lacks — a principled external orientation and the 1's capacity to act on values rather than dwell in feeling. At their best, {{A}} grounds {{B}}'s depth into purposeful action, and {{B}} teaches {{A}} that authenticity sometimes means sitting with what is, not rushing to fix it.

316-469.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both heart-center leads sharing a 6 supporting type, which creates a foundation of loyalty and emotional investment — but the 3 and 4 lead types pull in fundamentally opposite directions around authenticity versus achievement. {{A}} is wired to perform, optimize, and correct, while {{B}} is wired to feel deeply, differentiate, and preserve inner truth. This pairing has real potential for mutual depth, but it requires deliberate effort to bridge the gap between {{A}}'s results-orientation and {{B}}'s identity-driven emotional world.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry a 6 supporting type in the head center, meaning loyalty, reliability, and commitment to those they trust are non-negotiable values for both {{A}} and {{B}} — this shared instinct can build genuine long-term trust.
- The heart-center dominance in both means neither person dismisses emotional connection; this pairing takes relationships seriously and invests meaningfully.
- {{A}}'s 1 brings integrity and high standards that {{B}}'s 4 can deeply respect, since authenticity and moral seriousness matter to the 4.
- {{B}}'s 9 softens the relational space and creates a non-threatening atmosphere that gives {{A}}'s harder-edged 3+1 combination room to relax and be less performative.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- The 3 and 4 are adjacent heart types with a fundamental conflict: {{A}}'s lead 3 manages emotion by packaging and suppressing it in service of goals, while {{B}}'s lead 4 amplifies and dwells in emotion as the primary source of identity — this creates chronic misalignment in emotional tempo.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 adds a corrective, evaluative edge that is genuinely difficult for {{B}}'s lead 4, which is acutely sensitive to feeling judged, unseen, or reduced to a standard.
- {{B}}'s 9 tends to withdraw from pressure and delay action, which frustrates {{A}}'s 3+1 drive toward efficiency and correctness — {{A}} may read this as passivity or avoidance.
- {{A}} optimizes for external results and reputation; {{B}} optimizes for inner truth and uniqueness — these can feel like competing value systems rather than complementary ones.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to interpret {{B}}'s emotional depth and periodic withdrawal as self-indulgence or inefficiency, missing that for the lead 4, processing feeling is not a detour but the actual point.
- {{B}} is likely to read {{A}}'s image-consciousness and task-focus as emotional unavailability or superficiality, not recognizing that the lead 3 does care deeply — it just expresses care through doing, not dwelling.
- Both carry a 6, but {{A}}'s 6 seeks security through structure, competence, and proving reliability, while {{B}}'s 6 seeks security through emotional attunement and reassurance of belonging — they can feel equally anxious for very different reasons without realizing they share the same underlying need.
- {{B}}'s 9 may suppress dissatisfaction and hope {{A}} intuits it, while {{A}}'s 3 is tracking outcomes, not subtext — this creates a slow buildup of resentment that neither sees coming.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the 3's impulse to move past emotional content toward solutions; explicitly naming that feelings matter here — not just results — opens {{B}} up significantly.
- {{B}} should leverage the directness of the lead 4 rather than retreating into 9-style conflict avoidance; {{A}}'s 3+1 combination responds well to clear, honest statements and poorly to vague withdrawal.
- When tension arises, both can anchor to their shared 6 instinct — framing a difficult conversation in terms of loyalty, fairness, and shared commitment creates a language both genuinely understand.
- {{A}} should be especially mindful of the 1's critical voice in moments of stress; even well-intentioned correction lands as rejection for {{B}}'s lead 4, so timing and framing matter enormously.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: Type 3 grows toward 6 — toward deeper loyalty, humility, and genuine community — and type 4 grows toward 1 — toward principled action, groundedness, and moving out of emotional rumination. This means {{A}} already carries in their supporting 1 exactly what {{B}} needs to grow toward, and {{B}} already carries in their supporting 6 exactly what {{A}} needs to grow toward — making this a pairing with unusual mirroring potential if both are self-aware. {{B}} can invite {{A}} into emotional authenticity beneath the performance, modeling that identity doesn't have to be earned. {{A}} can model for {{B}} that action and external engagement are not betrayals of inner depth but expressions of it. The risk is that without growth orientation, each reinforces the other's defensive pattern — {{A}} staying shallow and driven, {{B}} staying withdrawn and self-referential.

478-836.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a high-intensity pairing that can generate remarkable creative and relational depth, but their centers of gravity pull in opposite directions — {{A}} leads from the heart, craving authentic emotional truth, while {{B}} leads from the gut, driven by power, protection, and forward motion. The shared 8 energy running through both tritypes gives this pair a rare capacity for honest, direct engagement without either person collapsing under pressure. The real challenge is that {{A}}'s 4-led need to be emotionally known can clash hard with {{B}}'s 8-led tendency to override feelings in favor of action and results.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry 8 energy — {{A}} as a supporting gut type and {{B}} as the dominant lead — meaning neither person flinches from confrontation or raw honesty, which builds genuine mutual respect.
- {{A}}'s 4 brings emotional intensity and depth that {{B}}'s 8 often quietly hungers for beneath its armored exterior; {{B}} can feel truly met rather than handled.
- {{B}}'s directness and protectiveness land as genuine strength for {{A}}, whose supporting 8 recognizes and values that force without being intimidated by it.
- Both resist phoniness in different ways: {{A}}'s 4 rejects inauthenticity on principle, while {{B}}'s 8 has little patience for games, so they tend to cut through social performance with each other quickly.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 4 needs to sit with emotional complexity, grief, and longing — sometimes for extended periods — while {{B}}'s lead 8 instinctively pushes to resolve tension and move forward, making {{A}} feel steamrolled or emotionally dismissed.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 adds an achievement and image layer that can read as shallow or performance-driven to {{A}}'s authenticity-obsessed 4, creating quiet contempt on {{A}}'s side.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 copes with pain through reframing and optimism; {{B}}'s 8 sees avoidance as weakness, and this mismatch in how each processes difficulty can cause real friction.
- {{B}}'s supporting 6 generates loyalty but also suspicion and anxiety about betrayal — {{A}}'s 4-driven individualism and emotional variability can inadvertently trigger {{B}}'s threat radar.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} reads {{B}}'s bluntness and forward charge as emotional unavailability or domination, when {{B}} is often simply operating in the language of action rather than withholding care.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s emotional depth and periodic withdrawal as manipulation or weakness, when {{A}} is processing internally in the way their 4 lead requires — not performing or punishing.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 can pivot to lightness or reframing mid-conflict, which {{B}}'s 8 interprets as not taking things seriously; in reality {{A}} is managing their own emotional flooding.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 can shift into efficiency mode during emotional conversations, optimizing for resolution rather than understanding — leaving {{A}}'s 4 feeling like an obstacle to be managed rather than a person to be known.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should lead with a clear, direct ask before unpacking emotional nuance — {{B}}'s 8 responds to clarity of need and loses the thread when submerged in feeling first.
- {{B}} should explicitly slow down and signal presence before offering solutions; the words "I'm listening, tell me more" activate {{A}}'s 4 in ways that action-oriented responses never will.
- When conflict escalates, {{A}}'s supporting 8 gives them the backbone to hold their ground — {{B}} should take this seriously rather than treating it as an obstacle, because {{A}} is not bluffing.
- {{B}}'s 6 loyalty means commitment is real once established; {{A}} should name and affirm that loyalty directly, as the 4's tendency to focus on what's missing can make {{B}} feel perpetually under-appreciated.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} can pull {{A}} out of emotional rumination and self-referential loops by modeling that action and self-expression in the world are equally valid forms of authenticity — not betrayals of the inner life.
- {{A}} can teach {{B}} that vulnerability is not weakness and that accessing the emotional register beneath the 8's armor — and even beneath the 3's achievement drive — is where real intimacy and influence live.
- {{A}}'s 4-led honesty about complexity can directly challenge {{B}}'s 8 tendency to flatten nuance into dominance or loyalty tests, helping {{B}}'s supporting 6 find security through genuine understanding rather than control.
- This pairing has real potential to forge something lasting precisely because neither person is easily softened into false comfort — growth here is earned, direct, and unusually honest.

513-612.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both head-center leads who share a deep orientation toward precision, reliability, and doing things right — anchored further by a shared supporting 1. The pairing has genuine intellectual kinship and a mutual respect for competence, but the 5-led withdrawal pattern and the 6-led need for reassurance and alliance create a persistent tension around availability and trust. This is a relationship with real compatibility potential, but it requires both people to consciously work against their default defenses.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both {{A}} and {{B}} lead from the head center, meaning they share a natural preference for thinking things through carefully before acting — conversations tend to be substantive and mutually stimulating.
- The shared supporting 1 gives both a strong ethical backbone; they will likely align on standards of quality, fairness, and responsibility, making them reliable partners in any collaborative work.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 drives competence and results, which {{B}}'s 6 genuinely respects and finds reassuring — a capable, consistent partner is exactly what a 6 is looking for.
- {{B}}'s 6-led loyalty is something {{A}}'s 5 quietly values; once {{A}} grants trust (which takes time), {{B}}'s steadfast presence is one of the few things that can draw a 5 out of isolation.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 5 needs significant alone time and emotional distance to feel safe; {{B}}'s lead 6 interprets withdrawal as a signal of unreliability or hidden disapproval, which triggers anxiety and increased bid for connection — exactly the dynamic that pushes {{A}} further away.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 creates a giving, relationship-tending energy that can feel like an implicit expectation of reciprocity; {{A}}'s 5 doesn't naturally track relational debts and may seem indifferent or ungrateful.
- Both share the supporting 1, which can manifest as mutual criticism — each has strong ideas about the 'right way' and neither backs down easily from a position grounded in principle.
- Under stress, {{A}} retreats into the mind and becomes more withholding (5 going to 7 in avoidance, or contracting inward), while {{B}} becomes more reactive and tests loyalty (6 going to 3 or cycling into doubt) — their stress responses are nearly incompatible in real time.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s questioning and need for verbal reassurance as intellectual insecurity or excessive emotionality, when in fact {{B}} is scanning for trustworthiness — something {{A}} values just as much but expresses through consistent, quiet behavior rather than words. Conversely, {{B}} reads {{A}}'s detachment and sparse communication as secrecy, superiority, or lack of care, when {{A}} simply treats privacy as a default rather than a statement about the relationship. {{A}}'s supporting 3 can also create a performance layer — projecting competence and confidence — that {{B}}'s 6 finds hard to read as authentic, fueling further suspicion. {{B}} may not realize that {{A}} expressing an opinion or sharing a system is actually a form of intimacy for a 5-led type.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should offer brief, explicit signals of trust and commitment — not because {{B}} is needy, but because {{B}}'s 6 lead genuinely needs verbal anchoring that {{A}}'s 5 lead considers redundant.
- {{B}} should resist the urge to over-question or seek confirmation during {{A}}'s quiet phases; framing check-ins as curiosity rather than surveillance will keep {{A}} from retreating further.
- Both should use their shared supporting 1 as common ground — starting disagreements from shared values ('we both care about getting this right') reduces the chance that {{B}} personalizes {{A}}'s corrections or {{A}} dismisses {{B}}'s concerns.
- {{A}} benefits from naming a boundary explicitly ('I need a few hours, then I'm back') rather than silently disappearing, which is the single highest-impact habit change for this pairing.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} offers {{A}} something a lead 5 rarely receives organically: sustained, loyal presence that doesn't demand performance in return — if {{A}} can tolerate the relational closeness, {{B}}'s 6 energy can gently draw the 5 out of over-detachment and toward genuine connection. {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally rare: a steady, non-reactive thinking partner who won't be swept into {{B}}'s anxiety spirals, modeling the grounded discernment that a 6 is always trying to cultivate. The shared 1 gives both a growth edge around self-compassion — they can either reinforce each other's inner critic or, at their best, hold each other to high standards while also extending grace. This relationship tends to deepen slowly; early friction around availability and trust is not a sign of incompatibility so much as the natural cost of entry for two types who are both, in different ways, slow to fully open.

147-513.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both driven by a deep need to get things right — {{A}} through principled moral reform (lead 1) colored by emotional intensity (supporting 4) and expansive idealism (supporting 7), and {{B}} through rigorous intellectual mastery (lead 5) backed by achievement-focus (supporting 3) and exacting standards (supporting 1). Their shared type 1 energy is the genuine bond here, creating a mutual respect for integrity and precision. The friction emerges from a fundamental center clash: {{A}} is gut-led and emotionally present, while {{B}} is head-led and characteristically withdrawn.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared type 1 foundation is a real and sturdy bridge: both hold high standards, dislike sloppiness or dishonesty, and feel a genuine calling to improve things.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 and {{B}}'s lead 5 can spark lively intellectual chemistry — {{A}} generates ideas with enthusiasm, {{B}} stress-tests them with depth.
- Both are drawn to purposeful, meaningful work rather than surface-level engagement, giving the relationship a sense of shared mission.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 appreciates {{A}}'s drive and competence, while {{A}}'s lead 1 respects {{B}}'s mastery and exactness.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 needs emotional resonance and to feel seen in their inner world; {{B}}'s lead 5 instinctively conserves emotional energy and pulls back from intensity, which can feel like abandonment to {{A}}.
- {{A}}'s lead 1 can be morally reactive — quick to name what's wrong and expect correction — while {{B}}'s lead 5 resents being told what to do and prefers to reach conclusions independently.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 wants to expand, try new things, and keep options open; {{B}}'s lead 5 prefers to go narrow and deep, finding {{A}}'s breadth scattered.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 values efficiency and results, which can clash with {{A}}'s 4-driven insistence that the process feel authentic and meaningful, not just productive.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s detachment and long silences as emotional indifference or disapproval, when {{B}} is simply processing — the lead 5 needs to retreat in order to engage genuinely.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s moral conviction and emotional expressiveness as irrational or pressure-laden, missing that for a lead 1 with supporting 4, feeling and principle are inseparable — it's not drama, it's integrity.
- {{A}} may feel {{B}} is withholding closeness as a control tactic; {{B}} may feel {{A}} is moralizing as a way to dominate — both misattribute the other's core coping pattern as intentional aggression.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should give {{B}} explicit permission and space to think before responding; pressing for immediate emotional reciprocity will cause {{B}}'s lead 5 to withdraw further.
- {{B}} should practice naming their position on {{A}}'s values — not just their analysis of the facts — since {{A}}'s lead 1 and supporting 4 need to feel that ethics and emotional reality are being taken seriously, not just data-processed.
- Both benefit from framing disagreements as shared problems to solve rather than personal indictments; the mutual type 1 streak means both are vulnerable to feeling criticized, even if {{B}} shows it differently than {{A}}.
- {{A}} should distinguish between moral urgency and emotional need when speaking — collapsing the two can make {{B}}'s 5 shut down entirely.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 5 can genuinely benefit from {{A}}'s 4-supported emotional courage: {{A}} models that vulnerability and conviction can coexist, nudging {{B}} toward the integration path of type 5 (moving toward 8's full embodied presence).
- {{A}}'s lead 1 can benefit enormously from {{B}}'s detached rigor — {{B}} offers a mirror that separates what is actually wrong from what merely offends {{A}}'s standards, helping {{A}} move toward type 1's growth line toward 7's genuine openness.
- The shared type 1 is not just a compatibility glue but a genuine site of accountability: both can call each other out on their own hypocrisies without it feeling like an attack, which is rare and valuable.
- Over time, {{A}} can teach {{B}} that emotional truth is data too, and {{B}} can teach {{A}} that not every imperfection is an emergency — a complementary exchange that matures both people.

268-417.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both heart-center dominant types, meaning this pairing runs on emotional depth, meaning-making, and a hunger for genuine connection — but they orient that hunger in almost opposite directions. {{A}}'s lead 2 reaches outward, finding identity through giving and being needed, while {{B}}'s lead 4 reaches inward, finding identity through being uniquely understood and emotionally authentic. This creates a bond with real warmth and real friction in roughly equal measure.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both lead with the heart center, so neither person is a stranger to emotional intensity or the desire for deep, non-superficial connection.
- {{A}}'s 2 genuinely wants to make {{B}} feel special and seen — and {{B}}'s 4 is starved for exactly that quality of attentiveness.
- {{B}}'s 4 brings creative depth and emotional honesty that {{A}}'s 6 (supporting head type) finds reassuring — here is someone with real loyalty to their inner truth.
- The gut types complement well: {{A}}'s supporting 8 and {{B}}'s supporting 1 both act on conviction, so this pair can move together when a shared cause or value is identified.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 gives generously but often expects reciprocal attention and appreciation; {{B}}'s lead 4 is more focused on receiving understanding than on demonstrating gratitude, which can quietly starve {{A}}.
- {{B}}'s supporting 7 craves novelty and resists being tied down emotionally; {{A}}'s supporting 6 craves security and consistency — these head types are in direct tension around how much freedom versus reliability the relationship should contain.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 can push and confront when frustrated; {{B}}'s supporting 1 responds to perceived criticism with self-righteous counter-judgment, meaning arguments between these two can escalate sharply before either person realizes it.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s need for solitude and emotional withdrawal as rejection or ingratitude, when {{B}}'s 4 is simply processing — absence is not abandonment for a 4.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s helpfulness as conditional or even subtly controlling, when {{A}}'s 2 genuinely experiences giving as love — the manipulation fear is a 4 projection, not always a 2 reality.
- {{A}}'s 6 expresses anxiety through checking in, seeking reassurance, and anticipating problems; {{B}}'s 7 interprets this as pessimism or suffocation and pulls away, which only amplifies {{A}}'s 6 anxiety in a loop.
- {{B}}'s 1 communicates dissatisfaction through principle and critique; {{A}}'s 2 hears critique as personal rejection rather than as an expression of {{B}}'s idealistic standards.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the urge to fix or reframe {{B}}'s darker emotional states — {{B}}'s 4 needs to feel the emotion is witnessed, not solved; staying present without offering solutions is a profound gift here.
- {{B}} should build the habit of naming appreciation explicitly and specifically; {{A}}'s 2 does not assume care is felt unless it is spoken, and a single sincere acknowledgment does more relational work than {{B}} expects.
- When conflict arises, both should agree on a pause signal — {{A}}'s 8 and {{B}}'s 1 together can turn a disagreement into a values clash very quickly, and neither type backs down easily in the heat of it.
- {{A}} can ask directly for what they need rather than hinting; {{B}}'s 4-led processing style means indirect emotional bids are frequently missed, not ignored.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s 4 holds a mirror up to {{A}}'s 2 around self-neglect — the 4's insistence on authentic selfhood can gradually teach {{A}} that their own needs, feelings, and identity deserve as much attention as those they serve.
- {{A}}'s consistent warmth and loyalty (2 and 6 together) provides the stable emotional ground that {{B}}'s 4 rarely finds but deeply needs; over time this can reduce {{B}}'s chronic sense of being fundamentally misunderstood.
- {{A}}'s 8 can model for {{B}}'s 1 that moral conviction does not require perfection to be acted on — power can precede purity.
- The relationship grows healthiest when {{A}} moves from giving-to-be-loved toward giving-from-fullness, and {{B}} moves from being-understood-to-exist toward connecting-in-order-to-share — both shifts loosen the subtle dependency dynamic that pulls this pairing toward codependency at its worst.

127-268.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a deep orientation toward service and care for others, anchored by the 2 energy both carry — though {{A}} expresses it as a principled duty through a 1 lead, while {{B}} lives it as an emotional imperative through a 2 lead. This gives them genuine common ground in values and relational warmth, but their motivational cores diverge sharply: {{A}} is driven by correctness and reform, {{B}} by connection and being needed. The relationship has real potential for mutual respect and complementary strengths, but will require consistent work around criticism, emotional validation, and the difference between moral integrity and relational loyalty.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry 2 energy, meaning service, generosity, and showing up for others feel natural and shared — this creates an immediate sense of 'we care about the same things.'
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 gives them warmth and attunement that {{B}}'s 2-lead genuinely responds to and trusts.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 respects {{A}}'s principled backbone; {{A}}'s 1 lead admires {{B}}'s protective instincts.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 can ease {{B}}'s 6-driven worry with optimism and reframing, offering a lightness {{B}} genuinely benefits from.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body: {{A}}'s 1 lead generates an internal critic that leaks outward — they will notice what is wrong, imprecise, or ethically off, and often feel compelled to say so. {{B}}'s 2 lead is highly sensitive to feeling evaluated or found wanting, experiencing {{A}}'s corrections as emotional rejection rather than helpful feedback. When {{B}}'s supporting 8 activates defensively in response to {{A}}'s critique, it can feel aggressive or disproportionate to {{A}}, triggering their 1's righteous indignation. Meanwhile, {{B}}'s 6 support can read {{A}}'s principled detachment as cold or untrustworthy, creating anxiety spirals that {{A}}'s 1 finds draining and irrational.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s emotional bids and need for reassurance (2 lead + 6 support) as dependency or manipulation, when {{B}} is simply operating from a relational security model.
- {{B}} interprets {{A}}'s 1-driven standards and critique as conditional love — 'you only approve of me when I'm doing it right' — when {{A}} genuinely believes correction is an act of care.
- {{A}}'s 7 support reframes problems with optimism; {{B}}'s 6 support needs worries to be taken seriously first, so {{A}}'s lightness reads as dismissive rather than helpful.
- {{B}}'s 8 directness can register as an attack to {{A}}'s 1, who conflates bluntness with moral failure, when {{B}} is actually trying to be honest and protect the relationship.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should lead with the 2 support — offer appreciation and connection first — before raising concerns or corrections; {{B}}'s 2 lead needs to feel loved before it can hear critique.
- {{B}} should distinguish between the 8's reactive pushback and genuine assertiveness; slowing down before responding to {{A}}'s criticism prevents escalation into a power struggle.
- {{A}} can ask {{B}} directly: 'Do you want me to problem-solve or just listen?' — this respects {{B}}'s relational priority while honoring {{A}}'s instinct to fix.
- {{B}} can name emotions explicitly rather than signaling through behavior; {{A}}'s 1 lead responds better to clarity than to emotional implication, which it tends to misread or dismiss.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} offers {{A}} a powerful mirror for integrating genuine emotional attunement — the 1's shadow is a moralism that can crowd out warmth, and {{B}}'s 2 lead consistently models leading with the heart rather than the rubric. {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally valuable: a model of internalized standards that don't depend on others' approval, which directly challenges the 2 lead's tendency to define worth through being needed. The risk is a co-enabling loop where {{A}} becomes the harsh standard-setter and {{B}} the self-erasing pleaser, reinforcing each other's stress patterns rather than their growth edges. When both are healthy, {{A}}'s integrity and {{B}}'s relational intelligence combine into a genuinely impactful, principled-yet-warm partnership.

258-712.summary: {{A}} leads with the 2's deep relational warmth, backed by the 5's strategic detachment and the 8's raw directness — a quietly powerful presence who gives deliberately. {{B}} leads with the 7's expansive enthusiasm, softened by a supporting 2 and structured by a supporting 1 — a visionary who genuinely wants to help but keeps moving. Shared 2 energy creates an immediate sense of mutual care, but their very different orientations to pace, depth, and emotional need create real friction beneath the surface warmth.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the 2's instinct for generosity and connection, giving this pairing an unusually warm baseline of goodwill toward each other.
- {{A}}'s lead 2 and {{B}}'s supporting 2 mean both are attuned to what the other person needs, often before it's spoken.
- {{B}}'s 7 enthusiasm and {{A}}'s 8 boldness align well when pursuing shared goals — this is a pairing that can build things, lead people, and inspire rooms together.
- {{A}}'s 5 and {{B}}'s 1 both bring a standards-oriented rigor, so they tend to respect each other's intellect and integrity even under stress.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 needs emotional depth and reciprocity; {{B}}'s lead 7 tends to skim emotional surfaces, reframe discomfort into positivity, and move on — which can leave {{A}} feeling unseen or dismissed.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 craves focused depth and sustained inquiry; {{B}}'s lead 7 is drawn to novelty, variety, and breadth, making prolonged deep dives feel like a trap rather than a reward.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 is confrontational and protective of its autonomy; {{B}}'s supporting 1 is critical and reform-minded — two gut types with very different ideas about who is right and who has the authority to say so.
- {{B}}'s 7 actively avoids pain and limitation; {{A}}'s 2-with-8 will sometimes force difficult relational truths into the open, which {{B}} can experience as heavy-handed or punishing.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s rapid optimism and subject-changing as shallowness or emotional avoidance, when {{B}} is genuinely energized by possibility and not necessarily running from depth.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s strategic slowness (supported by the 5) and emotional intensity (supported by the 8) as controlling or overly serious, when {{A}} is simply processing before committing.
- {{A}}'s 2 gives with the implicit expectation of being truly known in return; {{B}}'s 7 gives enthusiastically but diffusely, and may not register that {{A}} is keeping score on emotional reciprocity.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 can issue corrections or moral verdicts that {{A}}'s 8 receives as a power challenge rather than a principled observation, escalating quickly.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should resist the 7 impulse to reframe or pivot when {{A}} raises a concern — naming the emotional reality first, even briefly, signals to {{A}}'s lead 2 that the relationship is secure.
- {{A}} should give {{B}}'s 7 some latitude to brainstorm aloud without treating every idea as a binding commitment; {{B}} thinks by exploring, not by concluding.
- When gut energy flares — {{A}}'s 8 going confrontational or {{B}}'s 1 going critical — both benefit from naming the underlying fear rather than defending the position.
- Their shared 2 is a genuine bridge: invoking it directly ('I care about this because I care about us') tends to de-escalate faster than either logic or force.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s growth direction as a 7 runs directly toward 5 — the focused, depth-seeking investigator that {{A}} carries as a supporting type. In this sense, {{A}} literally models something {{B}} is growing toward: the ability to sit still, go deep, and resist the pull of endless options.
