- {{A}}'s lead 2 gives in order to feel needed and valued; {{B}}'s lead 8 is fiercely self-reliant and may not signal appreciation in ways {{A}} can register, leading {{A}} to feel quietly resentful.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 introduces standards and a corrective, moralizing edge that {{B}}'s 8 will resist hard — being told what is right or good by someone else is one of 8's core triggers.
- {{B}}'s 8 confronts conflict head-on and at volume; {{A}}'s 2-over-1 tends to soften, redirect, or appeal to conscience, which reads to {{B}} as passive or indirect.
- {{B}}'s supporting 7 keeps things moving and resists sitting with heaviness; {{A}}'s 5 needs to slow down, analyze, and sometimes retreat, creating mismatched rhythms.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to interpret {{B}}'s directness and forcefulness as lack of care or emotional crudeness, when in fact {{B}}'s 2 is very much present — it just expresses through protection and loyalty rather than attentiveness and service.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s mentoring impulse — the gentle correction, the principled framing — as a covert bid for control, not recognizing that {{A}}'s 1 genuinely believes they are helping.
- When {{A}}'s 5 kicks in and they withdraw to process, {{B}}'s 8 experiences this as stonewalling or weakness, not as the cognitive necessity it actually is.
- {{A}} may assume {{B}}'s enthusiasm and movement (7 support) means nothing is being taken seriously, underestimating how much {{B}} actually holds internally.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should name appreciation explicitly and often — {{A}}'s lead 2 runs on relational acknowledgment, and {{B}}'s default assumption that care is self-evident will leave {{A}} running on empty.
- {{A}} should lead with directness before softening: {{B}}'s 8 hears the diplomatic wrap as the message, and will lose trust if they later discover a harder truth was buried inside.
- When conflict heats up, {{A}} should resist the urge to pivot to principles and 'what's right' — engage the actual tension first, then bring in values once {{B}} feels heard.
- {{B}} should resist the reflex to escalate when {{A}} retreats; {{A}}'s 5 withdrawal is temporary and will produce better conversation if given room rather than pressure.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} something the 2-5-1 configuration quietly needs: permission to want things directly, without first making themselves useful to earn it. {{B}}'s 8 doesn't ask — it simply claims, and watching this can be liberating for {{A}}.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something the 8-2-7 genuinely lacks: reflective depth. {{A}}'s 5 support models that slowing down to think is not weakness, and {{A}}'s 1 provides an ethical anchor that can mature {{B}}'s raw power into principled leadership.
- The shadow risk is codependency in reverse — {{A}} over-giving and building silent resentment while {{B}} unconsciously relies on {{A}}'s structure and conscience without reciprocating the emotional labor.
- At their best, {{A}} sharpens {{B}}'s wisdom and {{B}} emboldens {{A}}'s agency — a mentor who finally acts and a challenger who finally reflects.

216-835.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} form a pairing of deep relational investment and formidable drive, but they approach the world from almost opposite centers of gravity — {{A}} leads from the heart with a compulsion to nurture and belong, while {{B}} leads from the gut with a compulsion to challenge, protect, and conquer. There is genuine complementarity here: {{A}} brings warmth and moral grounding, {{B}} brings power and strategic clarity. The friction, however, is real and requires deliberate attention, because {{A}}'s emotional needs and {{B}}'s blunt autonomy can create a cycle of over-giving and under-receiving that quietly erodes the relationship.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 genuinely wants to support people who are doing big things, and {{B}}'s lead 8 is almost always doing big things — this makes {{A}} a natural champion for {{B}}'s ambitions.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 values competence and results, and {{A}}'s supporting 1 holds high standards, so both share a mutual respect for doing things right and well.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 is fiercely loyal once trust is established, and {{B}}'s lead 8 prizes loyalty above nearly all else — this is a genuine bond-forming instinct.
- When {{B}} faces a real problem, {{A}}'s combination of emotional attunement (2), practical ethics (1), and loyalty under pressure (6) makes them an unusually steady and trustworthy partner.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 has an emotional economy that expects care to be reciprocated; {{B}}'s lead 8 gives protection and resources, not tenderness, and this asymmetry can leave {{A}} quietly depleted.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 will occasionally surface moral corrections or principled objections — and {{B}}'s lead 8 has a deeply visceral resistance to being told what to do or judged, which can turn a small disagreement into a power struggle.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 generates anxiety and needs reassurance; {{B}}'s supporting 5 retreats into detachment when overwhelmed, and these two patterns feed each other badly — {{A}} reaches for connection exactly when {{B}} withdraws.
- {{B}}'s blunt honesty, amplified by the 8's all-or-nothing gut energy, can land as harshness on {{A}}'s thin-skinned 2 lead, triggering shame rather than dialogue.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s directness and self-sufficiency as indifference or rejection, when in fact {{B}}'s lead 8 expresses care through action, problem-solving, and showing up in crises — not through emotional check-ins.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s help-giving and relational warmth as either neediness or a subtle attempt at control, missing that {{A}}'s 2 lead genuinely experiences giving as connection, not manipulation.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 looks for verbal reassurance and consistency as safety signals; {{B}}'s supporting 5 finds such requests draining and may go quiet, which {{A}} registers as a threat to the relationship rather than a recharge behavior.
- {{B}} can mistake {{A}}'s moral boundaries (driven by the supporting 1) for rigidity or passive judgment, rather than seeing them as a principled ethic that actually makes {{A}} a more reliable and trustworthy partner.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should state needs directly and specifically rather than hinting or hoping {{B}} will notice — {{B}}'s lead 8 responds to clarity and loses patience with indirection, and {{A}}'s supporting 6 anxiety can turn unspoken needs into resentment fast.
- {{B}} should offer explicit, concrete appreciation when {{A}} helps — a brief, sincere acknowledgment costs {{B}} almost nothing but addresses {{A}}'s core 2 hunger to know the giving was received and valued.
- When conflict arises, {{A}} should resist the 2's tendency to smooth things over prematurely; {{B}} actually trusts people more when they push back, so a direct statement of disagreement will land better than managed politeness.
- {{B}} should flag when a withdrawal is about needing space (5 support pattern) rather than anger, because without that signal {{A}}'s 6 will catastrophize the silence.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}} offers {{B}} something genuinely rare: consistent, non-transactional care that does not flinch when {{B}}'s 8 energy gets big, combined with the 1's willingness to hold {{B}} to a standard of integrity. This can pull {{B}} toward the 8's integration point — which is type 2 — helping {{B}} access vulnerability and genuine generosity rather than power-as-care. Conversely, {{B}} models for {{A}} what it looks like to assert needs without apology, hold a boundary without guilt, and trust personal strength rather than relying on being needed — all correctives to the 2's core trap. The real growth edge is mutual: {{A}} must learn that being loved by {{B}} looks like protection and presence, not warmth and words, and {{B}} must learn that {{A}}'s emotional attunement is a form of intelligence, not weakness. Done well, this pairing produces a partnership that is both deeply human and unusually capable.

315-925.summary: {{A}} leads with driven, achievement-oriented 3 energy refined by analytical 5 and principled 1, making them a precise, results-focused operator who measures worth through competence and output. {{B}} leads with harmony-seeking 9 energy supported by helpful 2 and curious 5, making them a steady, accommodating presence who values peace, connection, and intellectual depth. Together they share a genuine intellectual wavelength through their mutual 5, but the gap between {{A}}'s forward momentum and {{B}}'s conflict-averse steadiness will require deliberate navigation.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared supporting 5 is the clearest point of natural rapport — both appreciate analytical rigor, systems thinking, and getting things right before acting.
- {{A}}'s 3 respects competence above almost everything, and {{B}}'s 5-supported problem-solving approach earns that respect quickly.
- {{B}}'s lead 9 provides a calm, non-competitive presence that quietly defuses the performance pressure {{A}}'s 3 can carry, making the space feel safer than most.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 brings genuine warmth and attentiveness that {{A}}'s task-oriented 3 often craves but struggles to seek out on its own.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 moves fast, adapts readily, and keeps score by visible progress; {{B}}'s lead 9 moves at its own deliberate pace and can dig in with quiet stubbornness when pushed, creating a chronic pacing mismatch.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 applies high standards and will name imperfections directly; {{B}}'s 9 experiences this as pressure or implicit criticism and tends to withdraw rather than engage with it.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 needs reciprocal warmth and acknowledgment, but {{A}}'s 3 defaults to task-level recognition and can come across as emotionally withholding without meaning to.
- When stress hits, {{A}}'s 3 accelerates and sharpens while {{B}}'s 9 numbs and disengages — they move in opposite directions precisely when coordination matters most.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} frequently reads {{B}}'s 9-led conflict-avoidance as passive agreement or disengagement, not realizing {{B}} holds firm, considered positions that simply never get voiced unless the relationship feels completely safe.
- {{B}} can misread {{A}}'s image-consciousness and efficiency focus as shallowness or self-promotion, missing the genuine drive for excellence and contribution underneath the 3's polished surface.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 frames critique as an act of care — fixing what's broken — but {{B}}'s 9 absorbs it as a signal that the relationship itself is at risk, triggering shutdown rather than collaboration.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 gives generously and expects attunement in return; {{A}}'s 3 offers results and solutions as love language, which lands as efficient but not tender.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should explicitly invite {{B}} to disagree — ask direct questions like "What do you actually think about this?" and wait, because {{B}}'s 9 will not volunteer dissent without a clear, low-stakes opening.
- {{B}} should practice stating preferences and objections in the moment rather than accommodating and resenting later; {{A}}'s 3 genuinely responds to straightforward information and won't take it personally the way {{B}}'s 9 fears.
- When {{A}}'s 1 needs to raise a concern, framing it around shared standards ("I want this to be as strong as we can make it") lands far better than pointing at what's wrong.
- {{B}}'s 2 should name its need for appreciation explicitly rather than waiting for {{A}} to intuit it — {{A}}'s 3 is highly responsive to direct requests but often blind to unspoken emotional bids.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 9 models something {{A}}'s 3 genuinely needs: the ability to be still, to let worth exist independent of output, and to experience a relationship that isn't implicitly a performance.
- {{A}}'s 3 offers {{B}}'s 9 a clear example of purposeful self-assertion and goal ownership — healthy exposure to ambition that {{B}} can borrow without having to abandon its own pace.
- The real growth risk is a collusion pattern: {{B}}'s 9 accommodates {{A}}'s 3 to keep the peace, {{A}}'s 3 mistakes that accommodation for full buy-in, and both avoid the friction that would actually develop them.
- The relationship reaches its healthiest form when {{B}} trusts that voicing disagreement won't threaten connection, and {{A}} learns to value {{B}}'s honest resistance more than smooth agreement.

126-612.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share every number in their tritype, which creates an unusually strong foundation of shared values — loyalty, duty, helpfulness, and a desire to do what is right. Yet because their lead types differ (gut-driven 1 for {{A}} versus head-driven 6 for {{B}}), they approach the same ideals from fundamentally different stances: {{A}} leads with principled certainty while {{B}} leads with vigilant questioning. This creates a pairing that can feel deeply validating or quietly maddening depending on the day.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry a strong internal code of responsibility — the shared 1 energy means neither tolerates cutting corners or broken commitments.
- The supporting 2 in both creates genuine warmth and a mutual instinct to show up for people they care about, including each other.
- The shared 6 means both understand loyalty as an active, demonstrated practice rather than just a feeling.
- They will rarely have to explain why something matters morally — the other already gets it at a gut level.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body: {{A}}'s lead 1 produces a quality of settled moral conviction — when the right course of action is clear, {{A}} wants to move. {{B}}'s lead 6, by contrast, generates doubt, contingency thinking, and a need to stress-test decisions before trusting them. {{A}} can experience {{B}}'s hesitation as procrastination or a lack of backbone, while {{B}} can experience {{A}}'s decisiveness as rigidity or a failure to account for real risks. The supporting 6 in {{A}} means {{A}} does feel anxiety — but it surfaces after the principle is identified, not before, which puts these two consistently out of phase.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{B}} may read {{A}}'s certainty as arrogance or closed-mindedness, when in fact {{A}}'s gut center is simply processing faster and in a more embodied way than {{B}}'s head center registers as safe. Conversely, {{A}} may read {{B}}'s persistent questioning as disloyalty or a challenge to authority, when {{B}} is actually trying to secure the relationship and the plan by scanning for what could go wrong. Because both share a supporting 2, each may also silently expect the other to anticipate their emotional needs without stating them — and both can feel subtly overlooked when that doesn't happen.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should name the principle behind a decision out loud, not just the conclusion — this gives {{B}}'s lead 6 something concrete to evaluate rather than just a directive to follow.
- {{B}} should distinguish between anxiety-driven worst-case spirals and genuine concerns worth raising; flagging which one it is helps {{A}} respond with patience instead of frustration.
- When tension arises, both should lean into the shared 2 — expressing care directly rather than letting resentment build under a veneer of helpfulness.
- {{A}} can invite {{B}}'s input as a quality-control step rather than a threat to authority, which honors {{B}}'s vigilance as useful.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}} grows by loosening the grip of the lead 1's inner critic — {{B}}'s habit of questioning assumptions, when not anxiety-laden, is a genuine gift that can help {{A}} distinguish between principled standards and rigid perfectionism. {{B}} grows by borrowing {{A}}'s gut-level confidence: watching {{A}} act from conviction without needing external validation can teach {{B}} that trust in oneself is possible. Because neither is prone to avoidance or emotional withdrawal — the shared 1 and 6 both engage — this pairing has real potential to work through friction rather than around it, provided they treat each other's lead center as a different strength rather than a deficiency.

639-728.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both head-center leads, but they process the world through opposite head strategies — {{A}}'s lead 6 scans for threats and craves secure footing, while {{B}}'s lead 7 races toward possibility and resists being pinned down. Their supporting types create an interesting complementarity ({{A}}'s 3 and 9 vs. {{B}}'s 2 and 8) that can either balance or destabilize the pairing depending on how consciously each person works with their patterns. This is a relationship with real warmth and potential, but it requires both people to stretch past their default coping styles.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both leading from the head center means {{A}} and {{B}} share a natural orientation toward ideas, planning, and making sense of the world — conversations can be stimulating and wide-ranging.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 generates genuine warmth and attentiveness that {{A}}'s lead 6 deeply appreciates; feeling cared for lowers {{A}}'s baseline anxiety significantly.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 and {{B}}'s lead 7 share an energetic, goal-oriented frequency — they can feed each other's ambition and enthusiasm in productive bursts.
- {{A}}'s supporting 9 and {{B}}'s supporting 2 both prioritize harmony and others' comfort, creating a mutual goodwill that smooths over everyday friction.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 6 needs consistency, follow-through, and demonstrated loyalty — {{B}}'s lead 7 naturally pivots toward the next exciting thing, which can register to {{A}} as unreliable or noncommittal.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 is direct and confrontational when challenged; {{A}}'s supporting 9 suppresses conflict to keep the peace, meaning tension builds silently on {{A}}'s side until it erupts or calcifies into distance.
- {{A}}'s 6-driven worst-case-scenario thinking can feel like a wet blanket to {{B}}'s 7, who actively avoids dwelling in anxiety or limitation.
- {{B}}'s desire for freedom and open options can directly threaten {{A}}'s core need for a stable, predictable alliance.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} often reads {{B}}'s enthusiasm and subject-switching as a lack of seriousness or commitment, when {{B}} is simply wired to explore broadly before (or instead of) going deep.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s vigilance and questioning as distrust or pessimism, not recognizing that for a lead 6, doubt is an act of loyalty — {{A}} tests because {{A}} wants to believe.
- {{A}}'s supporting 9 creates a pattern of going along outwardly while quietly accumulating grievances; {{B}}'s lead 7 and supporting 8, both direct processors, rarely notice this passive resistance until it becomes a serious rupture.
- {{B}} may assume that {{A}}'s 3 ambition means {{A}} is fine with keeping things light and forward-moving, underestimating how much the lead 6 needs emotional grounding and reassurance underneath that performance.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should name anxieties and concerns directly and early — the 6's habit of testing indirectly, or the 9's habit of saying nothing, will frustrate {{B}}'s 7 and 8, who respond much better to plain speech.
- {{B}} should slow down enough to explicitly signal commitment and follow through on small promises; for {{A}}'s lead 6, consistency in the small things is the actual proof of trustworthiness.
- When {{B}}'s supporting 8 gets blunt or escalatory, {{A}} should resist the 9 impulse to shut down — a short, grounded response ('I need a moment before we continue') works better than silence or appeasement.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 can be a useful bridge: framing concerns as shared goals rather than worries tends to land better with {{B}}'s optimism-oriented lead 7.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 7 is one of the most powerful antidotes to {{A}}'s 6-driven fear paralysis — genuine enthusiasm and forward motion can pull {{A}} out of rumination and into action, if {{B}} offers this patiently rather than dismissively.
- Conversely, {{A}}'s lead 6 offers {{B}} something rare and genuinely valuable: real loyalty, sustained attention, and the willingness to think through consequences — the grounding that {{B}}'s 7 often lacks and secretly needs.
- {{A}} grows by practicing trust without complete certainty, learning that {{B}}'s freedom-seeking is not abandonment; {{B}} grows by tolerating depth, commitment, and the discomfort of sitting with someone else's anxiety instead of escaping it.
- At their best, {{A}} teaches {{B}} that security is worth building, and {{B}} teaches {{A}} that not every open door is a threat.

613-827.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} form a high-energy, results-oriented pairing with genuine loyalty at the center, but they approach the world through fundamentally different operating systems — {{A}} processes through anxious, analytical caution while {{B}} leads with gut-level force and forward momentum. The attraction is real: {{A}} is drawn to {{B}}'s strength and decisiveness, and {{B}} respects {{A}}'s reliability and follow-through. The friction is equally real: {{A}}'s need to question, verify, and build consensus can feel like a brake on {{B}}'s instinct to charge ahead.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both value loyalty fiercely — {{A}}'s lead 6 makes it a core need, and {{B}}'s supporting 2 makes it a love language, creating a bond that can feel like an alliance.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 and {{B}}'s lead 8 are both achievement-oriented and respect competence; they can build and execute together with impressive efficiency.
- {{B}}'s strength and protective energy is genuinely stabilizing for {{A}}'s lead 6, which is always scanning for trustworthy figures to anchor to.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 brings ethical grounding that {{B}}'s lead 8 — which has its own gut-level sense of justice — instinctively respects.

sections.heading: Where you grate

When channeled well, {{A}}'s vision of how things *should* be and {{B}}'s enthusiasm for what *could* be can align into shared idealism and ambitious collaboration.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 is wired to notice flaws, errors, and ethical lapses — and to say something about them. {{B}}'s lead 7 treats correction as constraint and will quickly resist, deflect, or reframe rather than absorb the critique.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 craves emotional honesty and depth; {{B}}'s lead 7 is structurally avoidant of pain and difficulty, which can leave {{A}} feeling unseen or dismissed.
- {{B}}'s pace is fast, scattered, and future-oriented; {{A}}'s 5 and 1 demand thoroughness and correctness before moving on — creating chronic friction around timelines and follow-through.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 can slip into image management over authenticity, which {{A}}'s 1 and 4 will both find quietly corrosive.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s optimism and reframing as avoidance of responsibility or intellectual laziness — what {{B}} experiences as healthy forward focus, {{A}} codes as dodging hard truths. Conversely, {{B}} is likely to experience {{A}}'s critical precision and emotional intensity as rigidity or negativity, missing that {{A}}'s standards come from deep care rather than judgment for its own sake. {{A}}'s supporting 4 can produce bouts of melancholy or a felt sense of being fundamentally different that {{B}}'s lead 7 genuinely doesn't know how to sit with — {{B}} may try to fix or cheer up what {{A}} actually needs witnessed. {{B}}'s supporting 9 may also go quiet or vague when {{A}}'s 1 wants a direct reckoning, which {{A}} interprets as indifference rather than conflict avoidance.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should front-load warmth before launching into critique — {{B}}'s lead 7 hears relentless correction as a wall and will mentally exit the conversation.
- {{B}} should resist the urge to immediately reframe or silver-line {{A}}'s concerns; slowing down to actually engage the problem signals respect to {{A}}'s 1 and 5.
- {{A}} can access {{B}}'s 9 by keeping tone collaborative rather than prosecutorial — the 9 wants harmony and will meet {{A}} there if not put on the defensive.
- {{B}} should avoid making commitments that the 7's scattered energy won't sustain — {{A}}'s 1 tracks broken follow-through and will lose trust quickly.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: At their best, {{B}} genuinely loosens {{A}}'s inner grip — the 7's delight in experience and the 9's ease can teach {{A}}'s lead 1 that not everything requires correction, and that joy is not frivolous. In return, {{A}} offers {{B}} something {{B}}'s lead 7 quietly needs but resists: depth, integrity, and the grounding that comes from seeing a thing all the way through. The risk pattern is a negative spiral where {{A}} tightens standards as {{B}} becomes more evasive, and {{B}} escapes further as {{A}} increases pressure — both moves feel self-protective but accelerate the rupture. Growth for this pairing requires {{A}} to distinguish between what truly matters ethically and what is merely a preference, and for {{B}} to develop the tolerance for discomfort that allows real intimacy rather than perpetual forward momentum.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- Two lead 8s in the same space means two people who instinctively move to control the direction, the pace, and the terms — collisions over dominance are not occasional, they are structural.
- The 4 support amplifies grievance-holding; when either {{A}} or {{B}} feels disrespected, the wound goes deep and the retaliation can be outsized relative to the original offense.
- The 7 support pushes both toward reframing pain into forward motion, which can cause each to prematurely escape conflict resolution rather than sitting with accountability.
- There is a risk of competitive one-upmanship where each escalates intensity to prove they are not the one who backs down first.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- Because {{A}} and {{B}} use the same defense architecture, each assumes the other's anger or withdrawal means exactly what it would mean coming from themselves — but the internal trigger stack can still differ in timing and threshold, leading to misread escalations.
- The 4 support in both creates a private emotional interior that the outward 8 presentation conceals; {{A}} may not realize {{B}} is genuinely wounded beneath the combative stance, and vice versa, because neither broadcasts vulnerability easily.
- Both may interpret the other's need for autonomy as rejection rather than a healthy self-regulation move, since the 8 lead reads space-seeking as a power withdrawal.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- Name the bid for dominance when you feel it — saying 'I notice we're both trying to steer this' is more productive than each pushing harder until someone breaks.
- Let the 4 support speak: both {{A}} and {{B}} have access to emotional vocabulary beneath the 8 surface; using it deliberately rather than defaulting to blunt force changes the register of conflict.
- Build in explicit repair rituals after clashes, because the 7 support in both will otherwise rush past unresolved hurt toward the next exciting thing, leaving a residue of unprocessed grievance.
- Be specific with appreciation — 8s tend to skip acknowledgment, but {{A}} and {{B}}'s shared 4 genuinely needs to feel seen, not just respected.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- The highest version of this pairing is two people who use their identical architecture to hold each other accountable in ways that softer companions never could — {{A}} cannot easily fool {{B}} about self-deception, and the reverse is equally true.
- The shared 8-to-2 growth path means both are capable of genuine generosity and vulnerability; consciously practicing that direction together rather than competing in strength creates the most sustainable bond.
- The risk is mutual stagnation in the 8's fixation on control and the 4's fixation on grievance — growth requires one, and ideally both, to voluntarily stand down first, modeling the very vulnerability the type most resists.

269-513.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} represent a classic heart-meets-head pairing — one leading with warmth, relational attunement, and the need to be needed, the other with intellectual mastery, autonomy, and principled competence. There is genuine mutual fascination here, as each offers what the other quietly lacks, but the gap between {{A}}'s emotionally expressive, connection-seeking lead 2 and {{B}}'s characteristically withdrawn lead 5 creates real friction that requires conscious navigation. With effort and self-awareness, this pairing can be deeply complementary; without it, each person risks feeling either smothered or abandoned.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 and {{B}}'s lead 5 share a head-center commitment to loyalty, reliability, and thinking things through — both value trust built over time rather than superficial charm.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 genuinely appreciates {{A}}'s social warmth and relational ease, areas where the 5-led {{B}} knows it has gaps.
- {{A}}'s supporting 9 creates a natural accommodating buffer, giving {{B}} the breathing room a lead 5 requires without {{A}} feeling entirely unseen.
- Both tend toward conscientiousness: {{A}}'s 6 brings loyalty and follow-through; {{B}}'s supporting 1 brings integrity and high standards — shared values around doing things right.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 gives freely and expects reciprocal warmth; {{B}}'s lead 5 guards energy and emotional resources closely, which can leave {{A}} perpetually feeling undernourished in the relationship.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 generates anxiety and seeks reassurance; {{B}}'s 5 finds emotional reassurance-seeking draining and may respond with fact-based logic rather than comfort, missing the point entirely.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 can deliver sharp, principled critiques; {{A}}'s lead 2 is sensitive to feeling evaluated or found lacking, especially by someone they have invested care in.
- {{A}}'s 9 may suppress its own unmet needs to avoid conflict, creating invisible resentment that {{B}}'s detached 5 will genuinely not detect until it erupts.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to interpret {{B}}'s withdrawal and emotional economy as rejection, coldness, or a sign that something is wrong in the relationship — the lead 2's core fear of being unloved reads distance as data. {{B}}, in turn, tends to interpret {{A}}'s emotional bids, hints, and need for closeness as intrusion or pressure, not as the love language they actually are. {{A}}'s supporting 6 anxiety can look irrational or manipulative to {{B}}'s analytically grounded lead 5, while {{B}}'s compartmentalized emotional style (with a supporting 3 that can seem performative rather than genuine) can seem cold or even dishonest to {{A}}.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should state needs explicitly and directly rather than hinting or giving in hope of reciprocation — the lead 5 in {{B}} will not reliably read between lines.
- {{B}} should offer brief, clear verbal acknowledgment of {{A}}'s feelings before pivoting to problem-solving; a single sentence of genuine recognition means more to a lead 2 than a ten-minute analysis.
- {{A}} should give {{B}} scheduled or predictable alone time rather than framing withdrawal as rejection — the 5's need for recharge is not personal.
- {{B}} should engage {{A}}'s supporting 6 directly with honest, consistent reassurance; vagueness or silence activates {{A}}'s anxiety spiral in ways that cost both people energy.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}} has a genuine opportunity to help {{B}} build emotional vocabulary and relational presence — the lead 5's growth edge is toward the 8 (embodiment, engagement) and its heart-center is underdeveloped, and {{A}}'s natural warmth models what connection without performance looks like. {{B}} offers {{A}} something equally valuable: the permission to stop giving in order to earn love, and an intellectual grounding that can steady {{A}}'s supporting 6 anxiety. The risk is that {{A}} over-functions emotionally while {{B}} under-functions, reinforcing both people's least healthy patterns rather than challenging them. At its best, this is a relationship where {{A}} learns that love can include boundaries and intellectual confidence, and {{B}} learns that vulnerability is not a liability.

478-729.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a restless creative energy — both carry the 7 in their tritype and are drawn to intensity, possibility, and self-expression. However, {{A}} leads with the 4's deep hunger for authenticity and emotional truth, while {{B}} leads with the 7's drive toward forward motion and positive reframing, making their emotional registers frequently out of sync. This pairing has real chemistry and genuine complementarity, but it requires deliberate work to bridge the gap between depth and lightness.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the 7, giving them a shared appetite for ideas, stimulation, and experience — conversations between them can be electric and wide-ranging.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 resonates with {{B}}'s lead 7, creating a mutual enthusiasm that can fuel creative projects and adventures.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 brings genuine warmth that {{A}}'s heart-led 4 genuinely appreciates, while {{A}}'s supporting 8 offers a boldness that {{B}}'s 7 finds exciting rather than threatening.
- Both dislike phoniness in different ways: {{A}}'s 4 craves authenticity, and {{B}}'s 7 resists pretense, so there's a shared allergy to superficiality that can bond them.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- The central friction is {{A}}'s lead 4 needing to descend into emotional depth versus {{B}}'s lead 7 instinctively pivoting away from pain and toward reframing — what feels like honesty to {{A}} can feel like wallowing to {{B}}.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 is direct and at times confrontational; {{B}}'s supporting 9 is conflict-avoidant and harmony-seeking, meaning {{A}} may keep pushing conversations {{B}} wants to close.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 has a helper instinct that can shade into managing or rescuing, which {{A}}'s 4 reads as intrusive or condescending to their self-concept as a unique individual.
- {{A}} can get absorbed in their own emotional world in a way that leaves {{B}} feeling unseen, triggering the 2's fear of being unappreciated.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s 7-led optimism as emotional avoidance or shallowness — a refusal to face what is real — when in fact {{B}} genuinely experiences life through a lens of possibility rather than suppressing pain.
- {{B}} is likely to read {{A}}'s 4-led intensity and melancholy as dramatization or self-indulgence, when {{A}} is in fact doing the sincere emotional work their lead type requires.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 comes out as bluntness in conflict; {{B}'s supporting 9 interprets this as aggression and shuts down, which {{A}} then reads as passivity or dishonesty — a loop that can repeat without either person understanding the other's mechanism.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should resist the 7's reflex to immediately reframe or silver-lining {{A}}'s emotional disclosures; staying present without fixing signals to {{A}}'s 4 that they are truly heard.
- {{A}} should recognize that {{B}}'s 7-led lightness is not a character flaw or avoidance — naming appreciation for {{B}}'s warmth (the 2) goes a long way given the 2's need to feel valued.
- When conflict arises, {{A}} can soften the 8's directness by leading with the 4's emotional vocabulary rather than the 8's declarative force, which gives {{B}}'s 9 room to stay engaged rather than withdraw.
- {{B}} can invite {{A}} into shared enthusiasm (the 7 channel they share) as a way to reconnect after emotional ruptures, rather than expecting {{A}} to snap out of depth on their own.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 4 offers {{B}} a genuine model for sitting with discomfort and discovering what lies beneath the surface — a real developmental gift for a 7 who tends to sprint past difficulty.
- {{B}}'s lead 7, in turn, can help {{A}}'s 4 loosen its grip on suffering as identity and experience the joy that the 4's own supporting 7 points toward but struggles to access.
- {{B}}'s 2 models generosity and other-orientation that can stretch {{A}}'s sometimes self-referential 4, while {{A}}'s 8 models a kind of self-authorization that can help {{B}}'s 9 develop stronger personal boundaries.
- At their best, this pairing produces something neither achieves alone: emotionally honest creativity with genuine vitality — the Messenger's depth amplified by the Peacemaker's connective warmth.

315-847.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both high-octane, driven types who can build something formidable together when aligned, but their routes to power differ sharply: {{A}} leads with image, competence, and polish while {{B}} leads with raw force, passion, and unapologetic directness. The pairing has real magnetism — each has what the other often lacks — but the tension between 3's performance-orientation and 8's confrontational authenticity can become a genuine fault line. Whether this relationship thrives or stalls depends on how much each is willing to be honest rather than strategic.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both are intensely goal-oriented: {{A}}'s lead 3 drives toward achievement and excellence, while {{B}}'s lead 8 drives toward impact and dominance — in a shared project, this creates formidable momentum.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 and {{B}}'s supporting 7 give them a shared intellectual current; they can riff on ideas, enjoy competence-based conversation, and respect each other's mental sharpness.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 and {{B}}'s lead 8 both care deeply about doing things *right* — 1 through principles, 8 through gut-level justice — which can create a strong ethical backbone in the relationship.
- Neither type wallows in passivity; they are both doers, and that shared energy creates mutual respect.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 manages perception carefully and pivots under pressure, which {{B}}'s lead 8 can experience as slippery or inauthentic — 8 expects people to stand their ground, not adjust their presentation.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 hungers for emotional depth and rawness; {{A}}'s lead 3 tends to suppress or bypass emotion in service of appearing capable, which will frustrate {{B}} at an almost visceral level.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 has a strong inner critic and a need for things to be done *correctly*; {{B}}'s lead 8 moves fast and can steamroll process, creating friction around standards and quality control.
- {{B}}'s bluntness can feel like an attack to {{A}}, who reads social feedback through the lens of image and success — direct criticism can land harder than {{B}} intends.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{B}} is likely to read {{A}}'s image-management and adaptability as political or two-faced, when {{A}} is actually trying to be effective and responsive — 3's shape-shifting is a strategy, not deception.
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s confrontational lead-8 style as power-hungry or controlling, missing that {{B}}'s 4 undercurrent means there is genuine emotional investment and vulnerability beneath the forcefulness.
- When conflict arises, {{A}}'s 5 support causes them to withdraw and analyze; {{B}}'s 8 lead wants to engage immediately and directly — this timing mismatch makes each feel abandoned or steamrolled respectively.
- {{B}}'s 7 optimism can seem like it glosses over problems that {{A}}'s perfectionist 1 considers non-negotiable, leading {{A}} to see {{B}} as reckless even when {{B}} is being genuinely visionary.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should curb the 8 instinct to dominate the conversational space when {{A}} is processing; giving {{A}} time to analyze (5) and formulate a principled response (1) yields far more honest dialogue than forcing an immediate answer.
- {{A}} needs to drop the 3 habit of reframing criticism or deflecting with competence — {{B}}'s 8 and 4 combination responds to directness and emotional honesty far more than to polished explanations.
- When {{A}} raises a standards-based concern (from the 1), framing it as principle rather than criticism of {{B}}'s character will prevent {{B}}'s 8 from going into challenge mode.
- {{B}} can invite {{A}}'s real feelings by explicitly distinguishing criticism of performance from criticism of worth — that distinction matters enormously to a lead 3.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} pushes {{A}} toward authenticity: the 8's refusal to accept a curated persona challenges {{A}}'s lead 3 to discover who they are beneath the achievement, which is genuinely developmental work for a 3.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something rare: a model of strategic finesse and calibrated action that the 8 often lacks — {{B}}'s raw power is made more effective when filtered through {{A}}'s precision and 1-supported integrity.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 can help {{A}} access emotional depth that the 3-5-1 configuration often bypasses, while {{A}}'s 5 support can give {{B}}'s passionate 8-4 intensity a grounding in analysis and evidence.
- The risk is that without real trust, {{A}} performs for {{B}} and {{B}} dominates {{A}}, locking both into their worst patterns — growth requires {{A}} to be real and {{B}} to be gentle enough to make that safe.

279-512.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a heart-meets-head pairing that can feel both deeply nourishing and quietly frustrating. {{A}}'s lead 2 orients everything around connection, warmth, and mutual care, while {{B}}'s lead 5 orients everything around understanding, privacy, and competence — two fundamentally different survival strategies that can complement each other beautifully if neither person pathologizes the other's style. The shared 2 energy between them is the most reliable bridge, giving {{B}} a soft relational channel and giving {{A}} the sense of being genuinely cared for.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry 2 energy — {{A}} as the lead and {{B}} as a supporting type — which means there is a genuine undercurrent of mutual care and investment in each other's wellbeing.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 brings playful curiosity that genuinely delights {{B}}'s lead 5; they can spend hours in engaged, exploratory conversation without running dry.
- {{B}}'s depth of knowledge and focused sincerity appeals to {{A}}'s desire to feel truly seen, not just socially entertained.
- {{A}}'s 9 creates a low-drama, accepting atmosphere that {{B}}'s 5 finds deeply safe — rare for a type that usually guards its inner world fiercely.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 runs on reciprocity and emotional responsiveness; {{B}}'s lead 5 withdraws to recharge and can go long stretches without emotional output, leaving {{A}} feeling quietly starved.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 carries a critical inner standard that can surface as pointed corrections or cool evaluations, which collides hard with {{A}}'s 2-and-9 need for harmony and approval.
- {{A}}'s 9 tends to suppress personal needs to keep the peace, which means resentment builds slowly and invisibly — a dynamic {{B}}'s detached 5 is not naturally wired to detect.
- {{A}}'s 7 can push toward spontaneity and social expansion in ways that feel draining and distracting to {{B}}'s need for controlled, quiet space.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s natural withdrawal as emotional rejection or proof of insufficient care, when {{B}} is simply doing what a lead 5 does — retreating to process and refuel. Conversely, {{B}} may misread {{A}}'s warmth and attentiveness as either smothering dependency or, through the lens of the 5's skepticism about motives, as a subtle bid for control — a misattribution that stings {{A}} deeply. {{A}}'s combination of 2 self-erasure and 9 conflict avoidance means {{B}} rarely receives a clear signal of what {{A}} actually needs, and {{B}}'s lead 5 is not inclined to read between the lines — so both end up frustrated for reasons neither has fully named.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should practice stating needs in plain, direct language rather than hinting or hoping {{B}} will intuit them; {{B}}'s 5 responds to clarity, not emotional subtext.
- {{B}} should offer brief but explicit signals of care and engagement — a specific compliment, a check-in question — because {{A}}'s lead 2 genuinely needs those moments to feel secure in the relationship.
- When {{B}}'s supporting 1 surfaces as criticism, framing it as a shared intellectual problem rather than a personal evaluation will help {{A}}'s 2-and-9 receive it without shutting down.
- {{A}} should give {{B}} advance notice before large social or emotional demands, respecting that the 5 needs to mentally prepare rather than be pulled into intensity unexpectedly.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} offers {{A}} something the 279 stack quietly needs but rarely asks for: intellectual structure, honest feedback, and a model of drawing firm boundaries without guilt. Exposure to {{B}}'s lead 5 and supporting 1 can help {{A}} develop a stronger personal spine — moving away from the 2's tendency to lose the self in others' needs. In return, {{A}} offers {{B}} something the 512 genuinely struggles to cultivate alone: embodied emotional warmth, ease with relational messiness, and the lived demonstration that intimacy does not have to be earned through competence. If {{B}} allows {{A}}'s influence in, the dormant 2 in {{B}}'s stack can finally come forward — and that is where this pairing reaches its real potential.

145-713.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a pairing of principled depth meeting enthusiastic momentum — they share a 1 in their tritypes and both bring intellectual seriousness, but they arrive from opposite directions: {{A}} leads with gut-based correctness and slows everything down to get it right, while {{B}} leads with head-based possibility and accelerates past obstacles to stay stimulated. This creates genuine creative tension that can either be generative or grinding depending on how well they navigate their fundamentally different relationships to limitation and error.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry a 1 in their tritype, meaning a shared baseline of caring about quality, ethics, and doing things properly — this gives them a common moral language that many other pairings lack.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 and {{B}}'s lead 7 are both head-center types, so intellectual engagement comes naturally; they can trade ideas with real enthusiasm.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 quietly appreciates {{A}}'s rigor even when the lead 7 chafes against it — {{B}} won't dismiss {{A}}'s standards as needless fussiness the way a pure 7 might.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 gives them emotional authenticity that {{B}}'s 3 and 7 combination secretly craves, since {{B}} often performs more than they feel.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 is wired to notice what's wrong, incomplete, or imprecise; {{B}}'s lead 7 is wired to reframe, skip ahead, and keep energy positive — this collision happens constantly and neither instinct is wrong, which makes it harder to resolve.
- {{B}}'s pace is the single biggest irritant for {{A}}: the 7-led tendency to generate ten half-finished ideas feels irresponsible to a lead 1 who finishes what they start.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 adds an emotional weight and need for depth that {{B}}'s supporting 3 can read as melodrama or inefficiency, creating a subtle but real dismissiveness.
- {{A}} needs time to process and perfect; {{B}} needs momentum and forward motion — scheduling, projects, and decisions will repeatedly expose this fault line.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} frequently reads {{B}}'s enthusiasm as lack of seriousness or intellectual shallowness, when in reality {{B}}'s lead 7 supported by 3 is deeply goal-oriented — they just move toward goals through energy rather than through careful preparation. Conversely, {{B}} reads {{A}}'s critical pauses as pessimism or obstruction, missing that {{A}}'s lead 1 with supporting 5 is not resisting progress but stress-testing it. {{A}}'s supporting 4 makes their corrections feel personal and moral, which lands much harder than {{A}} intends; {{B}} hears judgment where {{A}} means quality control. {{B}}'s supporting 1 occasionally surfaces as sharp criticism, which surprises {{A}} — they expect the 7 energy to be easygoing, and when {{B}} suddenly flips critical it feels hypocritical given how often {{B}} resists {{A}}'s own critiques.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should front-load the acknowledgment of what's working before delivering corrections — the lead 1's internal critic edits out the positive automatically, but {{B}}'s lead 7 needs that recognition to stay receptive.
- {{B}} should signal when they're genuinely committing versus brainstorming; {{A}}'s lead 1 treats every stated idea as a proposal to be evaluated, so {{B}} saying "I'm just thinking out loud" prevents unnecessary friction.
- Both should watch the 1 overlap: when both are in correction mode simultaneously, conversations collapse into competing standards rather than collaborative problem-solving.
- {{A}} can use {{B}}'s 3-supporting drive as a bridge — framing rigorous work in terms of outcomes and results lands better than framing it in terms of correctness.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} genuinely challenges {{A}}'s growth edge: lead 1 moving toward health integrates toward 7, and {{B}} is a living example of enthusiastic engagement with possibility rather than relentless internal auditing. If {{A}} can receive rather than critique {{B}}'s energy, {{B}} functions as a direct invitation into looseness, joy, and trust in process. {{A}} equally challenges {{B}}: 7 moving toward health integrates toward 5, and {{A}}'s deep 5-supported focus models exactly the kind of sustained, substantive attention that {{B}}'s lead 7 habitually escapes. The relationship works best as a slow burn — initial friction is high, but both types carry enough shared 1-integrity and intellectual appetite that genuine respect tends to develop over time, and that respect is a more durable foundation than immediate chemistry.

125-127.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a striking amount of core architecture — both are gut-led by type 1, and both carry the warmth and service orientation of a supporting 2. The real divergence lives in the head center: {{A}}'s supporting 5 pulls toward depth, analysis, and reserve, while {{B}}'s supporting 7 pulls toward enthusiasm, optimism, and expansiveness. This makes them natural allies in values and purpose, but frequent friction partners in method and pacing.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both lead with 1's principled, reform-minded drive — shared ethics and a sense of 'how things should be done right' create immediate mutual respect.
- The supporting 2 in each gives the relationship genuine warmth; both genuinely want to help, teach, and pour into others, which makes them feel seen and appreciated by one another.
- Both are naturally oriented toward mentorship and improvement, meaning their conversations often have a shared sense of purpose and mission.
- When aligned on a cause or project, this pairing can be remarkably effective — {{A}} providing depth and rigor, {{B}} providing energy and vision.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- Two lead 1s in one relationship means two active inner critics and two strong convictions about the 'right' way — disagreements can harden into moral standoffs rather than simple differences of opinion.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 craves thoroughness, privacy, and careful analysis; {{B}}'s supporting 7 craves novelty, momentum, and forward movement — these are genuinely opposing rhythms.
- {{B}} may gloss over problems or reframe difficulties with 7-optimism, which {{A}}'s 5 finds intellectually dishonest or insufficiently rigorous.
- {{A}}'s tendency to withdraw and go quiet (5 influence) can read to {{B}} as withholding or sulking, triggering {{B}}'s 7 impulse to escape tension rather than sit with it.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to interpret {{B}}'s 7-driven enthusiasm as scattered thinking or avoidance of hard truths — from {{A}}'s vantage point, depth is a prerequisite for real understanding, and {{B}} seems to skip steps. {{B}}, meanwhile, experiences {{A}}'s 5-influenced reserve and thoroughness as pessimism or emotional heaviness, not recognizing it as a form of care and rigor. Crucially, both believe they are being principled (via their shared 1 lead), so each can genuinely fail to see why the other's approach isn't working — they mistake a difference in *style* for a difference in *integrity*.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should name their need for processing time explicitly rather than going silent — {{B}}'s 7 fills silence with assumptions and tends to pivot away from unresolved discomfort.
- {{B}} should resist the urge to reframe or silver-lining a concern before {{A}} has finished unpacking it; {{A}}'s 5 needs the problem to be fully articulated before solutions feel credible.
- When disagreeing on standards or methods — which will happen — both should distinguish 'this is a values question' from 'this is a preference question' before engaging, since their shared 1 will otherwise escalate every debate into a moral referendum.
- {{B}} can invite {{A}} into enthusiasm by grounding ideas in evidence; {{A}} can invite {{B}} into depth by framing it as useful rather than heavy.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}} has a genuine developmental invitation from {{B}}: the supporting 7 models that optimism and forward momentum are not intellectual weaknesses, and {{A}}'s lead 1 can become less burdened by learning to hold possibility alongside critique. {{B}}'s invitation from {{A}} is equally real — the supporting 5 models that slowing down, sitting with complexity, and resisting premature resolution is not pessimism but precision. Both grow most, however, through their shared supporting 2: as they each move from helping-as-duty (a 1 pattern) toward helping-as-genuine-care, the relationship deepens from mutual respect into real intimacy.

147-359.summary: {{A}} leads with the gut center's drive for integrity, principle, and improvement, layered with the 4's hunger for authenticity and the 7's expansive idealism — a combination that produces a passionate, exacting, visionary personality. {{B}} leads with the heart center's focus on achievement, image, and results, supported by the 5's analytical detachment and the 9's smoothing conflict-avoidance — producing a capable, adaptive, quietly ambitious presence. These two can genuinely inspire each other, but their deepest values around authenticity, standards, and success are wired differently enough to create real friction.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 and {{B}}'s supporting 5 share a genuine appetite for ideas and competence, giving them an intellectual common ground that energizes conversation.
- Both carry all three centers, making each a well-rounded, capable partner who can respect the other's range.
- {{A}}'s visionary streak (1 + 7 together) resonates with {{B}}'s forward-momentum and goal-orientation — they both want to build something meaningful.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 can soften {{A}}'s sharp edges, creating a rare sense of ease that {{A}}'s inner critic doesn't always allow with others.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 holds rigorous ethical and quality standards — it notices when things are done wrong, and it says so; {{B}}'s lead 3 is wired to adapt presentation and cut efficient paths to success, which reads to {{A}} as corner-cutting or worse, dishonesty.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 craves emotional authenticity and depth; {{B}}'s lead 3 can sidestep genuine vulnerability in favor of a polished, effective persona, leaving {{A}} feeling like they're relating to a performance.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 conflict-avoidance means {{B}} may disengage or smooth over exactly the problems that {{A}}'s 1 insists must be confronted and corrected.
- {{A}}'s 7 can escalate into grandiose idealism; {{B}}'s 3 is results-focused and pragmatic, and will eventually lose patience with what it sees as impractical perfectionism.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s adaptability as inauthenticity or opportunism — the 3's natural image-shifting, which is genuinely strategic rather than deceptive, triggers the 1's moral alarm and the 4's contempt for the superficial.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s criticism and exacting standards as rigidity or self-righteousness — the 3 is oriented toward what works, so moralizing about what's right feels obstructive rather than principled.
- {{A}}'s 4 experiences emotions as meaningful signal and may share depth expecting reciprocity; {{B}}'s 3 tends to process emotion privately or instrumentally, leaving {{A}} feeling unseen.
- {{B}}'s 9 reads {{A}}'s directness as aggression and withdraws; {{A}}'s 1 reads {{B}}'s withdrawal as avoidance of accountability, and the cycle escalates in silence.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should distinguish between critique of an idea and critique of a person — {{B}}'s lead 3 ties identity closely to performance, so blunt correction lands as personal attack even when {{A}} intends it as problem-solving.
- {{B}} should offer {{A}} genuine transparency rather than a curated version of events; {{A}}'s 1 and 4 together have a finely tuned inauthenticity detector, and managing the message will backfire.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 is a real asset here — leading conversations with analysis and curiosity rather than with image-management disarms {{A}}'s critical reflex and opens genuine dialogue.
- {{A}} can leverage the supporting 7's warmth and optimism to frame feedback generatively rather than correctively, which {{B}}'s 3 will receive far better.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 models integrity, follow-through, and a willingness to be unpopular for the sake of what's right — qualities {{B}}'s 3 genuinely needs to develop as it matures beyond image toward authentic identity.
- {{B}}'s lead 3 can pull {{A}} out of paralysis-by-perfectionism, showing that good execution now often beats flawless execution never — a real antidote to the 1's over-idealism.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 offers {{B}} a mirror for emotional depth and self-knowledge that the 3-led system tends to bypass; sustained closeness with {{A}} can quietly become transformative for {{B}}'s inner life.
- If both are willing to stay in discomfort rather than default to their respective defenses — {{A}}'s moral criticism and {{B}}'s strategic withdrawal — this pairing has the potential to sharpen and deepen both people substantially.

712-845.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} form a pairing of high energy and high conviction, but they channel that force from very different centers — {{A}} leads from the head with optimism and people-warmth, while {{B}} leads from the gut with raw power and intensity. Their complementary center coverage (head-led vs. gut-led) gives them real range together, but their contrasting emotional styles — {{A}}'s 2-supported warmth versus {{B}}'s 4-supported hunger for depth — creates persistent friction around how feelings are handled. With mutual respect and honest communication, this pairing can be genuinely galvanizing; without it, {{A}} will feel steamrolled and {{B}} will feel coddled.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 7 brings generative energy and big-picture vision that {{B}}'s 8 finds genuinely exciting and worth backing with force.
- {{B}}'s directness and confidence give {{A}} a grounded partner who won't just validate every idea — the 1 in {{A}} quietly appreciates that honesty.
- Both carry a gut-center type ({{A}}'s supporting 1, {{B}}'s lead 8), giving them a shared language around integrity, standards, and doing things right.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 and {{A}}'s lead 7 meet in the head center — intellectual sparring, shared curiosity, and mutual respect for competence are genuine strengths here.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 7 reflexively reframes pain as possibility and keeps things moving forward; {{B}}'s lead 8 reads this as avoidance and loses trust fast.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 craves emotional authenticity and depth; {{A}}'s 2-colored warmth can feel performed or superficially cheerful to a 4, which is quietly infuriating.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 can slip into moralizing or principled correction; {{B}}'s 8 resists being told what is right with particular stubbornness.
- {{B}}'s 8 controls through confrontation and testing; {{A}}'s 2 responds by over-giving to restore harmony, which {{B}} often interprets as weakness rather than care.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} routinely misreads {{B}}'s directness and confrontational style as hostility or rejection, when {{B}} is simply leading from the gut without the social lubricant {{A}} considers normal.
- {{B}} misreads {{A}}'s enthusiasm and positive framing as shallowness or evasion, missing that the supporting 1 in {{A}} actually holds real moral seriousness beneath the optimism.
- When {{B}}'s supporting 5 pulls back to process internally, {{A}}'s 2 interprets the withdrawal as emotional abandonment and escalates warmth — which feels suffocating to {{B}}.
- {{A}} experiences {{B}}'s 4-driven emotional intensity as destabilizing drama; {{B}} experiences {{A}}'s 7-driven lightness as a refusal to take real things seriously.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should lead with directness rather than enthusiasm when something matters — {{B}}'s 8 responds to clarity and strength, not spin or softening.
- {{B}} should signal when withdrawal is about processing rather than punishment; {{A}}'s 2 cannot distinguish the two without explicit cues.
- {{A}}'s 1 and {{B}}'s 8 share a concern for integrity — anchoring hard conversations to shared values rather than feelings gives both types firmer footing.
- {{B}} should allow {{A}}'s warmth to land rather than immediately testing or challenging it; the 2 in {{A}} extends care genuinely, and reflexive 8 skepticism damages trust over time.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}}'s growth direction from 7 moves toward 5 — depth, focus, and the willingness to sit with difficulty rather than escape it — and {{B}}'s supporting 5 actively models this, making {{B}} a genuine growth edge for {{A}}. Conversely, {{B}}'s growth direction from 8 moves toward 2 — vulnerability, care, and openness to needing others — and {{A}}'s lead 7 paired with supporting 2 creates an environment where that softening is possible if {{B}} trusts it. The risk is that {{A}} takes on too much of {{B}}'s emotional labor through the 2, while {{B}} stays defended behind the 8's self-sufficiency. At their best, {{A}} teaches {{B}} that warmth is not weakness, and {{B}} teaches {{A}} that depth is not danger.

316-827.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both high-energy, action-oriented people who can build impressive things together — but they operate from very different centers of gravity. {{A}} leads from the heart with a 3's drive for achievement and image, kept disciplined by a supporting 1 and cautious by a supporting 6, while {{B}} leads from the gut with an 8's raw assertiveness, softened by a supporting 2 and energized by a supporting 7. This pairing has genuine complementary power, but also real friction between {{A}}'s need for structure and correctness and {{B}}'s expansive, rule-bending presence.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both are fundamentally doers: {{A}}'s lead 3 wants to achieve and {{B}}'s lead 8 wants to dominate the terrain — they naturally respect each other's drive and competence.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 brings relational warmth that {{A}}'s image-conscious 3 genuinely appreciates, and {{A}}'s supporting 6 responds well to {{B}}'s 8 protectiveness and reliability under pressure.
- When a project or challenge demands focus, these two can lock in together with unusual efficiency — {{A}} strategizes and optimizes while {{B}} pushes through obstacles without flinching.
- {{B}}'s supporting 7 can pull {{A}}'s sometimes anxious 6 out of worst-case-scenario thinking and inject genuine momentum into shared endeavors.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 is principled and critical, with a strong sense of the right way to do things — {{B}}'s lead 8 combined with a spontaneous supporting 7 will routinely short-circuit that order, which {{A}} experiences as chaos or disrespect.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 craves predictability and security; {{B}}'s 8/7 combination actively resists constraint and finds overly cautious planning suffocating.
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is polished, strategic, and image-aware — {{B}}'s lead 8 is blunt and unconcerned with presentation, and their unfiltered directness can feel threatening to {{A}}'s carefully maintained image.
- {{B}}'s lead 8 wants full autonomy; {{A}}'s supporting 1 subtly enforces standards and rules, which 8 reads as controlling or preachy.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} often interprets {{B}}'s 8-led bluntness as aggression or dominance plays, when {{B}} is simply operating from gut-level directness without intent to wound.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s 3-led polish and 1-supported correctness as inauthenticity or manipulation — the 8's instinct is that anyone this put-together must be hiding something.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 flags {{B}}'s risk-embracing 7/8 combination as reckless, while {{B}} genuinely cannot understand why {{A}} is cataloguing risks instead of moving.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 wants emotional reciprocity and genuine warmth — but {{A}}'s 3 tends to redirect intimacy into productivity and task accomplishment, leaving {{B}} feeling unseen relationally.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should drop the strategic framing when talking to {{B}} — lead 8 personalities detect spin immediately and lose trust fast; plain, direct language works far better than polished messaging.
- {{B}} should be conscious that {{A}}'s supporting 6 needs enough context and predictability to feel safe — springing big changes or confrontations without warning activates {{A}}'s anxiety loop and shuts communication down.
- {{A}} should name feelings as well as plans; {{B}}'s supporting 2 is listening for emotional honesty, not just competence reports.
- {{B}} should distinguish between challenging {{A}}'s ideas (welcome) and challenging {{A}}'s worth or image (activates 3's shame core and 6's defensiveness) — the tone of pushback matters enormously here.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 8 models a kind of self-trust and unapologetic presence that {{A}}'s 3 genuinely needs — learning to act without audience validation is a major growth edge for {{A}}, and {{B}} embodies it naturally.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 offers {{B}} something genuinely useful: a principled internal compass that {{B}}'s 8/7 combination can bypass in the pursuit of power or pleasure, and the discipline to follow through with integrity.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 can teach {{B}}'s lead 8 that loyalty is built through consistent trustworthiness, not just through strength — a nuance the 8 often overlooks.
- Long-term, this pairing grows most when {{B}} slows down enough to honor structure and {{A}} loosens enough to act before everything is perfectly planned — each holds exactly what the other underuses.

317-927.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a genuine warmth and enthusiasm rooted in their common 7 head type, giving this pairing real social chemistry and a shared love of possibility. But {{A}}'s heart-led drive for achievement and {{B}}'s gut-led need for peace create a fundamental difference in pacing and priority that the pair must navigate consciously. At their best, they balance each other well — {{A}} brings direction and ambition, {{B}} brings grounded acceptance and care.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 7 in both tritypes is the strongest connector: both {{A}} and {{B}} enjoy optimism, expansive ideas, and keeping things energized and forward-moving.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 genuinely wants to help others succeed, which aligns naturally with {{A}}'s lead 3 ambition — {{B}} can be a sincere cheerleader without feeling competitive.
- Socially, this pair tends to be warm and easy together; {{A}}'s polished 3 charm and {{B}}'s 9-led accommodating presence make them comfortable in shared environments.
- When {{A}} has a vision, {{B}}'s 9 flexibility means they rarely push back hard, giving {{A}} a sense of momentum and support.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is oriented around measurable progress and image; {{B}}'s lead 9 is oriented around harmony and inertia — {{A}} may experience {{B}} as frustratingly slow, passive, or underdirected.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 introduces a critical, corrective edge, and 9s are particularly sensitive to feeling judged or evaluated — this combination can quietly erode {{B}}'s comfort in the relationship.
- {{B}}'s tendency to go along rather than voice needs (classic 9 self-erasure amplified by the supporting 2) can frustrate {{A}}'s 3, which actually needs a real counterpart, not just agreement.
- Under stress, {{A}} accelerates and performs harder while {{B}} disengages and numbs — these opposing coping styles can make conflict resolution feel impossible.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s 9-led easygoing pace as a lack of drive or ambition, when in fact {{B}} simply operates from a different motivational center — peace and presence over achievement.
- {{B}} may experience {{A}}'s 3-led goal focus as surface-level or image-obsessed, and may quietly wonder whether {{A}} is connecting authentically or just performing connection.
- {{A}}'s 1 criticism, even when well-intentioned, registers to {{B}} as a fundamental rejection rather than useful feedback — {{B}}'s 9 hears correction as "you are wrong" rather than "I want things to be better."
- {{B}}'s support (from the 2) can feel like enabling or unconditional positive regard to {{A}}'s 3, which may cause {{A}} to subtly undervalue {{B}}'s emotional contributions.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should consciously dial back the supporting 1's evaluative tone — framing observations as preferences rather than corrections will keep {{B}}'s 9 from retreating into silence.
- {{B}} should practice naming desires and opinions directly rather than defaulting to "whatever you think" — {{A}}'s lead 3 actually functions better with a genuine collaborator than a blank agreement.
- Both can leverage the shared 7 to reset after tension: humor, new ideas, and future-oriented conversations are natural repair mechanisms for this pair.
- {{B}} should flag early when feeling steamrolled; waiting until resentment builds leads to the classic 9 explosion that {{A}} won't see coming.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something genuinely valuable: a model of self-directedness and engagement with personal goals, which can help {{B}}'s 9 resist the pull toward self-forgetting and drift.
- {{B}} offers {{A}} an equally important counterweight — the 9's capacity for non-judgmental presence and the 2's genuine warmth can teach {{A}}'s lead 3 that worth is not contingent on performance or output.
- The risk in this dynamic is a slow codependency where {{A}} sets the agenda and {{B}} perpetually accommodates — both parties need to actively resist this groove, as it will ultimately breed resentment in {{B}} and a subtle contempt in {{A}}.
- At their healthiest, {{A}} becomes less driven by external validation and {{B}} becomes more willing to occupy space — this is a pairing that can genuinely grow each person toward their integration points if both remain honest.

528-836.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a hard 8 backbone — directness, a refusal to be pushed around, and a preference for plain talk — but they arrive at that toughness from opposite directions: {{A}} leads with cool, analytical detachment while {{B}} leads with visceral gut-force. This creates a pairing with genuine mutual respect and real productive tension, but also a consistent friction between {{A}}'s need to think first and {{B}}'s drive to act now. The relationship can be powerfully complementary if both learn to honor the other's center, or it can become a quiet standoff between a fortress of intellect and a wall of will.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry 8 energy: {{A}} as a supporting gut type and {{B}} as the lead, meaning neither is easily intimidated by the other's directness or intensity.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 gives them a backbone that most 5s lack, and {{B}} will respect that {{A}} doesn't crumble under pressure or bold opinions.
- {{B}}'s supporting 6 craves trustworthy, reliable people — and {{A}}'s 5-led thoroughness and {{A}}'s supporting 2 care read as genuinely dependable once trust is established.
- Both dislike pretense: {{A}}'s 5 strips away noise to find truth, {{B}}'s 8 has zero patience for dishonesty or hidden agendas, so their conversations tend to be refreshingly unvarnished.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- The most persistent friction is pacing: {{A}}'s lead 5 needs to gather, process, and analyze before acting, while {{B}}'s lead 8 wants a decision and movement *now*, treating deliberation as stalling.
- Power is the other fault line — {{A}} wields knowledge and strategic control as power; {{B}} wields presence, confrontation, and will. Neither yields easily, and standoffs can calcify fast.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 has a performance and results orientation that {{A}}'s 5 may quietly dismiss as image management or superficiality.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 can slip into indirect influence — doing favors, managing the relationship through helpfulness — and {{B}}'s lead 8 is hypersensitive to any whiff of manipulation, which can trigger disproportionate pushback.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- When {{A}} goes quiet to process, {{B}} reads it as withholding, passive resistance, or even contempt — when in reality {{A}}'s 5 lead *requires* internal retreat before engaging.
- When {{B}} confronts directly or escalates in tone, {{A}}'s 5 lead interprets this as an assault on rational space and withdraws further, which {{B}} then reads as emotional stonewalling or cowardice.
- {{B}}'s supporting 6 runs an ongoing background check on loyalty; {{A}}'s 5 expresses trust through consistent behavior, not through vocal reassurance or demonstrations — leaving {{B}}'s 6 perpetually uncertain whether they're truly valued.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 warmth, when it does emerge, can confuse {{B}}, who expects the cool distance of the 5 and may wonder what {{A}} wants in return.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should name the need for processing time explicitly — a short "I need to think before I respond" goes a long way with {{B}}, who respects directness far more than silence.
- {{B}} should separate intensity of feeling from volume of delivery; {{A}}'s 5 lead shuts down under force but engages well with blunt, calm honesty.
- {{A}} can leverage the supporting 2 to initiate warmth and build relational safety with {{B}}, rather than waiting for {{B}}'s 8 to set the emotional tone.
- {{B}} should make loyalty explicit when it's felt — {{A}}'s supporting 6-absent tritype means {{A}} doesn't automatically scan for it, so naming "I've got your back" concretely helps more than {{B}} might expect.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} challenges {{A}} to move from analysis to action: the lead 5's greatest trap is infinite refinement, and {{B}}'s gut-driven momentum is one of the few forces that can break {{A}} out of it.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally valuable: strategic patience. {{B}}'s lead 8 can charge into conflict prematurely, and {{A}}'s 5-led thinking paired with the supporting 8's instinct for leverage can help {{B}} fight smarter, not just harder.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 can gradually soften {{B}}'s harder edges — not by managing {{B}}, but by modeling that vulnerability and care aren't weaknesses, which {{B}}'s growth edge toward 2 genuinely needs.
- At their best, this pairing produces a formidable team: {{A}} provides the map and the strategy, {{B}} provides the will and the force to execute it, and each holds the other accountable in ways few other types could.

317-358.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a dominant type 3 core, making this a high-voltage pairing of two achievement-driven, image-conscious individuals who instinctively respect each other's competence and ambition. The real differentiation comes in how they each support that lead 3 — {{A}} wraps it in 7's enthusiasm and 1's principled idealism, while {{B}} grounds it in 5's analytical depth and 8's raw power. This creates genuine synergy on big goals alongside real friction around pace, method, and who holds the reins.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both lead with type 3, so there's instant mutual respect for results, efficiency, and polished execution — neither has to explain the drive to succeed.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 brings generative energy and optimism that can genuinely excite {{B}}, who can sometimes get locked in analytical loops via the supporting 5.
