- {{A}}'s supporting 1 is the biggest friction point: it introduces internal standards, a critical eye, and a need for things to be done *correctly* — all of which chafe directly against {{B}}'s lead 7, which resists constraint and bristles at being evaluated.
- {{A}} wants to finish things with quality; {{B}} wants to keep options open and move to the next exciting thing, so shared projects can stall in a quiet standoff.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 seeks comfort and avoids confrontation, which can read to {{A}}'s 3 as passivity or lack of commitment — {{A}} interprets low conflict as low investment.
- Over time, {{A}} may feel like they're doing the heavy lifting of execution while {{B}} generates enthusiasm without follow-through.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} reads {{B}}'s lead-7 pivoting and option-keeping as a sign of unreliability or immaturity; {{B}} reads {{A}}'s lead-3 focus and {{A}}'s supporting-1 criticism as rigidity and joylessness.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 smooths over problems to keep the mood light, which {{A}}'s 3 interprets as dishonesty or avoidance — {{A}} wants to fix it, {{B}} wants to move past it.
- Both types run image-management strategies through their shared 3, but {{A}} manages image through competence and achievement while {{B}} manages it through likability and energy; each can misread the other's self-presentation as performance or superficiality.
- {{A}} doesn't realize that {{B}}'s enthusiasm *is* genuine commitment in 7's language; {{B}} doesn't realize that {{A}}'s directness and correction come from care, not superiority.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should flag when the supporting 1's critical voice is active — framing feedback as "here's how we hit the standard we both want" lands better with {{B}} than evaluative language, which triggers {{B}}'s 7 defenses.
- {{B}} should offer concrete follow-through signals to {{A}}'s lead 3 — specific commitments, not just enthusiasm, because {{A}} scores trust by execution, not by energy level.
- Both should watch for the shared 3 tendency to manage perception with each other; the relationship deepens when image-performance is put aside in favor of direct, messy honesty.
- {{B}} should resist the 9 pull to smooth over tension with {{A}} — {{A}}'s 3 and 1 need resolution, not harmony.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 is genuinely good medicine for {{A}}'s achievement-driven lead 3: it models that worth isn't contingent on output, and can help {{A}} decelerate enough to recover from the cost of constant striving.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 offers {{B}} something the lead 7 sorely needs — a principled internal compass and the satisfaction of finishing things with integrity rather than always chasing the next horizon.
- The risk is that growth stalls if {{B}} uses 9's conflict-avoidance to dodge {{A}}'s directness, or if {{A}} uses 1's moral authority to become prescriptive rather than inviting.
- At their best, {{A}} teaches {{B}} that depth and structure are sources of freedom, and {{B}} teaches {{A}} that presence and delight are legitimate goals, not distractions from real work.

216-639.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} form a relationship grounded in shared loyalty and a deep orientation toward commitment, largely because both carry the 6 energy — {{A}} as a supporting type and {{B}} as the lead. However, {{A}} leads from the heart, driven by a need to give and be needed, while {{B}} leads from the head, driven by a need for certainty and safety. This center difference creates both a powerful complementarity and a persistent low-level friction around trust, appreciation, and directness.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 6 influence means both {{A}} and {{B}} prize loyalty, reliability, and showing up consistently — this is the bedrock of any trust they build.
- {{A}}'s warm, attentive 2 lead is genuinely soothing to {{B}}'s lead-6 anxiety; being cared for helps {{B}} feel the world is less threatening.
- {{B}}'s 9 support brings a calming, accommodating quality that allows {{A}} to feel accepted rather than judged, which is rare and nourishing for a 2.
- Both are other-focused in their orientation: {{A}} gives care, {{B}} creates harmony — together they can build an unusually supportive and stable relational environment.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 introduces a moral-standards layer that generates quiet criticism when things don't meet an internal benchmark; {{B}}'s lead-6 is hyper-reactive to perceived judgment and can become defensive or withdrawn.
- {{B}}'s 6 lead means persistent questioning and doubt, which {{A}}'s 2 interprets as ungratefulness or distrust — a wound at the core of what the 2 needs to feel worthwhile.
- {{B}}'s 9 support enables a conflict-avoidant fade when tension rises, which frustrates {{A}}'s 1 that wants issues named and resolved properly.
- {{A}} can unconsciously over-help as a bid for appreciation; {{B}}'s 3 support can perform competence and self-sufficiency, leaving {{A}} feeling unneeded and unseen.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s anxious questioning and worst-case-scenario thinking as a personal vote of no-confidence, when in reality {{B}}'s lead-6 scans for threats as a baseline function — it isn't about {{A}}.
- {{B}} can misread {{A}}'s helping as unconditional, then feel blindsided when {{A}}'s supporting 1 eventually surfaces a correction or complaint — it can seem like the warmth was a setup.
- {{B}}'s 3 support means {{B}} sometimes defaults to presenting a competent, "I've got it handled" front, which {{A}} reads as emotional distance rather than the vulnerability-management it actually is.
- {{A}}'s indirect way of expressing needs — giving more to signal a desire to receive — is invisible to {{B}}'s head-centered, pattern-analytical style that takes things more literally.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should state needs plainly rather than hinting through acts of service; {{B}}'s 6 lead overthinks ambiguity and may never land on the right interpretation without explicit input.
- {{B}} should offer frequent, specific verbal appreciation — {{A}}'s 2 lead runs on acknowledged contribution, and {{B}}'s 3 support tends to forget that emotional receipts matter.
- When {{A}}'s 1 surfaces a grievance, framing it as a shared standard rather than a personal accusation reduces {{B}}'s 6-triggered defensiveness significantly.
- {{B}} should resist the 9-supported habit of going quiet or vague when stressed; {{A}} will fill that silence with worry and over-giving, escalating the cycle.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}} offers {{B}} a lived model of emotional directness and relational warmth that the head-dominant 6 genuinely needs in order to move from anxiety-management toward heart-opening.
- {{B}} offers {{A}} something equally rare: a reflective, questioning mind that can help {{A}}'s 2 pause before self-erasing, and whose 6 loyalty — once earned — is deep and unwavering.
- The friction between {{A}}'s supporting 1 and {{B}}'s lead 6 is actually a site of potential growth: {{A}} learns to hold standards with less rigidity, while {{B}} learns that being held accountable by someone who cares is not the same as being attacked.
- Long-term, this pairing tends to stabilize into something genuinely solid when both learn the difference between care that expects a return ({{A}}'s shadow) and loyalty that withholds full trust ({{B}}'s shadow) — naming those patterns honestly is the key unlock.

216-847.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a high-contrast pairing that can produce deep loyalty and real vitality together, but only after navigating some significant friction rooted in their opposite lead centers. {{A}} leads from the heart — orienting around connection, care, and moral integrity — while {{B}} leads from the gut, orienting around power, autonomy, and raw honesty. The draw between them is real, but so is the risk of one person dominating the relational space while the other quietly seethes.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 offers warmth and genuine attentiveness that {{B}}'s 8, at its best, deeply values once trust is established — 8s are fiercely loyal to those who show up for them.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 and {{A}}'s lead 2 both crave emotional depth and authenticity, giving this pair a shared language around meaning and feeling.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 and {{B}}'s lead 8 both carry a strong sense of justice and dislike hypocrisy — they can align powerfully around shared values or causes.
- {{B}}'s supporting 7 brings energy and spontaneity that {{A}}'s 2 genuinely enjoys, especially when {{A}} has been over-focused on others' needs at the expense of their own fun.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 8 occupies space loudly and instinctively asserts control; {{A}}'s lead 2, while warm, has a quiet expectation of reciprocity that 8's bluntness routinely bypasses without noticing.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 needs reassurance, consistency, and expressed loyalty — {{B}}'s 8 can read this as anxiety or neediness and respond with impatience rather than comfort.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 will criticize when ethics are violated; {{B}}'s lead 8 strongly resists being corrected or moralized at, making these moments flash-points for real conflict.
- {{B}}'s supporting 7 pulls toward freedom and new stimulation, which can feel like avoidance or flakiness to {{A}}'s 6, who is watching for signs of unreliability.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to interpret {{B}}'s directness and forcefulness as aggression or emotional unavailability, when {{B}} is often simply expressing strength as a form of presence, not rejection. Meanwhile, {{B}} may read {{A}}'s consistent giving and caregiving as subtle manipulation — the lead 8's default suspicion of people who seem 'too nice' can make {{A}}'s genuine warmth feel transactional or controlling. {{A}}'s 6 anxiety, when triggered, produces a need to talk things through and seek reassurance; {{B}}'s 8 interprets this as catastrophizing and shuts down rather than engaging. {{B}}'s 4 support brings emotional intensity and a craving to be seen in full complexity, which {{A}} — focused on harmony and the needs of others — may accidentally flatten by trying to soothe rather than witness.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} must lead with directness when expressing a need — {{B}}'s 8 responds to clear, honest asks and tends to disengage from indirect hinting or emotional pressure.
- {{B}} should explicitly name appreciation for {{A}}'s contributions; the 2 in {{A}} can endure a lot without complaint but will eventually withdraw if they feel taken for granted.
- When {{A}}'s 1 surfaces criticism, framing it around shared values rather than personal fault will land better with {{B}}'s 8, who hates being lectured but can respect a principled position.
- {{B}} should resist the impulse to dismiss {{A}}'s 6-driven anxiety as weakness — acknowledging the concern before problem-solving it will de-escalate faster than logic alone.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} has the potential to help {{A}} step out of the self-erasing helper role — the lead 8's refusal to shrink can model for {{A}}'s 2 that taking up space and having needs is not a moral failing. In return, {{A}} can teach {{B}} that vulnerability is not the same as weakness; the 2's warmth and the 6's steadfast loyalty can create the rare safe environment where {{B}}'s 8 actually lets down its guard. {{A}}'s 1 can hold {{B}} accountable in ways that push {{B}} toward genuine integrity rather than just dominance. Over time, if both commit to the friction rather than retreating from it, {{B}}'s 4 and {{A}}'s 2 can produce a relationship of unusual emotional honesty — but it requires {{A}} to stop over-accommodating and {{B}} to stop treating conflict as a power contest.

215-926.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share the 2's orientation toward care and relational warmth, but they channel it from very different centers of gravity — {{A}} leads with an active, directive heart that reaches outward, while {{B}} leads with a gut-driven peacefulness that absorbs and accommodates. This pairing can feel deeply nurturing and mutually devoted at its best, but it carries real risks of codependency, unspoken resentment, and a quiet power imbalance that neither may notice until it has calcified.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the 2's genuine desire to be useful and present for the people they love, creating an immediate felt sense of being cared for on both sides.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 brings intellectual depth and steady knowledge that directly calms {{B}}'s supporting 6 anxiety — {{B}} feels safer knowing {{A}} has thought things through.
- {{B}}'s lead 9 offers {{A}} a rare, judgment-free receiving space; the 9's non-reactive warmth lets {{A}}'s lead 2 give without feeling evaluated or scored.
- Both quietly share an idealism about how relationships and communities should function, even if {{A}}'s supporting 1 makes that explicit and {{B}}'s supporting 2 expresses it through gentle service.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body: {{A}}'s supporting 1 imposes standards — on situations, on quality, on what counts as 'right' — and the 1's inner critic does not stay interior for long. {{B}}'s lead 9 is wired to suppress anger and maintain harmony, so repeated 1-driven corrections from {{A}} will not produce open pushback; they will produce slow withdrawal and invisible resentment. Meanwhile, {{B}}'s 9 inertia frustrates {{A}}'s 2-1 drive: {{A}} wants to act, improve, and help in tangible ways, while {{B}} can defer decisions indefinitely. {{A}} may also feel chronically under-appreciated — the lead 2's core wound — because {{B}}'s 9 expresses gratitude mildly rather than demonstrably.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} frequently mistakes {{B}}'s agreeableness for genuine enthusiasm or full consent; the 9 says yes to keep peace, not always because they mean yes, and {{A}}'s lead 2 is not naturally suspicious of warmth.
- {{B}} hears {{A}}'s 1-flavored feedback as criticism of who they are rather than what they did, triggering the 9's core fear of disconnection and causing them to shut down rather than engage.
- When {{A}}'s supporting 5 needs to withdraw for solitude and processing, {{B}}'s supporting 6 interprets the distance as a signal that something is wrong in the relationship, generating anxiety that {{A}} then finds baffling.
- {{A}} can misread {{B}}'s peaceful silence as contentment, when {{B}} has simply not yet found a low-conflict way to voice a real need.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should treat {{B}}'s expressed opinion as a fragile offering: the 9 rarely volunteers disagreement, so when {{B}} does speak up, {{A}} must resist any impulse to counter or correct immediately.
- {{B}} must practice naming needs and objections while they are still small; the 9's pattern of accumulating unexpressed frustration until it becomes passive stonewalling is the single biggest threat to this pairing.
- {{A}} can use their supporting 5 to ask genuinely curious questions rather than delivering 1-style conclusions — inquiry disarms {{B}}'s conflict-avoidance far more effectively than advocacy.
- {{B}} can help {{A}}'s lead 2 by offering explicit, specific appreciation: the 2's hunger for acknowledgment is real, and vague warmth from a 9 rarely lands with enough weight to satisfy it.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: At their healthiest, this pair offers each other something central to their respective growth paths: {{B}}'s lead 9 models the acceptance and non-striving that {{A}}'s pressured 2-1 combination desperately needs, while {{A}}'s principled 1 and structured 5 give {{B}}'s 9 the external scaffolding that helps it move out of inertia and into purposeful action. The shared 2 energy is a genuine bridge, but it also creates a codependency trap where both orient so completely around the other's needs that neither develops a clear sense of autonomous self. True growth here requires {{A}} to practice receiving without orchestrating, and {{B}} to practice asserting without waiting for perfect safety — two moves that cut against each type's deepest habitual defense.

629-728.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a genuine warmth rooted in their mutual 2 supporting type, making this a pairing that can feel immediately comfortable and caring. However, the lead types — 6's vigilant anxiety-management and 7's optimism-driven escape from anxiety — represent opposite strategies for handling the same head-center energy, which creates both magnetic attraction and real friction. The relationship has strong potential but requires conscious work around security needs and follow-through.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry supporting 2 energy, meaning warmth, generosity, and attunement to others' needs feel natural to both — they'll rarely feel uncared for by each other.
- {{A}}'s loyalty (lead 6) resonates deeply with {{B}}'s relational warmth (supporting 2), and {{B}}'s enthusiasm can genuinely lift {{A}}'s spirits and interrupt anxious loops.
- Socially, both lean toward bringing people together — {{A}} through steady devotion and {{B}} through infectious energy — making them a complementary team in community or collaborative settings.
- The 9 in {{A}} and the 7 in {{B}} share a mutual desire to keep things light and avoid unnecessary heaviness, giving the pair an easy, enjoyable baseline.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 6 craves consistency, commitment, and reassurance; {{B}}'s lead 7 resists being pinned down and can reframe or exit situations that feel too demanding — this is a structural mismatch in how each defines safety.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 brings bluntness and confrontational energy that can activate {{A}}'s 6-anxiety, making {{A}} feel threatened or braced for conflict rather than secure.
- {{A}}'s 9 support type tends to suppress needs and defer, which means resentment can quietly accumulate while {{B}}'s 8 support type may bulldoze past subtle signals entirely.
- {{B}} can experience {{A}}'s vigilance and worst-case thinking as heavy or restrictive, while {{A}} can experience {{B}}'s optimism as irresponsible or even as a refusal to take real risks seriously.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to interpret {{B}}'s shifting plans, enthusiasm pivots, and future-spinning as unreliability or lack of true commitment — but for {{B}}, mental agility is how they stay vital, not a sign of disloyalty.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s risk-scanning and doubt as pessimism or a personal dampener, not recognizing it as due diligence born from the 6's genuine care about what could go wrong for both of them.
- Because both have supporting 2, each may assume the other is fine — both are practiced at putting others first — leading to a dynamic where neither fully voices their own unmet needs.
- {{A}}'s 9 support type smooths over conflict so effectively that {{B}} may genuinely not know when something is wrong, which then surprises {{B}}'s more reactive 8 side when tension finally surfaces.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should resist the 7 impulse to immediately reframe or silver-line {{A}}'s concerns — validation first, optimism second; {{A}} needs to feel heard before they can move forward.
- {{A}} should practice naming needs directly rather than hinting or going quiet (a 9 pattern), especially with {{B}}'s 8 side, which responds far better to clear directness than to subtle cues.
- When making plans or commitments, the pair benefits from concrete language — vague enthusiasm (7) mixed with anxious hopefulness (6) produces misaligned expectations; specificity is an act of care here.
- {{A}} can invite {{B}} into their concern by framing it as 'here's what I need to feel safe enough to say yes' rather than as a list of objections, which makes the 6's caution feel collaborative rather than obstructive.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} is a genuine catalyst for {{A}}'s growth: the 7's courage, forward motion, and trust in positive outcomes can slowly stretch {{A}}'s tolerance for uncertainty and help loosen the 6's grip on worst-case planning.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally valuable — the 6's loyalty, follow-through, and willingness to sit with difficulty models the kind of depth and presence that {{B}}'s growth line toward 5 is calling for.
- The shared 2 energy means both are capable of profound generosity, but growth requires each to turn some of that care inward: {{A}} must learn that self-trust is more reliable than external reassurance, and {{B}} must learn that staying present to discomfort doesn't mean being trapped.
- At their best, this pairing balances adventure with accountability — {{B}} pulls {{A}} toward possibility and {{A}} anchors {{B}} to the relationships and commitments that actually sustain them.

126-629.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a remarkable overlap in their core values — loyalty, duty, and genuine care for others — because both carry 2 and 6 energy in their tritypes. However, {{A}}'s gut-led 1 brings a reforming, standards-driven engine that can collide with {{B}}'s head-led 6 anxiety and the conflict-softening 9 influence in {{B}}'s gut position. This is a pairing with strong relational glue but real friction around criticism, certainty, and how each handles insecurity.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the 2's genuine warmth and desire to show up for the people they love, making the relationship feel safe and mutually nurturing.
- The shared 6 energy means both deeply value loyalty and reliability — {{A}}'s principled consistency is exactly the kind of trustworthy presence {{B}}'s lead 6 hungers for.
- Both are oriented toward responsibility and doing the right thing, so they rarely conflict over core ethics or commitments.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 helps smooth over moments of tension, giving {{A}} the low-conflict relational environment where their 1 can relax slightly.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 carries a sharp internal critic that often externalizes — a tendency to correct, improve, or point out what's wrong — which can feel relentless to {{B}}, whose lead 6 already generates enough inner self-doubt without incoming critique.
- {{B}}'s 6 lead can become suspicious, test loyalty indirectly, or loop in anxious what-if thinking, which {{A}}'s 1 finds irrational and hard to validate patiently.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 creates a tendency to suppress disagreement and go quiet rather than address problems directly, which clashes with {{A}}'s 1-driven need to name and resolve what is wrong.
- Over time, {{A}} may perceive {{B}} as passive or evasive, while {{B}} experiences {{A}} as rigid and judgmental.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s anxiety-driven questioning and hesitation as a lack of decisiveness or conviction, when in reality {{B}}'s lead 6 is running a thorough internal risk-assessment before committing — a sign of seriousness, not weakness. Conversely, {{B}} can misread {{A}}'s direct correction as personal disapproval or a withdrawal of care, when {{A}}'s 1 is simply expressing its core drive to fix what seems broken — it isn't a verdict on {{B}} as a person. {{B}}'s supporting 2 may also read {{A}}'s reserved emotional expression as coldness, while {{A}}'s supporting 2 is genuinely caring but filtered through the 1's restraint and high standards.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should flag the difference between critiquing a situation and critiquing {{B}} as a person — {{B}}'s lead 6 will collapse these unless {{A}} explicitly separates them.
- {{B}} needs to practice naming concerns in real time rather than letting the supporting 9 suppress them until resentment builds; {{A}}'s 1 responds far better to direct honesty than to silence followed by withdrawal.
- {{A}} can offer explicit reassurance when {{B}}'s 6 loops into doubt — not as coddling, but as accurate information that grounds the anxiety.
- {{B}} can acknowledge {{A}}'s high standards as a strength rather than a threat, which disarms the 1's defensive rigidity.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}} is challenged by this relationship to soften the 1's inner critic toward {{B}} and practice receiving anxiety without pathologizing it — the 6's doubt is not a character flaw but a legitimate processing style. {{B}} is challenged to move against the 9's pull toward accommodation and instead trust that honest conflict with {{A}} will not destroy the relationship; {{A}}'s 1 actually respects directness more than it respects appeasement. If both can stay grounded in their shared 2 warmth as a foundation, they can use their differences constructively — {{A}}'s clarity of principle helping {{B}} find firmer footing, and {{B}}'s relational attunement helping {{A}} connect principle to compassion.

146-416.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share the same three Enneagram types — 1, 4, and 6 — and the same archetype label, yet they inhabit fundamentally different experiential worlds because their lead types are swapped. {{A}} is a gut-led perfectionist who feels and questions through a moral framework, while {{B}} is a heart-led individualist who applies standards and anxiety through the lens of identity and emotional authenticity. This pairing has exceptional potential for mutual depth and resonance, but also a specific, recurring friction rooted in the head-heart-gut difference in how identical values get expressed.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the same philosophical triad, meaning genuine shared hunger for meaning, integrity, and emotional depth — conversations rarely stay shallow.
- The supporting 6 in both creates a mutual undercurrent of loyalty and rigorous questioning; neither is naive, and both respect careful thinking.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 and {{B}}'s supporting 1 mean each can genuinely appreciate what the other leads with — {{A}} has felt the pull of emotional authenticity; {{B}} has felt the pull of inner standards.
- There is a rare sense of being truly 'seen' here, because the other person carries all three of your types and understands each from the inside.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 compresses and sublimates anger into correction and critique; {{B}}'s lead 4 amplifies emotional states and holds onto them — this creates a pressure-differential where {{A}} reads {{B}} as melodramatic and {{B}} reads {{A}} as emotionally sealed off.
- {{A}} instinctively moves toward fixing or improving; {{B}} instinctively moves toward being fully felt and acknowledged, and 'fixing' can register as dismissal of the feeling.
- Both have an active inner critic, but {{A}}'s critic is externalized onto standards and behavior while {{B}}'s critic targets identity and worth — during conflict, {{A}} may argue about what was done wrong, while {{B}} experiences that as an attack on who they are.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{B}} is likely to interpret {{A}}'s principled stance as rigidity or emotional unavailability, missing that the supporting 4 in {{A}} is genuinely sensitive — it is simply not in the driver's seat.
- {{A}} is likely to interpret {{B}}'s emotional intensity as irrationality or self-indulgence, missing that the supporting 1 in {{B}} has already applied real moral rigor to arrive at that feeling.
- The shared 6 support means both are prone to anxiety and worst-case thinking, but {{A}}'s anxiety circles around 'am I doing the right thing?' while {{B}}'s circles around 'am I enough / will I be abandoned?' — in stress, each can accidentally confirm the other's deepest fear.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} benefits from naming the emotional need explicitly before {{A}} moves into problem-solving mode; {{A}} genuinely wants to help but defaults to correction, not containment.
- {{A}} benefits from pausing the critique long enough to ask what {{B}} actually needs in the moment — validation and understanding often need to come before any evaluation of right or wrong.
- Both share the 6's habit of anticipatory worry; agreeing to distinguish 'processing fear together' from 'making a decision' can prevent anxious spirals from becoming arguments about who is being more reasonable.
- When the inner critics in both activate during conflict, naming that dynamic out loud ('my critic is running right now') can interrupt the loop before it becomes mutual accusation.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s growth edge — moving from 1 toward 7, loosening rigidity and allowing joy and spontaneity — is something {{B}}'s lead 4 can model, since 4s know how to inhabit experience rather than judge it.
- {{B}}'s growth edge — moving from 4 toward 1, developing discipline and acting from principle rather than mood — is something {{A}}'s lead 1 naturally embodies, offering a living example rather than a lecture.
- The risk is that each tries to 'improve' the other using their own lead type as the standard; the opportunity is that each already carries the other's lead as a supporting type, so growth here is less about learning something foreign and more about trusting what is already inside them.

368-648.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a powerful loyalty-and-confrontation backbone through their common 6 and 8 energies, giving this pairing a natural pull toward joint causes, fierce protectiveness, and frank communication. The real axis of tension runs between {{A}}'s heart-center lead (3) and {{B}}'s head-center lead (6): one optimizes for image and achievement, the other interrogates motives and demands transparency. This is a dynamic, high-energy pairing with genuine chemistry and equally genuine friction around authenticity and trust.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 8 in both tritypes creates immediate mutual respect — neither {{A}} nor {{B}} backs down from confrontation, and both appreciate directness over diplomatic hedging.
- The shared 6 means both carry a deep loyalty instinct and a strong sense of duty to people and principles; when aligned on a cause, they become a formidable team.
- Both archetypes — The Justice Fighter and The Truth-Teller — orbit justice and accountability, so their values naturally converge on what matters most.
- {{A}}'s 3-led drive to accomplish and {{B}}'s 6-led drive to protect create a complementary push: one charges forward, the other holds the ground.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is wired to adapt its presentation for effectiveness — shifting tone, framing wins, managing how it's perceived — and {{B}}'s lead 6 is hardwired to detect exactly this kind of flexibility as a potential red flag for inauthenticity.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 adds a layer of emotional intensity and a hunger for realness that can feel like a constant audit of {{A}}'s motives, which the achievement-oriented 3 finds draining and unfair.
- {{A}}'s 3 wants to move, execute, and close; {{B}}'s 6 wants to stress-test, question, and verify — this creates real pacing friction in joint decisions.
- When stress hits, {{A}}'s 3 can become image-protective and evasive, triggering {{B}}'s worst-case 6 thinking into full suspicion mode.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s 6-led questioning as disloyalty or lack of confidence, when in fact {{B}} interrogates precisely because the stakes of trust feel so high to a loyalty-first type.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s image management and strategic framing as deception, when for a lead 3 this is simply the instinctive language of effectiveness — not manipulation.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 sometimes expresses hurt or disillusionment in emotionally dramatic terms that {{A}}'s pragmatic 3 dismisses as overreaction, causing {{B}} to feel both unseen and judged.
- {{A}}'s 8 assertiveness reads as confidence; {{B}}'s 8 assertiveness can read as aggression to {{A}} when it's paired with 6 anxiety — two different flavors of the same energy that don't always recognize each other.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should proactively share reasoning and behind-the-scenes thinking with {{B}} — the lead 6 doesn't need to be managed, it needs to be included; transparency disarms suspicion faster than any persuasion tactic.
- {{B}} should name the difference between raising a concern and withdrawing trust; {{A}}'s 3 lead will shut down emotionally if it concludes that no amount of achievement will ever be enough to satisfy {{B}}'s scrutiny.
- Both can lean on their shared 8 when things get tense — direct, clean conflict is healthier for this pairing than passive positioning or emotional withdrawal.
- {{A}} should resist the 3 reflex to reframe problems as opportunities when {{B}}'s 4 is expressing genuine pain; sometimes {{B}} needs to be heard before being problem-solved.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 challenges {{B}} to move from anxious vigilance into purposeful action — the 6's growth direction is toward 9's groundedness and ultimately 3's confident forward motion, so {{A}} can model this authentically.
- {{B}}'s lead 6, in turn, calls {{A}} toward the deeper integrity that 3 often bypasses: asking not just 'Am I succeeding?' but 'Is this true?' — a question {{B}}'s 4 makes unavoidable.
- The supporting 4 in {{B}} is the hidden gift for {{A}}: it offers {{A}}'s 3 a mirror for emotional authenticity that the heart center, ironically, often neglects in favor of performance.
- Long-term, this pairing grows strongest when {{A}} learns that vulnerability isn't a liability and {{B}} learns that ambition isn't a disguise — two hard lessons that only consistent mutual trust can teach.

146-638.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both driven by a deep need for integrity, loyalty, and justice, and the shared 6 energy across their tritypes gives them an immediate sense of recognition and mutual trustworthiness. However, {{A}} leads from the gut with a principled, reform-minded 1, while {{B}} leads from the head with an anxiety-scanning, alliance-testing 6 — creating meaningful friction around who gets to be 'right' and how trust is earned. This pairing has real potential for committed, values-aligned partnership, but requires deliberate work around criticism, emotional registers, and the difference between principled correction and relational challenge.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry 6 energy — {{A}} as a supporting head type and {{B}} as the dominant lead — which means loyalty, reliability, and showing up consistently are core values for both.
- {{A}}'s lead 1 and {{B}}'s 8 support share a gut-level outrage at injustice and a drive to act on what's wrong in the world, making the "Justice Fighter" archetype of {{B}} feel like a natural ally to {{A}}'s reformer mission.
- Both tend to be serious, committed, and skeptical of superficiality, which builds a sense of mutual respect quickly.
- When trust is established, the shared 6 foundation creates extraordinary loyalty — these two will show up for each other in concrete, reliable ways.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 externalizes an inner critic — it corrects, refines, and holds people to high standards — which directly triggers {{B}}'s lead 6 anxiety and the defensive force of {{B}}'s 8 support; being corrected can feel like being interrogated or found unworthy.
- {{B}}'s lead 6 tests trust through questions, doubt-voicing, and probing, which {{A}}'s 1 reads as unreliable or evasive — a violation of the principled straightforwardness {{A}} lives by.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 craves emotional depth, authenticity, and being seen as unique, while {{B}}'s supporting 3 pushes toward efficiency, results, and functional presentation — {{A}} may find {{B}} emotionally thin, and {{B}} may find {{A}} unnecessarily brooding.
- Both can dig in hard when they feel their core is threatened: {{A}} behind principle, {{B}} behind alliance and counterforce.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to interpret {{B}}'s anxiety-driven questioning and loyalty-testing as distrust or inconsistency, when it is actually the 6 lead's mechanism for building security — the doubt is the path to commitment, not the absence of it.
- {{B}} tends to interpret {{A}}'s 1-driven correction and standard-setting as moral superiority or rigidity, when {{A}} is genuinely trying to improve what they care about — the critique is an act of investment, not dismissal.
- {{A}}'s 4 support processes emotion through depth and introspection, which {{B}}'s 3 support reads as self-indulgent or stalled; meanwhile {{B}}'s 3-driven pragmatism reads to {{A}}'s 4 as inauthenticity or avoidance of real feeling.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should give {{A}} consistent follow-through on commitments — {{A}}'s supporting 6 notices every gap between stated values and actual behavior, and the lead 1 will name it directly and repeatedly until it's resolved.
- {{A}} should separate feedback from relationship evaluation; when {{A}}'s 1 critiques, {{B}}'s lead 6 hears 'you are not trustworthy,' so framing corrections as shared problem-solving rather than verdicts reduces defensive escalation from {{B}}'s 8 support.
- {{B}} should be allowed to voice doubts and worst-case scenarios without {{A}} shutting it down as catastrophizing — {{A}} can offer calm, grounded reassurance rather than counter-argument, which is what the 6 lead actually needs.
- Both benefit from explicitly naming the values they share before entering disagreement — establishing common ground first anchors the conversation and prevents the spiral into positional conflict.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s 8 support offers {{A}} something genuinely valuable: the gut-level permission to be assertive and confrontational without needing to morally justify every move first, loosening the inner critic's grip on {{A}}'s lead 1.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 can model emotional honesty and individuation for {{B}}, helping {{B}}'s lead 6 distinguish between authentic inner knowing and anxiety-driven reactivity — a crucial distinction the 6 rarely gets direct help with.
- Over time, {{A}}'s principled clarity can give {{B}} a stable moral anchor that reduces 6-style scanning and testing, while {{B}}'s relational warmth and strategic 3 support can help {{A}}'s 1 soften from lone reformer into effective, connected collaborator.
- The growth edge for both is learning that challenge — whether principled correction from {{A}} or loyalty-testing from {{B}} — is an expression of investment rather than threat, which transforms their friction from erosive to generative.

512-738.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both head-center leads, but they use that shared cognitive orientation in nearly opposite ways — {{A}}'s lead 5 drives inward toward depth, precision, and conservation, while {{B}}'s lead 7 drives outward toward expansion, stimulation, and possibility. The pairing has genuine intellectual chemistry and can be mutually stretching, but it is also prone to fundamental mismatches in pace, energy, and emotional style. With self-awareness, the tension between containment and expansion can become the relationship's greatest asset.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both are head-center leads who genuinely enjoy ideas, systems, and competence — conversations can go deep fast.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 brings relational warmth that {{B}}'s high-energy 7 actually finds grounding rather than smothering.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 respects mastery and capability, meaning {{A}}'s depth of knowledge earns real admiration rather than being dismissed.
- Both carry a gut-center type — {{A}} a 1, {{B}} an 8 — giving each a strong inner conviction; they can respect each other's moral seriousness and directness even when they disagree.
- When aligned on a shared goal or project, this pairing is unusually effective: {{A}} builds the framework and {{B}} drives execution with force.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 5 guards energy carefully and needs solitude to recharge; {{B}}'s lead 7 consumes energy outwardly and experiences withdrawal as rejection or dullness.
- {{B}} moves fast, synthesizes broadly, and pivots readily — behaviors that {{A}}'s 5 reads as intellectual shallowness and that {{A}}'s supporting 1 judges as lack of follow-through.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 introduces an inner critic and ethical rigor that chafes against {{B}}'s supporting 8, which bristles at being corrected or constrained by rules it didn't write.
- {{B}} can escalate stimulation and social commitments in ways that feel invasive to {{A}}, who needs a protected inner world to function well.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to interpret {{B}}'s relentless forward motion as avoidance of depth or emotional reality — and is partly right, since 7 does use activity to sidestep pain — but misses that {{B}}'s 3 and 8 together give it genuine drive and strategic intelligence, not just restlessness.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s silence and deliberateness as withholding, cold, or even passive-aggressive, missing that {{A}}'s lead 5 simply needs time to process before speaking and is not stonewalling.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 has genuine relational needs but often expresses them indirectly; {{B}}'s supporting 3 is image-aware and can miss emotional subtext, leaving {{A}} feeling unseen.
- {{B}} may experience {{A}}'s principled 1-supported critiques as personal attacks on its character, when {{A}} is primarily motivated by a shared standard, not dominance.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should state needs directly rather than expecting {{B}} to read subtle withdrawal signals — {{B}}'s 7-lead is genuinely poor at picking up quiet cues and is not being deliberately inattentive.
- {{B}} should build in explicit pauses after raising new ideas, giving {{A}}'s 5 time to analyze before responding; pushing for an immediate reaction will produce a shutdown, not a conversation.
- {{A}} can leverage its supporting 2 to frame concerns warmly before engaging its 1's critical voice — leading with connection rather than correction lands far better with {{B}}'s 8-supported directness.
- {{B}} can use its supporting 3's goal-orientation to find shared objectives, which gives {{A}}'s 5 a logical reason to engage rather than retreat into observation mode.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} challenges {{A}} to move from knowing to doing — the 7's comfort with action and risk can pull {{A}}'s 5 out of indefinite preparation and into actual engagement with the world, and {{B}}'s 8 models a kind of bold presence that {{A}}'s withdrawn 5 genuinely needs to develop. In return, {{A}} offers {{B}} something rare: a person who will not be swept up in the 7's enthusiasm without asking hard questions, and whose supporting 1 holds a consistent ethical standard that {{B}}'s 8 secretly respects even when it resists it. The risk is that {{A}} becomes {{B}}'s internal brake — resented rather than valued — and that {{B}} becomes a source of chronic overstimulation for {{A}}. The relationship grows when both recognize that {{A}}'s depth and {{B}}'s range are incomplete on their own, and that the discomfort each one produces in the other is precisely the growth edge each needs most.

147-358.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both driven, purposeful people who can build something genuinely impressive together — but they operate from fundamentally different moral and motivational engines. {{A}}'s lead 1 is animated by principle and an internal standard of rightness, while {{B}}'s lead 3 is animated by outcomes, image, and achievement. This produces a pairing of complementary ambition that is also a latent site of ongoing friction over integrity, efficiency, and emotional honesty.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both are high-functioning and outcome-oriented; {{A}}'s 1 wants to make things right, {{B}}'s 3 wants to make things work — these vectors often point in the same direction.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 brings visionary enthusiasm that genuinely energizes {{B}}'s lead 3, creating a shared forward momentum and appetite for big ideas.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 and {{A}}'s supporting 4 share a taste for depth and substance, meaning both can move past surface-level conversation when trust is established.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 and {{A}}'s lead 1 both carry strong gut energy, making this a pairing that can act decisively and hold its ground when it matters.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 holds an internal ethical compass and will call out corner-cutting; {{B}}'s lead 3 is pragmatic and image-conscious, and may experience that criticism as an attack on competence rather than a principled concern.
- {{B}}'s 3 suppresses or sidesteps emotion in the name of efficiency, which collides directly with {{A}}'s supporting 4, which needs authenticity and emotional resonance to feel safe in a relationship.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 can become blunt or domineering under pressure, triggering {{A}}'s 1-driven sense of wrongness and escalating into rigid standoffs neither party easily backs down from.
- {{A}}'s 4 can introduce melancholic intensity or a need for creative uniqueness that {{B}}'s results-focused 3 reads as self-indulgent or inefficient.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s adaptability and image-management as a lack of genuine conviction — seeing the 3's shape-shifting as moral flexibility rather than strategic intelligence. Meanwhile, {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s principled critiques as perfectionist obstruction, missing that the lead 1's corrections come from a deeply felt internal standard, not a desire to slow things down. {{A}}'s supporting 4 may express emotional needs in ways that feel abstract or dramatic to {{B}}'s 3, which processes feelings by moving through them quickly toward resolution. {{B}}'s supporting 5 can go cold and analytical during conflict, which {{A}}'s 4 experiences as withdrawal or emotional dismissal, compounding the disconnect.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should frame ethical concerns in terms of shared goals and outcomes rather than leading with what's wrong — {{B}}'s lead 3 hears criticism of process as criticism of self-worth.
- {{B}} should resist the urge to problem-solve {{A}}'s emotional expression immediately; {{A}}'s 4 needs to feel heard before it can move toward solutions.
- {{A}} can acknowledge {{B}}'s genuine competence explicitly — the lead 3 performs better and listens more openly when it feels seen as capable.
- {{B}} should offer transparency about process and reasoning, not just results; {{A}}'s lead 1 trusts the how as much as the what.
- Both should name when they're in reactive mode — {{A}}'s 1 goes rigid and {{B}}'s 8 goes forceful, and recognizing those states early prevents escalation.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} has real potential to help {{A}} loosen the grip of perfectionism — the lead 3's results-orientation and the supporting 8's boldness can show {{A}}'s 1 that effective action sometimes requires accepting good enough over ideal. In the other direction, {{A}}'s principled 1 and emotionally attuned 4 can be a genuine conscience for {{B}}, pulling the lead 3 toward integrity and the kind of authentic depth that 3 often sacrifices for image. The pairing sharpens both people: {{A}} learns to separate moral seriousness from moral rigidity, and {{B}} learns that authenticity is not inefficiency but a foundation for sustainable trust. The shared ambition is real — if they can negotiate the friction honestly, this pairing tends to produce work and connection that neither could generate alone.

479-827.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a striking contrast in centers — one leading from the heart with a deep need for authentic emotional meaning, the other leading from the gut with raw directness and a drive to command their world. Their shared 7 in the head center gives them a genuine spark of enthusiasm and adventurousness that can make early connection feel effortless, but the 4-8 lead pairing creates a fundamental tension between emotional interiority and forceful exteriority that will require real work to navigate. This is a relationship with genuine chemistry and genuine friction in roughly equal measure.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both {{A}} and {{B}} carry a nonconformist streak: {{A}}'s lead 4 insists on uniqueness and authenticity, while {{B}}'s lead 8 refuses to be controlled by convention — together they can feel like co-rebels against a bland or dishonest world.
- The shared 7 is the most immediate bond: both love novelty, humor, and the feeling of being alive, and can easily launch into adventures or big ideas together.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 genuinely wants to protect and cherish the people it loves, and {{A}}'s 4 — which craves being truly seen — can feel unusually held by {{B}}'s fierce loyalty.
- {{A}}'s 9 brings a calming, accommodating quality that can give {{B}}'s 8 the rare experience of not needing to fight for space.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 4 needs sustained emotional depth and time to process; {{B}}'s lead 8 is action-oriented and can read prolonged inner exploration as self-indulgence or stalling.
- {{B}}'s 8 generates and even enjoys direct confrontation, while {{A}}'s supporting 9 instinctively withdraws from conflict — this mismatch can leave {{A}} feeling steamrolled and {{B}} feeling like they're chasing a ghost.
- {{A}}'s 4 is emotionally thin-skinned and attuned to subtleties of tone; {{B}}'s bluntness, though rarely malicious, can land as wounding dismissal.
- When {{A}} goes melancholic and inward — a classic 4 stress pattern — {{B}}'s 8 may escalate pressure to get a reaction, which is precisely the wrong move.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to interpret {{B}}'s directness and boundary-pushing as indifference to their inner world, when in fact {{B}}'s lead 8 expresses care through action and presence, not emotional attunement.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s emotional withdrawal — amplified by the supporting 9 — as passive manipulation or weakness, rather than recognizing it as a genuine need for internal processing.
- {{A}}'s 4 communicates meaning through implication, metaphor, and emotional coloring; {{B}}'s 8 is literal and concrete, so {{A}} often feels unheard even when {{B}} is trying to engage.
- {{B}} may not grasp that {{A}}'s melancholy is not a demand for rescue or a performance — it is simply how the 4 experiences and integrates the world.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the 9's pull toward vague hinting and instead name needs directly — {{B}}'s 8 responds far better to clear, honest requests than to implied emotional cues.
- {{B}} should practice creating a deliberate pause before responding to {{A}}'s emotional content — even a few seconds of acknowledgment before problem-solving signals that {{A}} has been heard.
- Both can use their shared 7 as a reset button: when tension rises, shifting to humor, a shared plan, or something genuinely exciting can reduce defensiveness on both sides.
- {{B}} should be aware that 8-style intensity — raised voice, rapid-fire challenge — triggers {{A}}'s 9 into shutdown, which looks like passivity but is actually overwhelm.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} is a genuine catalyst for {{A}}: the lead 8's willingness to act, confront, and occupy space can push {{A}}'s 4+9 combination out of beautiful but stagnant rumination and into real-world self-assertion.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something rarer and more challenging — an invitation into emotional authenticity and genuine vulnerability, the very terrain {{B}}'s lead 8 is most defended against.
- {{A}}'s 4 models that depth of feeling is not weakness, which can be quietly transformative for an 8 who equates vulnerability with exposure.
- The risk is that {{B}} tries to 'fix' {{A}}'s emotional life rather than witness it, and {{A}} idealizes {{B}}'s strength without ever learning to access their own — so both must resist the pull toward those complementary but limiting roles.

316-612.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share two of three tritype numbers — the 6 and the 1 — but those numbers occupy very different roles in each person's stack, creating a pairing that feels immediately familiar yet subtly misaligned. {{A}}'s lead 3 drives toward performance, results, and image, while {{B}}'s lead 6 is oriented around security, trust-building, and vigilant questioning. Their shared 1 gives them a genuine ethical common ground, but the path each takes to that ground looks quite different.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared gut-center 1 gives both {{A}} and {{B}} a strong inner critic and a desire to do things the right way — they will rarely have to argue about basic standards or ethics.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 creates a real resonance with {{B}}'s lead 6: both understand loyalty, and {{A}} genuinely values reliability in ways that {{B}} can feel and trust over time.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 brings warmth and attentiveness that feeds {{A}}'s 3-driven desire to be seen and appreciated, making {{B}} feel like a natural ally and advocate.
- Both are fundamentally hardworking and responsible — in a shared project or commitment, they will rarely have to chase each other down.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 adapts persona and messaging to achieve results, and {{B}}'s lead 6 is precisely wired to detect inconsistency and inauthenticity — this combination can quietly erode trust even when {{A}} has no deceptive intent.
- {{B}} tends toward worst-case-scenario thinking and can slow decisions down with rounds of questioning; {{A}}'s 3 lead reads this as inefficiency or lack of confidence and may grow visibly impatient.
- {{A}}'s 1 pushes toward correction and optimization; so does {{B}}'s 1 — when both are stressed, this shared critical streak can turn outward at each other, producing a tense, judgmental atmosphere.
- {{B}}'s need for reassurance and emotional safety can feel like a demand on {{A}}, who is more oriented toward producing results than providing ongoing relational comfort.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{B}} can misread {{A}}'s 3-style image management as manipulation or superficiality, when for {{A}} it is simply strategic communication — the lead 3 does not experience adaptability as dishonesty.
- {{A}} tends to misread {{B}}'s vigilance and doubt as pessimism or obstruction, when {{B}}'s lead 6 is genuinely trying to protect the relationship or project by scanning for threats before committing.
- {{A}}'s emotional expressions are often instrumental and brief (a heart-center type in service of goals), while {{B}}'s supporting 2 expects warmth and reciprocal care — {{B}} may feel unseen even when {{A}} thinks they've been perfectly adequate.
- When {{B}} asks probing questions, {{A}} can feel accused or mistrusted; {{B}} is not attacking — they are doing exactly what their lead 6 does to feel safe enough to move forward.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should prioritize consistency over charisma with {{B}} — the lead 6 will trust a reliable track record far more than polished persuasion, so showing up the same way every time matters enormously.
- {{B}} should practice stating concerns once, directly, rather than cycling through anxious what-ifs; {{A}}'s lead 3 needs clear, actionable information and loses patience with spiraling.
- Both can ground tense moments by returning to the shared 1 value set — asking 'what's the right thing to do here?' gives each of them a neutral, principle-based footing that bypasses ego.
- {{A}} should explicitly name appreciation for {{B}}'s loyalty and support; {{B}}'s 2 and 6 together create a deep need to feel trusted and valued, not just used for their reliability.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} something the lead 3 genuinely needs but rarely seeks: a mirror that asks whether the goal being pursued is actually worth the cost, and whether the means are truly honest.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally valuable: the courage to stop analyzing and act, and a model for projecting confidence even when certainty isn't fully there yet.
- Over time, {{A}} can learn from {{B}}'s supporting 2 that genuine connection — not just performance — is what builds lasting loyalty; {{B}} can learn from {{A}}'s lead 3 that visible competence and forward momentum are themselves forms of reassurance.
- The shared 1 is the long-term anchor: when both mature into it, they become mutually accountable in a principled, non-punishing way that makes the relationship genuinely trustworthy for both.

528-549.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share the same lead type — the 5 — which creates an immediate sense of intellectual kinship, mutual respect for privacy, and a shared preference for depth over small talk. However, their supporting types pull them in meaningfully different directions: {{A}}'s 2 and 8 make them more outwardly relational and assertive, while {{B}}'s 4 and 9 make them more inwardly focused and conflict-avoidant. This pairing has genuine connective tissue but requires honest navigation of the tension between {{A}}'s directness and {{B}}'s withdrawal.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both lead with 5, so each respects the other's need for intellectual space, solitude, and competence — there's no pressure to perform or be 'on.'
- Conversations between these two tend to go deep quickly; neither is satisfied with surface-level exchange.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 genuinely wants to understand and help, which can feel quietly nourishing to {{B}}'s sensitive 4 side.
- {{B}}'s 9-grounded calm gives {{A}} — who carries the tension of both 5 and 8 — a rare sense of being met without judgment or competition.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s gut center is 8: blunt, confrontational when pushed, and impatient with avoidance. {{B}}'s gut center is 9: conflict-minimizing, slow to act, and prone to tuning out under pressure. This is the sharpest friction point.
- {{A}}'s 2 has an outward relational pull — it gives and expects connection in return. {{B}}'s 4 is inward and emotionally self-referential, which can read to {{A}} as withholding or ungrateful.
- {{B}} may find {{A}}'s assertive 8 energy overpowering or destabilizing, prompting more withdrawal rather than engagement — which in turn activates {{A}}'s 8 frustration.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} is likely to misread {{B}}'s 9-driven stillness and 4-driven inwardness as passive disinterest or emotional unavailability. From {{A}}'s vantage point — where the 2 reaches out and the 8 acts decisively — {{B}} can look like someone who refuses to show up fully. Meanwhile, {{B}} experiences {{A}}'s 8 directness and 2 expectations as intrusive or demanding, interpreting assertiveness as aggression rather than engagement. Neither correctly reads the other's default mode: {{A}} is not trying to dominate, and {{B}} is not being cold — they simply operate from opposite gut instincts.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should consciously dial back the 8 confrontational edge when {{B}} goes quiet — pushing harder will only deepen {{B}}'s 9 retreat.
- {{B}} should practice naming what they need out loud rather than expecting {{A}}'s 2 to intuit it; the 2 genuinely wants to help but needs a signal.
- Both share a 5 tendency to intellectualize emotion — deliberately distinguishing 'analyzing the feeling' from 'expressing the feeling' will serve this pairing well.
- {{A}} should not weaponize the 2's generosity to manufacture obligation; {{B}}'s 4 will detect inauthenticity immediately and shut down.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: At their best, this pairing is quietly transformative for both. {{A}}'s 8 groundedness and action-orientation can help {{B}} move from contemplation to actualization — a real growth edge for the 549, which tends to ideate without executing. In return, {{B}}'s 4 depth and 9 acceptance can soften {{A}}'s chronic vigilance, showing that not every interaction needs to be strategically managed. The shared 5 core means both genuinely value each other's minds, and when the relationship is secure, that intellectual respect becomes a stable foundation for the emotional risk-taking both types typically avoid.

127-947.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a gut-center dominance and a common 7 thread in the head center, which gives this pairing a surprising amount of instinctive compatibility and mutual enthusiasm. However, {{A}}'s 1-led drive for improvement and correctness will regularly collide with {{B}}'s 9-led need to preserve inner peace and avoid pressure. The relationship can be deeply rewarding, but it requires conscious work on how each person handles tension and unmet needs.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both are gut-led, meaning they share a grounded, instinctive orientation to the world — they often just *feel* what is right without needing to over-explain it.
- The shared 7 in the head center is a real gift: both {{A}} and {{B}} have a thread of optimism, appetite for ideas, and capacity for fun that keeps the relationship energized.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 genuinely loves to care for others, and {{B}}'s lead 9 is naturally warm and receptive — {{A}} will feel good giving, and {{B}} will feel safe receiving.
- 1 and 9 sit adjacent on the enneagram, so there's a native familiarity; {{A}} senses {{B}}'s underlying idealism, and {{B}} appreciates {{A}}'s principled integrity.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 operates with an active inner critic and a strong drive to correct what is wrong; {{B}}'s lead 9 experiences that same energy as pressure and will quietly dig in or check out.
- {{B}}'s 9-led inertia and tendency to defer decisions frustrates {{A}}'s 1, which needs momentum and follow-through to feel at ease.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 brings emotional intensity and a need to feel uniquely seen; {{A}}'s 1 tends to prioritize principle over emotional nuance, which can leave {{B}} feeling flattened.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 needs to feel appreciated and needed; when {{B}}'s 9 goes numb or disengages, {{A}} interprets it as indifference and quietly escalates.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} reads {{B}}'s withdrawal or delay as passive resistance or laziness — in reality, {{B}}'s lead 9 is managing overwhelm and trying to preserve internal equilibrium, not staging a protest.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s directness and corrections as controlling or cold — but {{A}}'s 1 is driven by genuine care for quality and shared standards, not a desire to dominate.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 gives in order to feel needed, and when {{B}}'s 9 doesn't vocalize gratitude or reciprocate explicitly, {{A}} privately concludes the effort doesn't matter.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 wants to be understood in its particularity and depth; {{A}}'s 1-led tendency to move toward solutions and standards can feel to {{B}} like their inner world is being bypassed entirely.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should treat every moment of imperfection as something that doesn't require a correction — {{B}}'s lead 9 is highly sensitive to the *tone* of being evaluated, and repeated critique triggers shutdown, not change.
- {{B}} should practice naming dissatisfaction or needs early, before they harden into passive resentment; {{A}}'s 1 cannot work with a problem it isn't allowed to see.
- Both should lean deliberately into their shared 7 energy — humor, lightness, and shared enthusiasm are genuine de-escalation tools for this pairing, not avoidance.
- When {{B}}'s supporting 4 needs emotional depth, {{A}} will connect best by suspending the urge to fix and simply staying present; {{A}}'s supporting 2 is capable of this, it just has to be allowed to lead.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 9 carries a quality of radical acceptance that is genuinely corrective for {{A}}'s inner critic — being loved without conditions is something {{A}}'s 1 desperately needs and rarely gives itself.
- {{A}}'s lead 1 offers {{B}} something equally valuable: a model of integrity, decisive action, and willingness to confront discomfort — all antidotes to 9's inertia.
- Notably, {{A}}'s stress line points toward 4, which is {{B}}'s own supporting type; this means {{B}} may recognize and hold space for {{A}} at their most reactive or self-critical moments with unusual grace.
- The shared 7 is not just a point of fun — for both types, 7 represents a genuine growth resource, and when this couple builds experiences of shared joy and expansion, it actively pulls both of them toward their healthier edges.

513-514.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a remarkably similar cognitive skeleton — both lead with the 5's drive for mastery and self-sufficiency, and both are anchored by the 1's principled perfectionism in the gut. The decisive divergence lies in the heart center: {{A}}'s supporting 3 pushes toward achievement, efficiency, and visible competence, while {{B}}'s supporting 4 pulls toward depth, authenticity, and personal meaning. This single difference quietly shapes nearly every interaction, creating both genuine intellectual kinship and a persistent undercurrent of mutual misreading.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both lead with type 5, so there is immediate mutual respect for expertise, privacy, and the need to think before speaking.
- The shared supporting 1 gives both a strong sense of standards and a commitment to getting things right, creating a foundation of intellectual integrity.
- Neither person is performatively emotional or socially demanding, so both can coexist comfortably in parallel focus without feeling neglected.
- Deep, topic-driven conversations come naturally; both {{A}} and {{B}} prefer substance over small talk and will readily spend hours in focused exchange.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 is wired for output and forward momentum — it measures value partly through results and recognition, which can make {{B}}'s 4-driven need to linger in meaning feel like stalling.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 needs emotional authenticity and a sense of unique significance; {{A}}'s 3 tends to suppress or reframe feelings in service of efficiency, which reads to {{B}} as emotional flatness or even inauthenticity.
- When the shared 1 activates the inner critic, both can become quietly self-righteous — but from different angles: {{A}} judges by standards of competence and results, {{B}} judges by standards of depth and genuine integrity.
- Neither is naturally expressive, so frustrations accumulate silently rather than being addressed, a risk amplified by two 5 leads who default to withdrawal.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- Because both lead with 5, each assumes the other operates the same way underneath — but {{A}}'s 3 means they are quietly tracking achievement and external validation, while {{B}}'s 4 means they are quietly tracking emotional resonance and personal meaning, two entirely different internal compasses.
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s introspective pauses and focus on significance as self-indulgence or inefficiency, when {{B}} is simply doing necessary meaning-making work.
- {{B}} is likely to read {{A}}'s results-orientation and polished competence as shallowness or image management, when {{A}} is genuinely expressing care through mastery and delivery.
- Both can feel unseen by the other without being able to name exactly why, because the friction is not in the lead type but in the quieter heart-center patterns each carries.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the 3's impulse to pivot quickly to solutions or outputs when {{B}} is processing; {{B}} often needs to articulate meaning before moving forward, and cutting that short creates distance.
- {{B}} should try to translate emotional or existential concerns into concrete language when possible — framing things in terms of integrity or quality (shared 1 language) rather than pure feeling is more likely to land with {{A}}'s 3.
- Both benefit from explicit check-ins, since two 5 leads can drift into extended parallel silence and mistake it for connection when one or both is actually withdrawn.
- Leverage the shared 1: agreeing on shared standards or principles provides neutral, intellectually safe ground when heart-level communication stalls.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 can genuinely expand {{A}}'s emotional range, pushing the 3's tendency to conflate self-worth with output and inviting {{A}} toward the kind of authentic self-knowledge that lies beyond achievement metrics.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 offers {{B}} something real in return: the capacity to take rich inner material and give it form, direction, and impact in the world, countering the 4's pull toward unfinished depth.
- The shared 5 lead means both are capable of accepting feedback delivered with precision and evidence rather than emotion, which makes genuine growth conversations possible if both commit to directness.
- Long-term, this pairing can develop into a quietly powerful intellectual and creative partnership — provided both resist the twin temptations of the 5: retreating into private worlds and expecting the other to intuit what was never said.

269-714.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} form a warm but asymmetrical pairing — {{A}}'s lead 2 is oriented toward deep relational care and security, while {{B}}'s lead 7 is oriented toward expansive experience and forward momentum. There is genuine chemistry in the early stages, as {{A}}'s attentiveness feels nourishing to {{B}}, and {{B}}'s energy and optimism can pull {{A}} out of anxious over-giving. The lasting challenge is that {{A}} needs emotional reciprocity and consistency, while {{B}} is wired to keep moving — which can leave both feeling subtly unseen over time.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 is naturally attuned to what others need, which {{B}}'s supporting 4 quietly craves — a sense of being truly seen and valued as an individual.
- {{B}}'s enthusiasm and warmth are easy for {{A}}'s harmony-seeking 9 to enjoy; there is little friction in casual, positive interactions.
- Both carry a genuine generosity — {{A}} gives emotionally and practically, {{B}} gives through ideas, invitations, and inspiration.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 adds an idealistic streak that resonates with {{A}}'s 6-driven desire for something trustworthy and principled to believe in.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:

- {{A}}'s lead 2 eventually needs reciprocal care — when {{B}}'s 7 glosses over emotional heaviness to stay in forward motion, {{A}} can slip into quiet resentment.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 can be sharply critical, and {{A}}'s 2 is particularly vulnerable to criticism from those it gives to, making these moments disproportionately wounding.
- {{A}}'s 9 avoids conflict while {{B}}'s 7 avoids depth — together they can easily collude to keep things pleasant on the surface while real tensions accumulate.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:

- {{B}} may read {{A}}'s emotional needs or gentle hints as neediness or a guilt-trip, not recognizing this as the shadow side of 2's giving style.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should state needs directly and early rather than relying on hints or hoping {{B}}'s 7 will intuit them; {{B}}'s head center scans for ideas, not unspoken feelings.
- {{B}} should build small, consistent follow-through habits with {{A}} — these matter far more to {{A}}'s 6 than grand gestures, and trust is built in the mundane details.

- {{A}} benefits from naming resentment before it compounds — the 2+9 combination tends to swallow frustration until it erupts, which shocks {{B}}'s 7, who thought everything was fine.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} a genuine invitation to pursue personal joy, curiosity, and self-interest rather than always subordinating those to others' needs — {{A}}'s 2 grows by learning that desire is not selfishness.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} a model of emotional constancy and relational depth; {{B}}'s 7 grows by staying present with discomfort rather than reframing or escaping it, and {{A}}'s steady warmth makes that feel safe enough to try.
- The pairing carries real risk if {{A}} becomes the emotional engine of the relationship while {{B}} enjoys the ride — growth requires {{B}} to consciously invest emotional labor, not just enthusiasm.
- At their best, {{A}}'s grounded care and {{B}}'s expansive vision complement each other beautifully: {{A}} deepens and anchors, {{B}} opens and energizes, and both are pulled toward a fuller version of themselves.

638-826.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a striking overlap — both carry 6 and 8 energy — but occupy those numbers from opposite positions of power. {{A}} leads with head-center anxiety and loyalty, supported by 8's forcefulness; {{B}} leads with gut-center dominance and protection, modulated by a supporting 6's concern for trust. This creates a pairing of immense shared values but fundamentally different rhythms: {{A}} thinks before acting, {{B}} acts before thinking.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry 6 and 8, meaning loyalty, protection, and directness are shared core values — neither has to explain why betrayal is a cardinal sin.
- {{A}}'s lead 6 and {{B}}'s supporting 6 create genuine common ground around skepticism of authority and a deep need for trustworthy alliances.
- {{B}}'s lead 8 and {{A}}'s supporting 8 mean both can handle confrontation without shutting down — real disagreements can be aired rather than buried.
- There is a natural 'us against the world' bond here; when externally threatened, these two cohere fast and fight hard on each other's behalf.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body: {{A}}'s lead 6 produces deliberation, second-guessing, and a constant need to verify safety before committing — behaviors that {{B}}'s lead 8 reads as hesitation or weakness. {{B}} makes bold, instinct-driven moves and expects others to keep pace; {{A}} wants more information, more consensus, more time. {{A}}'s supporting 3 adds a layer of image-management and strategic positioning that can feel slippery to {{B}}, who prizes raw directness. Meanwhile, {{B}}'s lead 8 tendency toward control and dominance can trigger {{A}}'s 6-driven suspicion — the very loyalty {{A}} prizes makes them hypersensitive to power imbalances.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} often reads {{B}}'s bluntness and decisiveness as aggression or a bid for control, when {{B}} is usually just leading from the gut with no manipulative intent.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s questioning and need for reassurance as disloyalty or a lack of confidence, missing that for lead-6 types, rigorous scrutiny *is* how trust is built.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 generates a quiet expectation of appreciation and emotional reciprocity for protection given; {{A}}'s head-led processing can look like emotional unavailability even when it isn't.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 can make {{A}} appear to shift stances based on audience, which {{B}} — valuing gut-honest directness — may flag as inauthenticity.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should offer transparency about reasoning, not just outcomes — {{A}}'s lead 6 needs to understand the 'why' behind a decision to feel safe rather than managed.
- {{A}} should give {{B}} unambiguous, direct signals of trust; 8-led types experience roundabout reassurance as noise, but a clear 'I'm with you' lands immediately.
- Both should name the shared loyalty value explicitly during conflict — it is their genuine anchor and can de-escalate fast.
- {{A}} can frame important asks in terms of goals and outcomes (activating {{A}}'s own 3 support and {{B}}'s action bias) rather than lengthy risk analysis that loses {{B}}'s attention.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} offers {{A}} a powerful model of moving from anxiety into action — the lead-8 willingness to trust instinct and project strength can gradually help {{A}}'s 6 loosen its grip on worst-case thinking. In return, {{A}} offers {{B}} something genuinely rare for lead-8 types: a loyal, rigorous voice that will actually push back, ask hard questions, and stress-test plans before commitment — which is exactly the caution {{B}}'s gut-first style can miss. {{B}}'s supporting 2 has genuine warmth to offer {{A}}, and when that care lands, it directly soothes {{A}}'s core 6 fear of being abandoned or unsupported. The growth ceiling for this pairing is high if trust is established — two people who share both loyalty and force, but temper each other's respective blind spots of anxiety and impulsivity.

127-317.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share every number in their tritypes — 1, 2/3, and 7 — yet the lead-type difference is significant: {{A}} is anchored in gut-center idealism and moral principle, while {{B}} is anchored in heart-center achievement and image. This creates a pairing with genuine overlap in energy and ambition but real friction around integrity vs. pragmatism, and warmth vs. performance.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 7 in the head center gives both {{A}} and {{B}} an optimistic, idea-generating, forward-moving energy — conversations are rarely boring and planning together feels natural.
- Both carry the 1's drive for quality and high standards, so they respect each other's commitment to doing things well rather than just doing them fast.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 and {{B}}'s lead 3 both orient toward people — one through genuine care, the other through skilled attunement — making them socially effective as a team.
- They share a results-oriented ambition that lets them collaborate on projects with real momentum.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
