- Both carry 8 gut energy, which means that when tension does surface it can escalate into a battle of wills — two people accustomed to controlling their environment colliding head-on.
- {{B}} may experience {{A}}'s 2-driven helpfulness as subtly manipulative (giving in order to create obligation), while {{A}} may experience {{B}}'s 3-driven efficiency as cold or self-serving.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to interpret {{B}}'s achievement focus as superficiality or image management, missing that {{B}}'s 3 genuinely equates competence with worth — it is not performance for its own sake but a deeply held identity.
- {{B}} tends to misread {{A}}'s relational warmth and attentiveness as a form of soft manipulation, because the 5+2 combination can look like strategic ingratiation to a 5+3 who maps relationships onto utility.
- Crucially, both lead with 5's withdrawal reflex under stress, meaning neither is likely to name what is actually wrong — they will retreat into analysis or busyness, leaving the relational static unaddressed and growing.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- Lean into the shared 8 channel first: direct, honest, non-apologetic statements land better for both than hints or passive emotional signals.
- {{A}} should name relational needs explicitly rather than signaling them through acts of helpfulness and waiting for reciprocity that {{B}}'s 3 may never think to provide unprompted.
- {{B}} should periodically step outside the task frame and ask how {{A}} is doing relationally — not as a checkbox but as a genuine pause, since {{A}}'s 2 will disengage quietly if it feels invisible.
- When conflict escalates via the shared 8, agree in advance on a de-escalation signal; both are capable of shutting down or doubling down, and neither naturally backs off first.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} a useful mirror for the shadow side of the supporting 2: {{B}}'s 3 can help {{A}} see when helpfulness has become a strategy for feeling indispensable rather than an expression of genuine care.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally valuable — the 2's relational attunement can model that connection and loyalty are worth cultivating for their own sake, not just as leverage for success.
- Both can push each other past the 5's hoarding tendency: {{A}}'s 2 nudges {{B}} toward authentic generosity, and {{B}}'s 3 nudges {{A}} to make competence visible and actionable rather than stored internally.
- The relationship grows strongest when both stop competing on the 5+8 axis (who is smarter, tougher, more in control) and allow the heart-center difference to be a genuine complement rather than a source of suspicion.

713-847.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a common 7 thread that generates real chemistry — both crave boldness, momentum, and big-picture thinking. But their lead types diverge sharply: {{A}}'s lead 7 pilots from the head, staying optimistic and future-focused, while {{B}}'s lead 8 pilots from the gut, pushing hard for control and raw truth. This pairing has genuine spark but requires both people to stretch past their default defenses to reach real depth.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 7 energy is a genuine bond: both {{A}} and {{B}} are drawn to adventure, expansive ideas, and refusing to be boxed in.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 and {{B}}'s lead 8 both orient toward achievement and winning — they can be a formidable team with shared ambitions.
- Neither person defaults to passivity; {{A}}'s enthusiasm and {{B}}'s force create a high-energy, action-oriented dynamic that rarely stalls.
- Both distrust excessive sentimentality, which means they can move fast without getting bogged down in emotional processing.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 7 instinctively reframes pain and keeps things light; {{B}}'s lead 8 reads this as evasion and finds it infuriating — 8s need to know where people really stand.
- {{B}}'s blunt confrontational style can feel like an assault to {{A}}'s 7, who prefers to sidestep direct conflict in favor of options and reframing.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 brings principled, sometimes moralizing energy; {{B}}'s 8 deeply resists being corrected or lectured, making this a recurring flashpoint.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 craves emotional authenticity and depth, which {{A}}'s 7-led structure tends to deflect through humor or future-planning.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s intensity as aggression or a power grab, when for {{B}}'s lead 8 it is simply honest, unfiltered presence. Conversely, {{B}} reads {{A}}'s positivity and reframing as superficiality or a lack of substance, when it is actually {{A}}'s genuine head-center processing style. {{B}}'s supporting 4 may feel they never fully reach {{A}} emotionally — that {{A}} is always just out of reach behind an optimistic veneer — while {{A}} may feel {{B}} is trying to dominate rather than connect. {{A}}'s supporting 1 can come across as rigidly moralistic to {{B}}, who interprets rule-enforcement as a challenge to their autonomy rather than a principled standard.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the 7 habit of deflecting with humor or pivoting to possibilities when {{B}} raises something uncomfortable — {{B}} needs to feel met directly.
- {{B}} should distinguish between directness (useful) and domination (destabilizing) — {{A}}'s supporting 1 will dig in defensively if it feels steamrolled rather than challenged fairly.
- When {{B}}'s supporting 4 surfaces and seeks real emotional exchange, {{A}} can honor this by pausing the optimism and saying something true rather than something energizing.
- {{A}} can name their reasoning process explicitly — this satisfies both {{B}}'s 8 need for transparency and {{B}}'s 7 appreciation for ideas.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} is genuinely positioned to push {{A}} toward the 7's growth edge: facing uncomfortable truths rather than reframing around them, and developing more depth and follow-through (echoing 7's integration line toward 5). {{A}} meanwhile can help {{B}} access the 8's integration line toward 2 — modeling openness, enthusiasm, and trust that the world doesn't always require a defensive posture. The risk in this pairing is collusion: {{A}}'s 7 and {{B}}'s shared 7 support can keep things perpetually exciting and forward-moving while both avoid the vulnerable inner work their heart types (3 and 4 respectively) are calling for. When both commit to not using momentum as escape, this pairing has real transformative potential.

317-528.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both high-competence, results-oriented people who approach the world through radically different primary lenses — {{A}} leads with heart-driven achievement and image, while {{B}} leads with head-driven analysis and autonomy. This creates a dynamic that is intellectually stimulating and productively complementary at its best, but prone to mutual misreading of motive and style when under stress. The pairing works when both respect each other's distinct intelligence rather than competing for whose mode of mastery is 'correct.'

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both {{A}} and {{B}} are fundamentally builders — {{A}}'s lead 3 drives toward visible, effective systems, and {{B}}'s lead 5 with supporting 8 drives toward mastery and structural power, so they naturally align around ambitious, complex goals.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 and {{B}}'s lead 5 can spark genuine intellectual energy: the 7 brings generative ideation and the 5 brings rigorous depth, making them effective thought partners.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 respects strength and directness, which {{A}}'s lead 3 and supporting 1 both project through competence and ethical conviction.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2, though not dominant, can quietly appreciate {{A}}'s social fluency and drive to perform for others — the 2 understands wanting to matter to people, even if the 5 lead keeps that need muted.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is image-aware and strategically adaptable in social contexts; {{B}}'s lead 5 tends to find this kind of social shaping superficial or even suspect, creating quiet friction around authenticity.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 wants momentum, positivity, and forward motion, while {{B}}'s lead 5 insists on thorough analysis before acting — these pacing styles clash repeatedly.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 carries strong convictions about the right way to do things; {{B}}'s supporting 8 resists being directed or corrected, even when the critique is valid.
- {{B}}'s 5 lead guards energy and information carefully, which can feel withholding to {{A}}, who expects visible investment and engagement from collaborators.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s detachment and silence as lack of interest, disengagement, or passive power plays — when in reality {{B}}'s lead 5 is simply processing internally and conserving cognitive resources, not withdrawing relationally. Conversely, {{B}} tends to interpret {{A}}'s lead 3 adaptability — shifting tone, adjusting the pitch, optimizing presentation — as inauthenticity or manipulation, missing that for {{A}} this is genuine competence, not deception. {{A}}'s supporting 7 has a habit of reframing problems optimistically and pivoting quickly, which {{B}}'s 5 reads as intellectual shallowness or avoidance of hard truths. {{B}}'s supporting 2, when it does surface, may offer help in ways that feel subtly controlling to {{A}}'s 1, which has its own standards and resists being managed.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist filling {{B}}'s silences with enthusiasm or reassurance — give the lead 5 time to formulate, and treat that pause as engagement, not absence.
- {{B}} should recognize that {{A}}'s polished presentation is a form of respect and care, not a mask — probing for 'what {{A}} really thinks' will land better than treating their competence as a performance to see through.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 gives them genuine precision and principle; leading with that in conversation with {{B}} — rather than the 3's goal-framing — will earn more trust from the 5 and 8.
- {{B}} should be direct when they need space or disagree, because {{A}}'s lead 3 is highly attuned to vague social signals and will misread ambiguity as disapproval, triggering defensive image-management.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} offers {{A}} something genuinely difficult for a lead 3 to access: the discipline to stop performing and actually sit with incomplete knowledge, making {{A}} more rigorous and less reactive to external validation. {{A}} offers {{B}} the skill of translating deep analysis into real-world impact and human resonance — something the lead 5 genuinely needs but rarely asks for. Worth noting: under stress, 3 moves toward 9's disengagement and 5 moves toward 7's scattered avoidance — in a dysfunctional moment, both can simultaneously check out in different ways, making conflict invisible but unresolved. At their best, {{A}}'s systemic drive and {{B}}'s strategic depth combine into something neither could build alone: rigorous, effective, and actually implemented.

279-469.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both heart-centered leads sharing a gut support in 9, which creates a warm, emotionally attuned bond with a genuine appetite for peace and connection. However, the 2-lead's outward, giving orientation collides in meaningful ways with the 4-lead's inward, identity-focused hunger — one reaches toward others to feel loved, the other withdraws into depth to feel real. This pairing has real potential for intimacy, but requires honest work around emotional bypassing, unspoken needs, and the distinct ways each person experiences feeling unseen.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both lead from the heart center, so emotional attunement is nearly immediate — this pair tends to feel each other quickly and deeply.
- The shared 9 in the gut gives both {{A}} and {{B}} a genuine orientation toward harmony, making the relationship feel safe and low-conflict on the surface.
- {{B}}'s 4 craves being truly known; {{A}}'s 2 genuinely delights in knowing others intimately — this is a rare and nourishing match of supply and need.
- Both types care about authentic relating over superficiality, even if they approach that authenticity differently.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 tends to reframe, uplift, and move past difficult emotions — exactly the kind of emotional bypassing that {{B}}'s lead 4 finds maddening and inauthentic.
- {{A}}'s lead 2 needs to feel needed and appreciated, which can tip into subtle demands for positive feedback; {{B}}'s 4 will resist performing gratitude they don't authentically feel.
- {{B}}'s 6 support introduces anxiety-driven testing and skepticism about others' motives — {{A}}'s 2, already prone to people-pleasing, may exhaust themselves trying to constantly reassure {{B}}.
- Both share a 9 gut, meaning neither is naturally confrontational; unresolved resentments from both sides can quietly accumulate into a significant distance.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} often reads {{B}}'s emotional withdrawal as rejection or ingratitude, not understanding that the 4's inward turning is a search for self, not a verdict on the relationship. {{B}}, in turn, reads {{A}}'s cheerful helpfulness as deflection or even manipulation — the 4 suspects that people who give so freely must want something in return, or are avoiding something real. {{A}}'s 2 genuinely believes they are being open and loving; {{B}}'s 4 experiences that same openness as surface-level until {{A}} shows willingness to sit with darkness rather than fix it. Neither fully trusts that the other is telling the complete emotional truth.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the 2-and-7 impulse to problem-solve or reframe when {{B}} expresses pain — {{B}}'s 4 needs the feeling witnessed first, not redirected.
- {{B}} should name their withdrawals explicitly rather than going silent; {{A}}'s 2 will spiral into anxious over-giving when left without a signal.
- When {{B}}'s 6 support activates doubt or suspicion, a direct question works far better than an indirect test — {{A}}'s 2 is actually quite responsive to explicit requests.
- {{A}} should practice stating their own needs plainly rather than hinting through over-service; {{B}} respects directness and will feel more trust when {{A}} drops the helper mask briefly.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} offers {{A}} something genuinely rare: a relationship that will not be satisfied by {{A}}'s service, forcing the lead 2 to confront what they actually want and feel outside of their helper role. {{A}} offers {{B}} a model of other-orientation — gently challenging the 4's tendency to make everything a story about the self, and demonstrating that connection doesn't require suffering as proof of depth. The shared 9 support means both can learn to use their capacity for peace not as avoidance but as a genuine container for hard conversations. If {{A}} grows toward 4 (their stress line) with curiosity rather than fear, and {{B}} integrates 1 and 2 on their growth path, this pairing can become unusually honest and mutually transformative.

316-648.summary: {{A}} leads with the 3's drive to achieve, project competence, and adapt to succeed, backed by the 6's loyalty and the 1's exacting standards. {{B}} leads with the 6's vigilant, trust-testing loyalty, deepened by the 4's emotional authenticity and the 8's blunt confrontational edge. These two can form a highly committed, productive pairing, but the 3's image management will repeatedly collide with the 6's built-in lie detector, making trust the central — and non-negotiable — currency of this relationship.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry 6 energy — {{A}} as a supporting type and {{B}} as the lead — which means loyalty, reliability, and follow-through are genuinely shared values rather than just talked about.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 and {{B}}'s lead 6 both hold a strong internal sense of 'how things should be done,' creating natural alignment around diligence and standards.
- {{B}}'s 8 support respects competence and results, and {{A}}'s lead 3 delivers exactly that, earning real (not just superficial) regard from {{B}}.
- When trust is established, this pair can be a formidable team — {{A}} drives momentum and {{B}} stress-tests the plan for blind spots.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is a natural shape-shifter, adapting presentation to the audience to maximize success; {{B}}'s lead 6 reads this as potential inauthenticity and grows suspicious, triggering a vigilance loop that {{A}} finds exhausting and unfair.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 will confront {{A}} bluntly when something feels off, and {{A}}'s 3 — wired to protect its image and avoid the shame of being 'found out' — can become defensive or evasive, which only deepens {{B}}'s distrust.
- {{A}}'s 1 support produces sharp inner criticism that can externalize as judgment; {{B}}'s 4 support craves emotional recognition, not critique, so {{A}} can accidentally make {{B}} feel unseen or evaluated rather than valued.
- The pace mismatch is real: {{A}}'s 3 wants to move, execute, and adapt; {{B}}'s 6 wants to slow down, verify, and feel safe before committing.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s questioning and skepticism as disloyalty or as a personal attack on their competence, when {{B}} is actually running standard 6-lead security checks that apply to everyone they care about.
- {{B}} interprets {{A}}'s polish and goal-focus as emotional unavailability or as proof that {{A}} only values outcomes over people, missing that the supporting 6 in {{A}} genuinely wants to be a dependable partner — it just expresses through delivery rather than vulnerability.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 needs to feel that its inner world is seen as unique and meaningful; {{A}}'s 3, wired for efficiency and results, may breeze past those emotional cues entirely, leaving {{B}} feeling reduced to a function in {{A}}'s plan.
- {{A}} may read {{B}}'s 8-fueled bluntness as aggression and pull back behind a polished mask, which {{B}} then reads as confirmation that {{A}} is hiding something.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should practice dropping the performance layer earlier rather than later — {{B}}'s lead 6 will eventually probe for what's underneath, and voluntary transparency builds far more trust than information revealed under pressure.
- {{B}} should name the 6-lead anxiety explicitly ('I'm stress-testing this, not attacking you') rather than letting suspicion come out as interrogation or provocation, which triggers {{A}}'s defensive 3.

- {{B}} should channel the 8 support's directness toward clear, specific concerns rather than broad challenges to {{A}}'s character, which hits the 3's shame core and shuts down real dialogue.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} invites {{A}} to distinguish between authentic achievement and performed success — the 6's refusal to simply accept the 3's image at face value, though uncomfortable, pushes {{A}} toward the 3's genuine growth edge: being valued for who they are, not just what they produce.
- {{A}} invites {{B}} to trust that competence and follow-through are themselves a form of care — the 3's consistent delivery can, over time, provide the 6 exactly the safety evidence it needs to relax its vigilance.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 models emotional depth that {{A}}'s heart-center 3 is paradoxically disconnected from; in a healthy version of this relationship, {{A}} slowly learns to access feeling rather than just performing it.
- This pairing tends to grow through friction rather than comfort — if both commit to the discomfort of being genuinely seen, the shared 6 loyalty holds it together long enough for real transformation to occur.

137-612.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a core thread of 1 energy — both carry a deep commitment to integrity and doing things right — but they approach the world from fundamentally different command centers: {{A}} leads with gut-level certainty and principled drive, while {{B}} leads with head-center vigilance and relational loyalty. This pairing can be genuinely complementary, but it asks both people to tolerate the other's very different relationship to doubt, speed, and emotional warmth. The shared 1 foundation gives them a real meeting point; the lead-type gap is where real work is required.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 1 in both tritypes creates an immediate ethical resonance — both {{A}} and {{B}} care about doing things correctly, keeping commitments, and having integrity, which builds a durable foundation of mutual respect.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 brings genuine warmth toward {{A}}, and {{A}}'s supporting 3 responds well to feeling appreciated and seen — this creates a functional loop of effort and recognition.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 can offer {{B}} an energizing sense of possibility, and {{B}}'s lead-6 loyalty offers {{A}} the reliable, trustworthy partner their 1 deeply values.
- When aligned on a shared mission or project, these two can be highly productive: {{A}} brings structure and optimism, {{B}} brings thorough risk-assessment and relational care.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 operates from a place of inner conviction — when {{A}} has determined what's right, the path is clear. {{B}}'s lead 6 operates from active doubt and needs to test, question, and verify before committing, which {{A}} can experience as foot-dragging or lack of resolve.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 is future-oriented and optimism-seeking, while {{B}}'s lead 6 is wired to anticipate what could go wrong — these two orientations can clash badly in planning or crisis situations.
- {{B}} may also experience {{A}}'s 3 efficiency drive as cold or impersonal, especially when {{B}}'s 2 support is craving emotional acknowledgment before moving on to the next task.
- {{A}}'s 1 can become subtly critical when standards aren't met; {{B}}'s 6 can become reactive or suspicious when it senses judgment, creating an escalation cycle neither fully understands.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s 6-driven questioning as disloyalty, indecisiveness, or lack of confidence — when in fact it is {{B}}'s primary way of building genuine trust and safety before committing fully.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s 1-driven certainty as arrogance or closed-mindedness — when it is actually {{A}}'s sincere effort to anchor to clear principles rather than dismiss {{B}}'s concerns.
- {{A}}'s 7 reframe ("let's focus on the upside") is genuinely meant to be helpful, but {{B}}'s 6 often hears it as minimization of real risk, which triggers more anxiety rather than less.
- {{B}}'s 2 support expresses care through attentiveness and checking in, but {{A}}'s 1 lead can interpret this as hovering or lack of trust in {{A}}'s competence.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the urge to resolve {{B}}'s concerns quickly with optimism or corrective logic; {{B}}'s lead 6 needs to feel genuinely heard before it can move forward, not redirected.
- {{B}} should name the intention behind their questioning — "I'm asking because I want to trust this, not because I doubt you" — which disarms {{A}}'s defensive 1 reaction.
- When {{A}} offers constructive criticism (inevitable given the lead 1), framing it as shared standards rather than personal judgment will land far better with {{B}}'s loyalty-sensitive 6.
- {{B}} can leverage their supporting 1 to speak {{A}}'s language — grounding concerns in principles and ethics rather than feelings will earn more traction with {{A}}'s gut-center lead.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 6 provides {{A}} with something genuinely valuable: a rigorous second-guesser who catches the blind spots that {{A}}'s confident 1 and forward-moving 7 tend to skip over.
- {{A}}'s principled clarity and structured optimism can help {{B}}'s 6 move from anxious cycling to grounded conviction — {{A}} models what it looks like to act from inner certainty rather than external validation.
- The shared 1 creates an unusual growth opportunity: both can call each other toward integrity without it feeling like an attack, because both understand that standard as a sincere aspiration, not a weapon.
- Long-term, {{A}} grows by learning that questioning is a form of loyalty, and {{B}} grows by learning that confidence is not the same as rigidity — each holds a piece of what the other needs.

145-469.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share the 4 as a supporting and lead type respectively, creating a genuine foundation of depth, authenticity-seeking, and discomfort with superficiality. However, {{A}}'s gut-led 1 brings principled, corrective energy that can clash hard with {{B}}'s heart-led 4, which is already primed for shame and the fear of being fundamentally flawed. This pairing has real intimacy potential, but it requires conscious navigation of {{A}}'s critical streak and {{B}}'s emotional volatility.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both share the 4 archetype — {{A}} as a supporting type and {{B}} as lead — meaning each values authenticity, depth of meaning, and disdain for hollow pleasantness.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 and {{B}}'s supporting 6 both operate in the head center, giving them a shared interest in understanding systems, ideas, and motivations, even if their styles differ.
- {{A}}'s high inner standards and {{B}}'s 4-driven need for genuine connection create a relationship that neither person will let become lazy or routine.
- There is a shared seriousness here — both are introspective and drawn to the complex rather than the convenient.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 has a powerful inner critic that frequently externalizes as evaluation and correction; {{B}}'s lead 4 already carries a deep fear of being defective, so {{A}}'s reforming impulse can land as chronic wounding.
- {{B}}'s emotional swings, amplified by the lead 4's identity-intensity, may register to {{A}}'s 1 as irrational excess or a failure of discipline.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 seeks to smooth over conflict and find peace, while {{A}}'s lead 1 wants problems identified and corrected directly — this creates a frustrating push-pull around resolution.
- {{B}}'s supporting 6 generates anxiety and loyalty-testing questions that {{A}}'s 5 support can find draining and hard to take seriously.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s emotional processing as self-indulgence or drama, when for {{B}}'s lead 4, feeling deeply and expressing that feeling is not performance — it is how identity is located and confirmed.
- {{B}} is likely to experience {{A}}'s principled directness as personal rejection or moral condemnation, when for {{A}}'s lead 1, the criticism is usually about the idea or action, not the person's worth.
- Under stress, {{A}}'s supporting 5 pulls toward withdrawal and analysis, while {{B}}'s supporting 6 pulls toward seeking reassurance and contact — these are nearly opposite responses, so both people feel abandoned at the exact moments they most need support.
- {{B}} may feel perpetually evaluated even in casual interactions, because {{A}}'s 1 baseline is one of calibration and correctness rather than emotional presence.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should consciously lead with acknowledgment of {{B}}'s emotional reality before offering any correction or analysis — {{B}}'s lead 4 needs to feel seen as a person before it can hear feedback as useful rather than attacking.
- {{B}} should practice naming feelings as feelings ('I feel unseen') rather than framing them as moral verdicts about {{A}} ('you never care'), which will trigger {{A}}'s 1 defensiveness around being fair and good.
- {{A}} can build trust with {{B}} by occasionally setting aside the corrective impulse entirely and simply inhabiting depth together — the shared 4 energy makes this possible.
- {{B}}'s supporting 6 tendency to test loyalty through questioning should be surfaced explicitly rather than enacted indirectly, as {{A}}'s lead 1 responds much better to clarity than to ambient suspicion.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 4 genuinely offers {{A}} something rare: a model for accessing emotional authenticity and self-compassion without needing to first earn it through correctness or usefulness, which is exactly where {{A}}'s lead 1 gets stuck.
- {{A}}'s lead 1 can offer {{B}} structural grounding — a sense that values and commitments can anchor identity beyond the shifting tides of feeling, which the supporting 9 in {{B}} longs for but cannot generate alone.
- The risk is that both types carry significant self-criticism — {{A}}'s 1 inner critic and {{B}}'s 4 shame loop can amplify each other rather than dissolve each other if the relationship becomes a site of mutual evaluation.
- At their best, this pairing produces something rare: a relationship of genuine integrity and emotional honesty, where both people are pushed to be more whole than they would be separately.

359-748.summary: {{A}} leads with the 3's drive for achievement and image, softened by the 5's analytical reserve and the 9's accommodating calm — a polished, strategically harmonious presence. {{B}} leads with the 7's hunger for experience and possibility, sharpened by the 8's directness and given emotional texture by the 4's need for authenticity. These two can spark real creative and intellectual energy together, but the same qualities that make them exciting to each other will also produce friction around pace, authenticity, and directness.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:

- {{A}}'s supporting 5 and {{B}}'s lead 7 meet in the head center, producing lively intellectual exchanges where {{B}} generates ideas and {{A}} stress-tests them.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s 7 enthusiasm as shallow or commitment-averse, missing that the supporting 4 gives {{B}} genuine emotional stakes that simply don't lead with vulnerability.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s polished 3-led presentation as calculated or inauthentic, not recognizing that the supporting 5 underneath it is genuinely analytical and the supporting 9 genuinely values harmony — this isn't just spin.
- {{A}}'s 9 support handles disagreement by going quiet or deferring; {{B}}'s 8 support reads silence as stonewalling or passive resistance rather than discomfort-avoidance.
- {{B}}'s 4 support occasionally surfaces emotional intensity or a sense of being misunderstood, which {{A}}'s 3-lead tends to reframe as a problem to be solved rather than an experience to be witnessed.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the 9-supported impulse to smooth things over and instead bring enough directness to satisfy {{B}}'s 8-influenced need for honest engagement — vagueness reads as evasion to {{B}}.
- {{B}} should deliberately slow their 7-led pace when {{A}} signals a need to analyze or process; skipping over {{A}}'s 5-supported thinking phase will erode trust over time.
- {{A}} can disarm {{B}}'s 4-driven authenticity radar by stepping out from behind the 3 persona occasionally — sharing a genuine uncertainty or failure costs less than {{A}} fears and gains significant relational ground.
- {{B}} should offer recognition that is specific and real; vague enthusiasm feels hollow to {{A}}'s 3, which needs acknowledgment that is grounded in actual achievement, not just encouragement.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 is a genuine invitation for {{A}}'s lead 3 to stop equating worth with performance — the 4's insistence on authenticity can help {{A}} access emotional honesty rather than emotional management.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 models something {{B}}'s lead 7 genuinely needs: the discipline to go deep into one thing rather than laterally across many, and {{B}} often respects this quality even when it frustrates them.
- {{A}}'s supporting 9 can introduce grounding and patience that moderates {{B}}'s 8-inflected urgency, helping {{B}} see that not every situation requires force.
- Over time, this pairing has real growth potential precisely because each person carries what the other under-develops — {{A}} needs more raw aliveness and authenticity, {{B}} needs more focus and stillness — but this only works if both resist the temptation to stay in their respective comfort registers.

379-629.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a warm, socially oriented surface that makes initial connection feel easy and natural. Beneath that ease, however, their lead types pull in meaningfully different directions — {{A}}'s 3 is driven by image, forward momentum, and adaptive success, while {{B}}'s 6 is anchored in loyalty, vigilance, and the need for authentic security. Their shared 9 in the gut center is a genuine bridge, but it can also become a trap that keeps both from surfacing real tensions.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared gut-9 gives both {{A}} and {{B}} a genuine desire for harmony and a dislike of unnecessary conflict, creating an instinctively peaceful baseline.
- {{A}}'s heart-center 3 and {{B}}'s supporting 2 mean both are relationally warm and socially attentive — they read rooms well together.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 brings optimism and enthusiasm that can genuinely ease {{B}}'s 6-driven anxiety, offering a lift that feels good rather than dismissive.
- Both value connection and will work hard to preserve the relationship, making this a pairing that tends toward durability when both feel safe.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is image-aware and chameleon-like, adapting presentation to context — this directly triggers {{B}}'s lead 6 radar, which is specifically tuned to detect inconsistency and inauthenticity.
- {{B}}'s 6 needs to voice fears and stress-test plans; {{A}}'s supporting 7 treats negativity as something to route around, making {{B}} feel unheard or dismissed.
- {{A}} moves toward goals and positive momentum; {{B}} slows down to scan for risk — these paces conflict when decisions need to be made.
- Both carry a supporting 9, which means neither partner is naturally equipped to force confrontation, so resentments can quietly accumulate for a long time.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{B}} is likely to read {{A}}'s image management and optimistic reframing as evasion or a lack of depth, when in reality {{A}}'s 3 lead genuinely processes experience through the lens of performance and forward motion — it is not deception, it is a core orientation. {{A}}, meanwhile, tends to interpret {{B}}'s questioning and worst-case thinking as distrust or a personal vote of no-confidence, when {{B}}'s 6 lead is simply running its standard security protocol — skepticism is how {{B}} gets to trust, not evidence that trust is absent. {{A}} expects encouragement to signal loyalty; {{B}} expects consistency and transparency to signal it, and these currencies do not automatically translate.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should name fears as fears rather than framing them as evidence of {{A}}'s shortcomings — the 6's interrogative style can read as accusation even when it is not intended that way.
- {{A}} should slow down and offer concrete, repeated demonstrations of reliability rather than defaulting to enthusiasm and charm, which the 6 finds insufficient as proof of commitment.
- Both must actively counteract the shared 9's pull toward postponing hard conversations — they will need to build a deliberate habit of check-ins, since neither will raise issues naturally.
- {{A}} benefits from letting {{B}}'s concerns land without immediately reframing them positively; {{B}} benefits from flagging when a specific reassurance, rather than a general solution, is what is needed.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}} stretches {{B}} toward a more trusting, opportunity-embracing posture — the 3's confidence in forward movement, paired with the 7's genuine delight in possibility, can slowly loosen the 6's grip on worst-case thinking. {{B}} stretches {{A}} toward something harder: real accountability and authentic self-disclosure, pushing past the 3's tendency to manage image rather than reveal interior experience. If {{A}} can learn to stay present to {{B}}'s anxiety without deflecting it, and {{B}} can learn to extend provisional trust before every detail is verified, the relationship becomes a place where both grow beyond their respective defense strategies rather than around them.

136-216.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a surprising amount of structural DNA — both carry 1 and 6 energy — but they orient that shared material from very different centers of gravity. {{A}} leads from the gut with principled correction and improvement as the primary lens, while {{B}} leads from the heart with relational care and the need to be needed. This pairing can be deeply loyal and mutually productive, but the same shared values can become the source of their sharpest friction.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 6 in both tritypes creates an immediate foundation of loyalty, reliability, and long-term commitment — neither person takes relationships lightly.
- Both carry 1 energy and implicitly understand each other's drive to do things *right*; {{A}} at the core, {{B}} as a supporting instinct.
- {{B}}'s warmth softens {{A}}'s rigidity, and {{A}}'s structured follow-through gives {{B}} a dependable anchor they can genuinely trust.
- Both are oriented toward service and responsibility, making them a highly functional team in practical, goal-oriented contexts.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 means the inner critic runs the show: standards are high, mistakes are noted, and correction can feel reflexive rather than compassionate — which directly threatens {{B}}'s deep need for appreciation and validation.
- {{B}}'s lead 2 gives care somewhat conditionally; over time {{B}} may use emotional generosity as leverage, which {{A}}'s 6 will eventually detect and resent as manipulative.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 adds a performance and efficiency angle that can read as cold or self-serving to {{B}}, who measures relationship health by emotional presence.
- When stressed, {{A}} tightens rules and increases criticism while {{B}} escalates helping behaviors to manage anxiety — these stress responses can create a suffocating loop.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s relentless giving as a tactic or a bid for control rather than genuine love, because {{A}}'s own care language is acts of principled correction and holding standards. {{B}} interprets {{A}}'s criticism — even when meant as investment — as rejection or proof of not being good enough, triggering the 2's core fear of being unloved. The shared 1 energy actually deepens this misread: {{A}} assumes {{B}} should be equally comfortable with direct critique because {{B}} also has 1 in their tritype, not recognizing that {{B}}'s 1 is a *supporting* voice filtered through a 2 lead, not an identity anchor. Both can end up feeling unseen by the person they most expected to understand them.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should distinguish between correcting a behavior and evaluating a person — {{B}}'s heart-center lead means these feel identical to them, and specificity matters enormously.
- {{B}} should practice asking for appreciation directly rather than engineering situations where {{A}} is obligated to be grateful; {{A}}'s 6 and 1 both dislike feeling managed.
- Both should leverage their shared 6 by naming security needs explicitly — "I need to know you're still committed" lands better than either criticism or over-giving.
- {{A}} can offer warmth through acknowledgment before launching into improvement mode; even a brief recognition activates {{B}}'s best energy rather than their defensive energy.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: This pairing has genuine long-term growth potential precisely because their shared types (1 and 6) create enough common ground to survive the friction. {{A}} is challenged by {{B}} to integrate real emotional attunement — not just the efficient warmth of the supporting 3, but the messier, slower care of actual relationship presence. {{B}} is challenged by {{A}} to move toward self-worth that doesn't depend on being needed, leaning into the 1's interior moral self-respect rather than the 2's relational validation loop. Their mutual 6 anxiety, if addressed together rather than managed separately, can become a profound source of earned trust over time. The risk is calcification: {{A}} becoming the judge, {{B}} becoming the martyr — and both calling it love.

126-136.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are strikingly similar in architecture — both gut-led 1s with a shared 6 in the head center — giving this pairing a bedrock of shared values, mutual loyalty, and a drive toward correctness and integrity. The real divergence lives in the heart center: {{A}}'s supporting 2 orients toward relational warmth and being needed, while {{B}}'s supporting 3 orients toward achievement, efficiency, and image. This creates a pairing that feels safe and principled but can quietly drift into two different definitions of what a relationship is actually for.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both lead with 1, so integrity, duty, and high standards are non-negotiable shared values — neither has to explain why doing things right matters.
- The shared supporting 6 creates a powerful loyalty bond; both are people who show up, keep promises, and take commitment seriously.
- Mutual 6 anxiety means both understand the need to vet people and situations before trusting, so they tend to give each other the benefit of the doubt once trust is established.
- Both have a strong sense of responsibility and can build systems, routines, or shared projects with genuine dedication.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body: Two lead 1s in close relationship means two active inner critics — disagreements can harden quickly into moral standoffs where both feel they are objectively correct. {{A}}'s supporting 2 creates a relational pull: they want warmth, appreciation, and to feel genuinely needed, which can read to {{B}} as emotional pressure or inefficiency. {{B}}'s supporting 3 introduces a performance and image layer that {{A}} (whose 2 values sincerity over presentation) may distrust or quietly judge as inauthentic. Over time, {{A}} may feel like they're giving more than they're receiving, while {{B}} may feel like {{A}} is too focused on emotional dynamics at the expense of getting things done.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} interprets love and connection through the lens of the supporting 2 — care is demonstrated by attending to people's needs and feelings, and a relationship that doesn't include that texture feels cold or transactional. {{B}} interprets effort and commitment through the lens of the supporting 3 — doing excellent work, delivering results, and maintaining a competent shared image *is* the expression of care. So {{B}} may be genuinely invested but show it in ways {{A}}'s 2 doesn't register as warmth, while {{A}}'s relational attentiveness may seem to {{B}}'s 3 like it's veering off-task. Both share supporting 6, but even their shared anxiety can misfire: {{A}} worries about relational security (am I valued?), while {{B}} worries about performance security (are we succeeding?).

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should name needs directly rather than expressing them through acts of service and hoping {{B}} reciprocates — {{B}}'s 3 is goal-oriented and responds better to explicit asks than to implicit emotional signals.
- {{B}} should occasionally slow down from outcome-focus to acknowledge {{A}}'s relational contributions, since {{A}}'s 2 will quietly tally whether the care they offer is seen.
- Both share lead 1's tendency to critique — agree early on a norm for giving feedback so it doesn't land as personal attack.
- When conflict arises, invoke the shared 6 loyalty rather than the shared 1 righteousness: 'we're on the same side' de-escalates faster than 'I'm right.'

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: Both are being called toward the lead 1's integration point — type 7's ease, spontaneity, and release of control — which neither naturally accesses. {{A}}'s growth edge via the supporting 2 involves letting go of approval-seeking and trusting that they are valued without having to earn it constantly. {{B}}'s growth edge via the supporting 3 involves decoupling self-worth from achievement and allowing authentic vulnerability rather than polished competence. In the best version of this pairing, {{A}} models emotional generosity that softens {{B}}'s drive-oriented shell, and {{B}} models focused ambition that helps {{A}}'s 2 stop over-giving and invest energy in clear goals — but this only works if both are actively doing their own inner work rather than projecting their undeveloped qualities onto each other.

316-729.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} bring genuinely complementary energies — one driving toward achievement and correctness, the other toward possibility and harmony — but the gap between {{A}}'s heart-led intensity and {{B}}'s head-led expansiveness creates real friction around standards, follow-through, and emotional depth. At their best, {{A}} gives {{B}} grounding and direction while {{B}} gives {{A}} levity and warmth. At their worst, {{A}} becomes a critic and {{B}} becomes an escapist, and neither gets what they actually need.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 and {{B}}'s supporting 2 share a strong social orientation — both are attuned to others, personable, and relationship-invested in their own ways.
- {{B}}'s enthusiasm and vision naturally energize {{A}}'s goal-driven 3, making big projects feel exciting rather than just obligatory.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 creates a relaxed, accepting atmosphere that can temporarily quiet {{A}}'s anxious supporting 6, making {{A}} feel genuinely safe.
- Both carry gut support — {{A}}'s 1 and {{B}}'s 9 — which means both, in their own way, want a stable, fair world, even if they disagree on how to get there.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 has a strong inner critic that projects outward as correction and high standards; {{B}}'s lead 7 resists constraints and does not respond well to being told it's doing something wrong.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 needs reliability, follow-through, and proven commitment — three things {{B}}'s scattered lead 7 can struggle to consistently deliver.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 will often avoid conflict by going along with {{A}}, which temporarily satisfies {{A}}'s 3 desire for smooth progress but builds quiet resentment in {{B}}.
- {{A}} may find {{B}}'s habit of generating options without committing to be wasteful or irresponsible; {{B}} may find {{A}}'s task-focus joyless and constricting.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s 6 interprets {{B}}'s 7-led inconsistency as untrustworthiness or lack of seriousness, when {{B}} is genuinely engaged — just nonlinearly.
- {{B}}'s 7 reads {{A}}'s 1-driven criticism as negativity or control, missing that for {{A}}, correcting things *is* a form of care and investment.
- {{A}} assumes {{B}}'s easygoing 9 energy means {{B}} is fine, not realizing that {{B}} may have checked out rather than truly accepted the situation.
- {{B}} underestimates how much {{A}}'s lead 3 ties self-worth to outcomes — what looks like ambition is often anxiety in disguise, and {{B}}'s breezy optimism can feel dismissive rather than reassuring to {{A}}'s underlying 6 fear.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should lead with appreciation before correction — {{B}}'s supporting 2 is genuinely responsive to warmth, and the 1's critique lands far better when {{B}} first feels seen rather than evaluated.
- {{B}} should practice explicit follow-through, not just enthusiasm: naming a specific next step satisfies {{A}}'s 6 need for reliability more than any amount of excitement about a plan.
- {{A}} should flag anxiety directly rather than converting it into task-lists or standards — saying "I'm feeling uncertain about this" is more connecting than "here's what's wrong with the approach."
- {{B}} should resist the 9 impulse to just agree; {{A}}'s lead 3 actually respects directness and will trust {{B}} more when {{B}} pushes back honestly rather than accommodating and quietly disengaging.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s natural spaciousness — the 7's optimism combined with the 9's equanimity — is genuinely therapeutic for {{A}}'s anxious 6, offering a lived model of trust that {{A}} cannot manufacture through effort alone.
- {{A}}'s focus and follow-through can be deeply useful to {{B}}, helping translate the 7's many vivid ideas into completed work that {{B}}'s 7 alone rarely reaches.
- The risk is a slow drift into parent-child dynamics, where {{A}}'s 1+6 manages and monitors while {{B}}'s 7+9 evades and placates — both must consciously resist this pull.
- At their healthiest, {{A}} learns from {{B}} that not everything needs to be optimized or corrected, and {{B}} learns from {{A}} that depth, consistency, and standards are not the enemy of joy.

145-738.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} occupy almost opposite ends of the enneagram's energetic spectrum — {{A}}'s lead 1 is disciplined, principled, and inward-critical, while {{B}}'s lead 7 is expansive, pleasure-seeking, and future-focused. This creates a pairing of genuine creative tension: real friction is baked in, but so is a powerful growth mirror that neither could easily find elsewhere. The relationship works best when both people treat the discomfort as data rather than a threat.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both {{A}} and {{B}} carry strong conviction — {{A}}'s lead 1 has principled certainty, {{B}}'s supporting 8 has forceful will, and they can respect each other's directness and refusal to be pushed around.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 and {{B}}'s lead 7 share a head-center appetite for ideas; their conversations can crackle with intellectual energy, each bringing a different angle (depth vs. breadth).
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 drives toward achievement, which resonates with {{A}}'s lead 1 desire to improve and make things better — they can be a highly productive pair when goals align.
- Both have an independent streak: {{A}}'s 5 needs autonomy to think, {{B}}'s 7 needs freedom to roam, so neither tends to smother the other.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 runs on a strong inner critic and holds high standards for how things should be done; {{B}}'s lead 7 is wired to move fast, cut corners when necessary, and resist being corrected — {{A}}'s perfectionism will feel like a leash to {{B}}.
- {{B}}'s lead 7 routinely avoids pain, difficulty, and limitation; {{A}}'s supporting 4 is drawn toward depth, melancholy, and the full weight of experience — {{B}} will find this heavy, {{A}} will find {{B}}'s relentless positivity dishonest.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 craves authentic emotional intimacy; {{B}}'s lead 7 deflects emotional intensity with humor, reframing, or simply moving on, which can leave {{A}} feeling unseen.
- Power struggles are possible: {{A}}'s lead 1 is rigid in matters of principle, {{B}}'s supporting 8 digs in when it feels controlled, and neither yields easily.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} is likely to read {{B}} as irresponsible, superficial, or morally sloppy — mistaking 7's optimism and adaptability for a lack of integrity, and reading 3's image-awareness as inauthenticity. {{B}} is likely to read {{A}} as joyless, rigid, or punishing — mistaking 1's principled seriousness for judgment and 4's emotional depth for excessive negativity. Critically, when {{A}}'s 4 surfaces pain or dissatisfaction, {{B}}'s lead 7 will reflexively try to reframe or dismiss it rather than sit with it, which {{A}} experiences as dismissal rather than support. Meanwhile, {{A}} may misinterpret {{B}}'s rapid pivots and restless enthusiasm as lack of commitment rather than as a fundamentally different relationship to time and possibility.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should lead with appreciation or a shared vision before offering critique — {{B}}'s lead 7 shuts down under sustained correction but is genuinely responsive to enthusiasm and forward momentum.
- {{B}} should resist the urge to immediately reframe or 'silver-lining' {{A}}'s concerns; {{A}}'s 1 and 4 both need their perspective taken seriously before solutions are offered.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 is a natural bridge: engaging {{B}} intellectually around ideas and possibilities tends to land better than moralizing from the 1.
- {{B}} should make explicit commitments and follow through on them — {{A}}'s lead 1 tracks consistency closely, and broken promises erode trust faster than almost anything else.
- {{A}} can signal to {{B}} when they need depth vs. problem-solving, since {{B}} genuinely cannot always tell the difference.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: The growth lines here create an unusually precise mirror: Enneagram 1 grows toward 7 (spontaneity, trust in abundance, release of control), meaning {{B}} literally embodies a quality {{A}} is being called to develop. Conversely, 7 grows toward 5 (stillness, depth, expertise, sitting with what is) — and {{A}}'s supporting 5 models exactly that capacity for {{B}}. If both are self-aware, this pairing becomes a living growth edge rather than just a personality clash. The risk is that neither does the actual internal work and instead resents the other for being 'too much' of what they fear: {{A}} experiencing {{B}} as chaotic and unserious, {{B}} experiencing {{A}} as constraining and grim. The reward, when both lean in, is that {{A}} loosens into joy and trust while {{B}} develops the depth and follow-through their lead 7 so often skips.

378-739.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a dazzling overlap in 3 and 7 energy, making them feel immediately like kindred spirits — fast-moving, ambitious, and wired for excitement. But beneath the surface, {{A}}'s heart-led drive for achievement and status (lead 3, bolstered by a confrontational 8) pulls in a very different direction than {{B}}'s head-led pursuit of freedom and experience (lead 7, softened by a conflict-averse 9). This is a pairing with real chemistry and real friction, often at the same time.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 3 and 7 energy creates instant rapport: both are enthusiastic, future-oriented, and love the thrill of a bold new project.
- {{A}}'s drive to succeed and {{B}}'s hunger for stimulating experiences make them natural collaborators who push each other toward bigger moves.
- Socially, this pairing is magnetic — {{A}}'s polished confidence and {{B}}'s infectious optimism complement each other beautifully in public.
- Neither type dwells easily in the past, so the relationship tends to feel forward-moving and energizing rather than stuck.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is acutely image-conscious and competitive; {{B}}'s lead 7 is allergic to being boxed in by expectations or performance pressure, which can make {{A}} feel unsupported.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 brings blunt, confrontational energy when things go wrong; {{B}}'s supporting 9 instinctively softens or sidesteps conflict, which {{A}} can read as evasion or spinelessness.
- {{A}} wants to win and be recognized for it; {{B}} wants to keep options open and move to the next experience, making sustained collaboration on long-term goals genuinely hard.
- {{B}}'s 7-led reframing of setbacks as "not a big deal" can feel deeply invalidating to {{A}}, who measures reality through the lens of success and failure.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}} as flaky or uncommitted — mistaking {{B}}'s 7-led need for freedom as a lack of seriousness rather than a core operating principle.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}} as uptight or ego-driven — mistaking {{A}}'s 3-led focus on outcomes and reputation as vanity rather than a genuine engine of motivation.
- When {{A}}'s 8 comes out in anger or directness, {{B}}'s 9 goes quiet or deflects, which {{A}} interprets as indifference — but {{B}} is actually absorbing the conflict internally and feeling overwhelmed.
- {{B}} may not realize that enthusiasm alone doesn't satisfy {{A}}; {{A}} needs acknowledgment of specific achievements, not just general excitement about what's possible next.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist turning every conversation into a performance review or scorecard — {{B}}'s lead 7 will shut down or bolt when it feels like a commitment trap.
- {{B}} should practice naming {{A}}'s wins explicitly and directly, rather than pivoting immediately to the next big idea; a moment of recognition goes a long way with a lead 3.
- When conflict arises, {{A}} should dial back the 8-style confrontation long enough to let {{B}}'s 9 surface what's actually bothering them, rather than forcing a rapid resolution.
- {{B}} should resist the urge to reframe or minimize problems that matter to {{A}} — sometimes the most useful thing is simply to sit with what went wrong before moving on.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} a genuine invitation to loosen the grip on outcomes and find joy in the process itself — the 7's gift of presence and delight is something {{A}}'s relentless 3 badly needs.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} focus, follow-through, and a model for converting enthusiasm into real results — the 3's discipline is a natural corrective to 7's tendency to scatter energy across too many ideas.
- The real risk in this pairing is mutual enabling of avoidance: {{A}} can use busyness and achievement as a shield against deeper feeling, and {{B}} can use optimism as a shield against pain — together they may collude in staying on the surface.
- Growth for this pair comes when they slow down enough to ask each other harder questions: what are we actually afraid of, and what are we building this for?

126-529.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a pairing of two quietly principled, service-oriented types who share a supporting 2 but lead from very different centers — gut-driven moral conviction versus head-driven analytical detachment. This gives them a real basis for mutual respect and shared purpose, but their core operating styles create consistent friction around emotional availability, criticism, and the pace of engagement. With self-awareness, they can form a complementary team; without it, {{A}} feels unsupported and {{B}} feels scrutinized.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry a supporting 2, meaning both genuinely want to be useful and care about the people around them — this shared Helper impulse creates warmth and a sense of being on the same side.
- {{A}}'s lead 1 brings ethical rigor and a drive for improvement; {{B}}'s lead 5 brings deep knowledge and careful analysis — together they can solve real problems with both integrity and intelligence.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 softens {{B}}'s 5 tendency toward cold detachment, making {{B}} more adaptive and easier for {{A}} to work alongside than a purely 5-led type might be.
- Both are serious, competence-oriented people who value substance over superficiality, so they rarely bore each other.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 is wired to notice what is wrong and correct it — this directness reads as constant criticism to {{B}}'s 5, which is extremely sensitive to feeling judged or managed.
- {{B}}'s lead 5 requires significant alone time and guards its inner world carefully; {{A}}'s supporting 6 needs reassurance and consistent engagement, which {{B}} can find draining and {{A}} finds frustrating to have to ask for.
- {{A}}'s 2 wants reciprocal warmth and appreciation; {{B}}'s 5 expresses care through knowledge and competence rather than emotional attunement, and this gap can leave {{A}} feeling lonely even in the relationship.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 may go along with {{A}}'s 1-driven plans on the surface while quietly disengaging internally, creating a slow-burn resentment neither is immediately aware of.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s withdrawal and emotional reserve as indifference or lack of investment; in reality, {{B}}'s 5 is often deeply invested — it just processes internally and does not signal that investment in ways {{A}}'s 2 and 6 can easily read.
- {{B}} experiences {{A}}'s corrections and high standards as controlling or hypercritical, not recognizing that {{A}}'s lead 1 is applying the same exacting standard to itself — it's not personal targeting, it's a worldview.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 generates anxiety through worst-case thinking and seeks verbal reassurance; {{B}}'s 5 finds this puzzling or irrational, and may dismiss the concern rather than address the underlying need for connection.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 merges quietly with the environment and avoids explicit conflict, so {{A}} may not realize {{B}} has disagreements until they surface in a much larger way.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should make a deliberate practice of separating observation from judgment when speaking to {{B}} — framing concerns as questions rather than corrections will keep {{B}}'s 5 from going defensive and shutting down.
- {{B}} should offer explicit, proactive reassurance to {{A}} even when it feels unnecessary — {{A}}'s 6 does not pick up on implicit signals, and a short, clear statement of trust goes a long way.
- Both should use their shared 2 energy as a conversational bridge: grounding difficult conversations in 'how can I help' rather than 'what is wrong' lowers the temperature for both types.
- {{B}} should practice naming disagreements rather than deferring via the supporting 9; {{A}}'s 1 actually respects directness and will engage more fairly with an explicit objection than with passive withdrawal.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}} challenges {{B}} to move from pure analysis into engaged, accountable action — the 1's insistence that knowledge must serve ethical purpose is genuinely stretching for a 5 that can become comfortable with indefinite reflection.
- {{B}} offers {{A}} something equally valuable: a model of nonjudgmental observation, where data is gathered before verdicts are issued — this can meaningfully soften {{A}}'s 1 tendency to arrive at conclusions too quickly.
- {{A}}'s growth edge in this relationship is learning to provide safety before correction, so {{B}} can stay present rather than retreat; {{B}}'s growth edge is tolerating more emotional demand and reciprocating {{A}}'s 2 in kind.
- When both are at their best — {{A}} leading with principled warmth and {{B}} leading with grounded wisdom — this pairing produces the kind of thoughtful, reliable partnership that gets genuinely difficult things done.

316-728.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a high-energy pairing that can accomplish a great deal together, but they operate from fundamentally different orientations — {{A}} leads with disciplined ambition and an anxious need for reliability, while {{B}} leads with expansive enthusiasm and a drive to keep options open. The shared appetite for engagement and doing keeps them attracted to each other, but {{A}}'s need for structure, loyalty, and correctness constantly rubs against {{B}}'s instinct to improvise and escape constraint. This pairing has real potential, but it demands conscious negotiation of pace, accountability, and emotional depth.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both 3 and 7 are high-drive, externally oriented types who thrive in social settings and move fast — they energize each other naturally.
- {{A}}'s competence and presentation (lead 3) impresses {{B}}, while {{B}}'s warmth via supporting 2 and bold directness via supporting 8 excite {{A}}.
- {{B}}'s 8 and {{A}}'s gut support (1) both value directness — neither will shy away from hard conversations when it matters.
- Together they can be a formidable team: {{A}} provides focused execution and {{B}} generates ideas and momentum.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 demands precision, proper process, and follow-through; {{B}}'s lead 7 resists being pinned to a single plan and pivots freely, which reads to {{A}} as sloppy or uncommitted.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 has a deep need for reliability and loyalty — exactly what a 7-led type struggles most to consistently provide.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 pushes back hard when feeling controlled; {{A}}'s 1 and 3 combined can come across as both critical and image-policing, triggering {{B}}'s resistance.
- {{A}} wants sustained commitment to shared goals; {{B}} wants to stay excited — when the novelty fades, {{B}} can mentally check out before {{A}} has any warning.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s spontaneity and mental pivoting as disloyalty or irresponsibility (a direct 6 fear trigger), when {{B}} simply experiences commitment through enthusiasm rather than consistency.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s task-focus, criticism, and controlled presentation as joyless rigidity or emotional unavailability, missing that {{A}}'s 3 suppresses feelings in service of goals — there is real emotion underneath.
- {{A}}'s combination of 3 image-management and 6 anxiety can look like uptightness or passive judgment to {{B}}, who experiences {{A}} as taking the fun out of things.
- {{B}}'s 2 genuinely wants warmth and to feel appreciated, but {{A}}'s transactional 3 energy can make interactions feel like performance reviews rather than connection.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should treat follow-through as a direct act of care toward {{A}} — honoring small commitments addresses {{A}}'s 6 security anxiety more than words of reassurance ever will.
- {{A}} should lead with acknowledgment of {{B}}'s ideas and energy before redirecting or correcting — {{B}}'s supporting 2 needs to feel valued before it can receive critique without triggering the 8's defensiveness.
- {{A}} should name anxiety explicitly rather than converting it into criticism or task-pressure; the 1's inner critic is most destructive when it leaks out sideways.
- {{B}} should resist the 7's reflex to reframe problems optimistically before {{A}} has felt heard — the 6 in {{A}} needs to feel the concern is taken seriously, not bypassed.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 7 is one of the best antidotes to {{A}}'s 1-driven inner critic and 3-driven performance anxiety — genuine play and levity can help {{A}} reconnect to intrinsic worth rather than earned value.
- {{A}}'s discipline and follow-through (3+1) can model for {{B}} that sustained commitment to one direction actually produces deeper satisfaction than constant novelty, directly addressing the 7's core avoidance of pain through distraction.
- The central growth risk is role calcification: {{A}} becoming the joyless enforcer and {{B}} becoming the escapee, which hardens both into their worst patterns.
- When this pairing is working well, {{A}} learns that imperfection is survivable and {{B}} learns that structure is not imprisonment — those are exactly the core growth edges for types 1/3 and 7 respectively.

215-713.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a heart-meets-head pairing with a meaningful shared gut anchor in their common 1, which creates a genuine thread of principled, improvement-oriented energy between them. {{A}} leads with warmth, relational investment, and a mentor's instinct to guide, while {{B}} leads with expansive enthusiasm, future-scanning optimism, and a builder's appetite for systems and ideas. The dynamic can be vitalizing when both are at their best, but real friction arises around emotional depth, reciprocity, and follow-through.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared supporting 1 gives both {{A}} and {{B}} a respect for doing things right — they can bond over ethics, standards, and the desire to improve the world around them.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 brings intellectual curiosity that genuinely matches {{B}}'s lead-7 appetite for ideas and stimulating conversation; these two can go deep on concepts together.
- {{B}}'s enthusiasm and optimism energize {{A}}, who as a lead 2 loves to contribute to something that feels alive and meaningful.
- {{A}}'s mentoring instinct and {{B}}'s systems-building drive can combine into genuinely productive collaboration — {{A}} supports the people, {{B}} designs the structure.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 needs to feel emotionally seen, appreciated, and deeply connected — {{B}}'s lead 7, which instinctively avoids emotional weight and commitment, can leave {{A}} feeling chronically undernourished.
- {{B}}'s scattered, future-jumping energy will frustrate {{A}}'s supporting 1, which values follow-through, responsibility, and finishing what was started.
- {{A}} can slide into quiet resentment when giving goes unreciprocated; {{B}} rarely notices the score is being kept because 7s tend to assume everyone is fine and moving forward.
- Both carry a supporting 1, which means both can be quietly critical — but they may disagree sharply on *what* needs correcting, leading to principled standoffs.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} often interprets {{B}}'s warm enthusiasm as deep relational investment, then feels blindsided when {{B}} moves on to the next thing — {{B}} wasn't being deceptive, just true to 7's restless forward motion.
- {{B}} takes {{A}}'s helpfulness at face value and misses the implicit relational contract underneath it: lead-2 helping carries an expectation of acknowledgment and reciprocity that {{B}} never consciously signed.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 gives them a quietly withdrawn, analytical side that {{B}} may read as coldness or disengagement, when it's actually {{A}} processing carefully before acting.
- {{B}}'s reframing of difficult emotions as opportunities or silver linings looks emotionally avoidant — even shallow — to {{A}}'s heart-centered worldview, though for {{B}} it's a genuine coping and motivating strategy rooted in 7's core structure.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} must name needs directly rather than hinting or hoping {{B}} will notice — lead 7 is not wired to read emotional subtext, and silence will be taken as contentment.
- {{B}} should practice deliberately slowing down to ask {{A}} how they are *feeling*, not just what they *think* — it signals the relational presence {{A}}'s lead 2 requires to feel secure.
- When disagreements arise, both can invoke the shared 1 energy by framing the conversation around shared values and standards rather than blame — "what's the right thing to do here" is language both will respond to.
- {{A}} should resist the urge to guilt-trip; {{B}} should resist the urge to reframe {{A}}'s concerns into positivity before they've been fully heard.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} genuinely challenges {{A}} to stop measuring love through sacrifice — the 7's self-referencing, pleasure-oriented energy can be a healthy mirror for {{A}}'s lead 2, which struggles to prioritize its own joy.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something the lead 7 rarely gets: consistent, warm presence from someone who actually pays attention to how {{B}} is doing beneath the enthusiasm — this can support real emotional grounding in {{B}} over time.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 and {{B}}'s supporting 3 together create a competence bridge — shared respect for knowledge and results can build trust that the emotional work between them is worth it.
- The shared 1 is ultimately a growth anchor: when both are operating at their best, they share a conscience-driven commitment to integrity that can hold the relationship to a higher standard than either would maintain alone.

135-714.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a high-contrast pairing held together by a single powerful shared thread: both carry the energy of the 1. {{A}} leads with it — principled, precise, and improvement-driven — while {{B}} carries it as a supporting anchor beneath an enthusiastic, expansive 7 lead. This means they can respect each other's values, but their fundamental orientations toward life (correction vs. expansion, rigor vs. possibility) create real friction that requires conscious navigation.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 1 energy gives both {{A}} and {{B}} an ethical backbone — when values are on the table, they often land in the same place.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 and {{B}}'s lead 7 are both head-center types, so intellectual sparring and idea-exchange feel energizing rather than exhausting.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 gives them enough structure-appreciation to genuinely respect {{A}}'s standards rather than dismissing them outright.
- Both are quietly ambitious — {{A}} through the supporting 3's drive for competence and achievement, {{B}} through the 7's appetite for big-picture impact.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body: {{A}}'s lead 1 is wired to notice what is wrong, incomplete, or improvable — and that inner critic easily becomes an outer critic. {{B}}'s lead 7 is wired to escape discomfort, reframe negatives, and keep moving forward; sustained criticism from {{A}} will feel suffocating and may trigger {{B}}'s flight response. {{A}}'s supporting 5 also craves depth and deliberate pacing, while {{B}}'s 7 lead generates options rapidly and resists slowing down long enough to finish what was started. {{B}}'s supporting 4 adds an emotional intensity and desire for authentic expression that can feel dramatic or self-indulgent to {{A}}'s tightly controlled 1-3-5 stack.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}} as scattered, undisciplined, or intellectually shallow — mistaking {{B}}'s generative enthusiasm for a lack of seriousness.
- {{B}} is likely to read {{A}} as rigid, joyless, or controlling — mistaking {{A}}'s principled precision for a personal attack on {{B}}'s ideas.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 wants recognition for measurable competence; {{B}}'s supporting 4 wants recognition for uniqueness and inner truth — these are genuinely different emotional currencies, and each may feel unseen by the other.
- {{B}} avoids pain by reframing or moving on; {{A}} processes problems by analyzing and correcting them — so the same difficult situation will prompt opposite instincts.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should frame feedback as shared standards rather than personal corrections — invoking the 1 values both share lands far better than leading with critique.
- {{B}} should resist the 7 impulse to pivot away from hard conversations; {{A}}'s lead 1 needs the issue to be genuinely resolved, not just reframed positively.
- When disagreements arise, both can anchor to the ethical common ground that their shared 1 energy provides — this is a reliable reset point.
- {{B}} should give {{A}}'s supporting 5 real intellectual respect: bring depth, not just enthusiasm, and {{A}} will open considerably more.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: This pairing carries a structurally significant mirror: on the Enneagram's stress and growth lines, 1 moves toward 7 in health (becoming more spontaneous and joyful) and 7 moves toward 1 in integration (becoming more disciplined and purposeful). That means {{A}} and {{B}} literally embody each other's growth direction. At their best, {{B}} shows {{A}} what it looks like to trust life without needing to fix it first, and {{A}} shows {{B}} what it looks like to see something through to its full, careful completion. The risk is that this dynamic runs in the unhealthy direction instead — {{A}} becoming more rigid under stress, {{B}} becoming more scattered — which amplifies the friction rather than the growth. Conscious intention is what determines which version of this mirror they get.

612-649.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a 6-led foundation, which creates an immediate sense of mutual recognition — both understand the anxious search for trustworthy, stable connection. However, their supporting types pull them in meaningfully different directions: {{A}} moves outward through helpfulness and principled correction, while {{B}} turns inward through emotional depth and harmony-seeking. This pairing has genuine staying power but will require deliberate effort to bridge their contrasting relational styles.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body: The 6-to-6 core is the bedrock here — both {{A}} and {{B}} prize loyalty above almost everything else, test relationships carefully before committing, and once committed, show up with real dedication. They will quickly recognize each other's caution as trustworthiness rather than coldness, which accelerates genuine bonding. Both carry a quiet anxiety about the world and will feel less alone knowing the other operates from a similar vigilance. {{A}}'s supporting 2 offers the warmth {{B}}'s 6 craves, and {{B}}'s supporting 9 offers the calm steadiness {{A}}'s 6 finds deeply reassuring.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 is improvement-oriented and can be quietly critical; {{B}}'s supporting 9 goes numb or withdraws when standards are imposed, which frustrates {{A}} further.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 is emotionally self-referential and needs to be seen in their uniqueness; {{A}}'s supporting 2 wants to give and help, and may feel shut out or unappreciated when {{B}} turns inward.
- {{A}}'s 1 sees moral clarity as caring; {{B}}'s 9 experiences it as pressure and responds with passive resistance.
- {{B}}'s 4-driven emotional withdrawals can spike {{A}}'s 6 abandonment anxiety, prompting {{A}} to either over-help (2) or correct (1) — both of which push {{B}} further away.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
