- {{A}}'s warmth and generosity (supporting 2) makes {{B}} feel genuinely welcomed, and {{B}}'s confidence and drive (supporting 3 and 8) energizes {{A}}.
- Neither type dwells naturally in heaviness or pessimism, so the relationship can sustain a buoyant, forward-looking tone.
- Both dislike being boxed in, so they tend to give each other room to move and explore rather than clinging or over-structuring.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 brings a bluntness and appetite for confrontation that directly collides with {{A}}'s supporting 9, which is wired to smooth conflict and keep the peace at almost any cost.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 is performance- and image-oriented; {{A}}'s supporting 2 is oriented toward relational harmony and others' approval — these are different definitions of what it means to succeed or matter, and can breed quiet resentment.
- When stress hits, {{A}} tends to merge and accommodate (9) or over-give (2), while {{B}} tends to push harder and dominate (8) — these stress responses can make conflict escalate rather than resolve.
- {{A}} may find {{B}} self-focused and forceful; {{B}} may find {{A}} conflict-avoidant and indirectly manipulative.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} often reads {{B}}'s directness and intensity (8) as aggression or lack of care, when for {{B}} directness is simply honest engagement, not an attack.
- {{B}} often reads {{A}}'s conflict-avoidance (9) and people-pleasing (2) as spinelessness or passive aggression, when {{A}} is genuinely motivated by a desire for harmony, not manipulation.
- Because both lead with 7 and outwardly project optimism, each may assume the other is fine when they aren't — neither is naturally inclined to surface discomfort, and their different suppression strategies ({{A}} minimizes, {{B}} steamrolls past) mean real issues can go unaddressed for a long time.
- {{B}} may not realize how much {{A}} shapes themselves around others' needs, and {{A}} may not realize how much {{B}} defines themselves through achievement and impact.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should dial back the 8's instinct to push or dominate during disagreements — {{A}}'s supporting 9 will simply shut down or disappear rather than engage if the pressure feels unsafe.
- {{A}} should practice naming what they actually want or feel before defaulting to accommodation (2) or numbing out (9) — {{B}} genuinely respects directness and will respond better to a clear statement than to hints.
- Both should watch the shared 7 tendency to reframe difficult emotions into positivity too quickly; some problems need to sit and be named before being resolved.
- {{B}} can frame hard conversations as problem-solving rather than challenge or critique, and {{A}} can remind {{B}} that harmony is not the same as avoidance — both are valid concerns that need room.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} challenges {{A}} to develop a spine: the presence of 8 energy in the relationship forces {{A}} to either become more grounded in their own gut knowing (moving toward a healthier 9 and a more boundaried 2) or to stay stuck in passive accommodation.
- {{A}} challenges {{B}} to slow down and actually connect: the warmth of {{A}}'s 2 and the ease of their 9 can soften {{B}}'s harder edges and model that relationships don't have to be won or performed for.
- Both grow by integrating what the other already carries — {{A}} needs more of {{B}}'s self-assertion, and {{B}} needs more of {{A}}'s genuine other-orientation — which means this pairing has real developmental potential if both are willing to be honest about where they are limited.

136-469.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a pairing of principled gut energy meeting rich heart energy — both serious, values-driven, and allergic to superficiality. Their shared 6 creates a meaningful bridge of loyalty and commitment, but their lead types (1 and 4) operate from fundamentally different orientations toward truth: {{A}} trusts objective standards, while {{B}} trusts subjective emotional experience. The relationship holds real potential for mutual growth, but will require deliberate work to bridge the gap between {{A}}'s inner critic that corrects the world and {{B}}'s inner critic that mourns it.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the 6 as a head-center support, meaning loyalty, follow-through, and trustworthiness are non-negotiable values for each — this creates rare relational bedrock.
- Lead 1 and lead 4 both have fierce integrity; neither is interested in performance for its own sake, and both can sniff out inauthenticity quickly.
- {{A}}'s 3 and {{B}}'s 4 are adjacent heart types, giving both an awareness of identity, meaning, and the desire to matter — they understand each other's seriousness about purpose.
- Neither person does casual or shallow; this pairing tends toward depth, commitment, and a shared sense that relationships should mean something.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 operates from a clear internal rulebook — things are right or wrong, efficient or wasteful — while {{B}}'s lead 4 lives in emotional nuance and resists being flattened into categories.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 adds a goal-oriented, results-driven current that can feel impatient with {{B}}'s need to sit with feeling before acting.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 introduces a conflict-avoidant passivity that can frustrate {{A}}'s lead 1, which wants problems named and addressed directly.
- When stressed, {{A}} becomes hypercritical and rigid; {{B}} becomes withdrawn and convinced of being fundamentally misunderstood — these stress responses are mutually amplifying.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s emotional intensity and identity focus as self-indulgence or inefficiency, when in fact it is {{B}}'s primary means of accessing truth.
- {{B}} is likely to experience {{A}}'s corrections and standards as a failure to appreciate complexity or emotional reality, when {{A}} is genuinely trying to help things be better.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 can come across as image-conscious or achievement-focused to {{B}}'s lead 4, which prizes raw authenticity above polished outcomes — {{B}} may quietly question whether {{A}} is being real.
- {{B}}'s 4-led longing and sense of lack can look like chronic dissatisfaction to {{A}}, who values improvement through action rather than through feeling.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the reflex to correct or redirect when {{B}} is processing emotionally — {{B}}'s lead 4 needs to feel genuinely received before it can hear feedback or problem-solve.
- {{B}} should name emotional needs explicitly rather than withdrawing when hurt; {{A}}'s lead 1 reads ambiguity as a problem to solve and may escalate rather than soften.
- Both share the 6's anxiety about trust and security — invoking loyalty and shared commitment ('I'm in this with you') is a language that lands for both.
- {{A}} benefits from framing observations as 'I noticed' rather than 'you should'; {{B}} benefits from translating feelings into actionable requests so {{A}} has something concrete to work with.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s 4 has a natural growth line toward 1 — in integration, {{B}} moves toward the principled action and clarity that {{A}} embodies as a lead, making {{A}} a genuine growth mirror for {{B}}.
- {{A}} can grow by absorbing {{B}}'s capacity to sit in emotional ambiguity and honor subjective experience, developing the emotional attunement that lead 1 often bypasses in its drive toward correctness.
- The risk is codependency in their shared 6 anxiety — if both are stressed simultaneously, the relationship can become a loop of worry, over-responsibility, and mutual reassurance-seeking rather than grounded support.
- At their best, {{A}} helps {{B}} channel depth into disciplined action, and {{B}} helps {{A}} understand that not every problem is a flaw to be corrected — some things are simply felt, and that is enough.

528-614.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both head-centered leads who share an intellectual orientation and a hunger for depth, making their initial connection feel unusually substantive. However, 5 and 6 process the world through very different anxieties — {{A}} retreats inward to preserve autonomy and competence, while {{B}} reaches outward to build security through tested alliances — and this divergence creates real friction around intimacy, reassurance, and trust. The supporting types add texture: {{A}}'s 2 and 8 give warmth and directness, while {{B}}'s 4 and 1 add emotional intensity and moral conviction, producing a pairing that is stimulating but requires deliberate effort to stay calibrated.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both 5 and 6 are head-center types who value intellectual rigor, and conversations between {{A}} and {{B}} tend to go deep fast — they both distrust surface-level engagement.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 and {{B}}'s supporting 1 share a gut-level orientation toward integrity and taking stands, giving them a common ethical backbone.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 provides genuine warmth that soothes {{B}}'s 6-driven need for reliable allies — {{B}} senses that {{A}} actually cares, not just performs care.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 brings emotional depth and authenticity that {{A}}'s lead 5 quietly prizes; {{A}} respects people who are genuinely individuated rather than socially performed.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 5 instinctively withdraws to recharge and think independently, while {{B}}'s lead 6 interprets that withdrawal as a loyalty signal — and usually a negative one.
- {{B}}'s 6 may cycle through doubt and reassurance-seeking in ways that feel energetically expensive to {{A}}, who guards personal resources carefully.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 can be blunt and confrontational; this activates {{B}}'s 6 threat-scanning, making ordinary directness land as aggression.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 can slide into moral criticism when stressed, and {{A}}'s 8 in particular does not tolerate being judged or corrected — expect friction here when either person is under pressure.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s persistent questioning and need for verbal confirmation as distrust or insecurity — even paranoia — when it is actually {{B}}'s primary mechanism for building a secure bond. Conversely, {{B}} reads {{A}}'s need for solitude and self-containment as emotional unavailability or a covert withdrawal of commitment, when for {{A}} it is simply how the lead 5 functions and refuels. {{B}}'s supporting 4 can generate emotional intensity or melancholy that {{A}}'s 5 experiences as destabilizing, while {{B}} may feel {{A}} is dismissive of inner experience. These misreads compound because neither type leads with direct emotional disclosure — problems fester beneath intellectual discussion.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should offer explicit, unprompted reassurance to {{B}} — not just presence, but verbal acknowledgment of commitment; {{B}}'s 6 needs to hear it stated, not inferred.
- {{B}} should distinguish between genuine concern worth raising and anxiety-driven testing, and bring questions to {{A}} directly rather than circling them.
- When {{A}}'s supporting 8 wants to be direct, checking whether {{B}} is already activated by stress first will prevent the conversation from becoming a conflict about tone.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 criticism is best offered as a shared value conversation, not a correction — {{A}}'s 8 energy will resist any framing that feels like a lecture.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}}'s lead 6 can push {{A}} toward greater relational accountability — {{A}}'s 5 tends to live in the mind and can neglect how its self-sufficiency affects those it claims to care about, and {{B}} will not let that slide quietly. In return, {{A}}'s lead 5 models internal authority and independent thinking that {{B}}'s 6 genuinely needs to develop — the capacity to trust one's own conclusions without constant external validation. {{A}}'s supporting 2 can be stretched by {{B}}'s supporting 4 to recognize and name its own emotional needs, not just tend to others'. Over time, if both can tolerate the friction without retreating into their respective defenses — {{A}} into detachment, {{B}} into suspicion — this pairing produces two people who are sharper, more trusting, and more emotionally honest than they would be apart.

379-415.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share the heart center as their lead, which creates an immediate sense of mutual emotional recognition — but the 3 and 4 are arguably the most philosophically opposed heart types, splitting on the question of image versus authenticity. This pairing has real creative and intellectual potential, but it requires both people to resist their default defenses: {{A}}'s tendency to perform and smooth things over, and {{B}}'s tendency to withdraw and critique. The relationship can be genuinely transformative if both are willing to do that work.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both lead from the heart and care deeply about identity, meaning, and how they show up in the world — this gives the relationship a sense of emotional seriousness neither takes lightly.
- {{B}}'s 4 is drawn to what feels rare and significant, and {{A}}'s polished 3 combined with 7's infectious enthusiasm can read as genuinely compelling and magnetic at first.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 and {{B}}'s supporting 5 can find common ground in ideas — 7 generates them rapidly, 5 stress-tests them, and together this can produce sharp, creative thinking.
- Both have an artistic or aesthetic sensibility: {{A}}'s 3 crafts presentation and vision, {{B}}'s 4 seeks depth and originality, and when these forces align on a shared project, the output tends to be distinctive.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- The core friction is structural: lead 3 manages identity through achievement and external validation, while lead 4 manages identity through authenticity and emotional depth — {{A}} instinctively adapts to the room, which {{B}}'s 4 reads as shapeshifting or inauthenticity.
- {{A}}'s supporting 9 wants harmony and will smooth over conflict; {{B}}'s supporting 1 holds firm on standards and can be pointedly critical, meaning {{B}} often pushes just when {{A}} is trying to de-escalate.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 reframes pain and keeps things moving forward, while {{B}}'s lead 4 insists on sitting inside difficult feelings — this difference in emotional processing pace creates real friction over time.
- {{B}}'s 4 needs to feel singular and deeply understood; {{A}}'s 3 is efficiency-oriented and may unconsciously treat {{B}}'s emotional needs as a problem to solve rather than a state to witness.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s emotional intensity and periodic withdrawal as dramatic or self-indulgent, while {{B}} reads {{A}}'s optimism and social adaptability as performance — both misreadings are understandable, and both are partially wrong.
- When {{B}}'s supporting 1 delivers a critique, {{A}}'s lead 3 hears an attack on their image and competence; {{A}} then either deflects (3) or goes quiet (9), which {{B}} interprets as defensive avoidance rather than genuine hurt.
- {{A}}'s 9 attempts at peace-making — minimizing, redirecting, keeping things pleasant — land for {{B}}'s 4 as dismissal of legitimate feeling, when {{A}} genuinely believes they are helping.
- {{B}}'s 5 withdraws to process privately; {{A}}'s 3 moves quickly and interprets that silence as rejection or disengagement rather than as {{B}}'s normal mode of reflection.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the 7 impulse to reframe toward the positive and the 9 impulse to smooth things over; {{B}} needs acknowledgment of depth before any pivot to solutions or optimism.
- {{B}} should recognize that {{A}}'s adaptability is a genuine skill, not a character flaw — lead 3 shifts presentation, not necessarily values, and naming that distinction out loud reduces the 'fake' accusation that poisons this pairing.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 delivers criticism with moral weight; framing feedback as shared problem-solving rather than correction will help {{A}}'s 3 stay open instead of defensive.
- {{A}} can invite {{B}} in by slowing down and asking specific questions about {{B}}'s inner experience — this signals that depth is welcome, which disarms {{B}}'s 4 fear of being unseen or ordinary in the relationship.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} something genuinely valuable: sustained contact with authentic feeling and the courage to be seen without a polished frame. For a lead 3, this is real developmental territory.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} momentum — the ability to take something emotionally significant and make it visible, actionable, and shared with the world, which counters the 4's pull toward private rumination.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 can help {{B}}'s 4 access lightness and possibility without abandoning depth, modeling that joy and significance are not opposites.
- {{B}}'s 4-1 combination pushes {{A}} toward integrity that isn't contingent on audience approval — over time, this pressure, if received well, can help {{A}}'s 3 build a self-concept that doesn't collapse when external validation disappears.

459-479.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a rare emotional wavelength — both are 4-led and supported by 9, meaning they instinctively seek depth, authenticity, and a peaceful relational atmosphere. The critical divergence is in how each accesses the head center: {{A}}'s supporting 5 pulls inward toward quiet analysis and solitude, while {{B}}'s supporting 7 pushes outward toward stimulation and possibility. This creates a pairing of profound resonance and genuine friction in nearly equal measure.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both are 4-led, so mutual recognition of emotional depth and a hunger for meaning is nearly immediate — neither has to explain why surface-level connection feels hollow.
- The shared supporting 9 creates a gentle, non-intrusive relational rhythm; neither person steamrolls the other, and there's a natural warmth and ease in cohabiting emotional space.
- Creative and aesthetic sensibilities tend to align strongly, as the 4 core in both orients them toward beauty, nuance, and the poignant over the practical.
- When both are healthy, {{A}}'s reflective stillness and {{B}}'s buoyant openness form a genuinely complementary pair — grounded depth meets engaged aliveness.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 generates a genuine need for withdrawal, silence, and solitary processing; {{B}}'s supporting 7 generates restlessness and a pull toward new experiences and outward engagement, and these two drives work against each other at the pace level.
- {{B}} may unconsciously use 7 energy to sidestep painful emotions, which the 4-lead in {{A}} will notice and quietly resent as a form of inauthenticity.
- {{A}} can slip into protracted rumination and emotional heaviness that {{B}}'s 7 finds depleting; {{B}}'s optimistic reframing can feel dismissive to {{A}}.
- Both share the 9's conflict-avoidant gut, meaning neither will easily surface grievances — resentments can calcify beneath a pleasant exterior.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s 7-driven energy and forward focus as emotional avoidance or a refusal to sit with difficulty, when {{B}} may genuinely be coping or finding joy rather than fleeing.
- {{B}} is likely to read {{A}}'s 5-supported withdrawal as coldness, rejection, or loss of interest, when {{A}} is simply refueling in the way the 5 requires — privately, quietly, and without agenda.
- Both being 4-led means both are quietly tracking whether they feel truly *seen*; when each misreads the other's coping mechanism, the core 4 wound of feeling fundamentally misunderstood can activate simultaneously in both people, making repair harder.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should resist the 7's instinct to reframe or fast-forward past {{A}}'s heavier emotional states — staying present with discomfort is what {{A}}'s 4 needs to feel met.
- {{A}} should communicate withdrawal explicitly rather than going silent; a simple signal that space is needed (not a rupture) prevents {{B}}'s 4 from catastrophizing.
- Both should actively schedule direct conversations about tension — the shared supporting 9 will otherwise keep both nodding along until a much larger blowup occurs.
- When conflict does arise, {{A}} benefits from leading with feeling statements rather than analytical distance (5 defense), and {{B}} benefits from slowing down enough to feel the full weight of an issue rather than leaping to resolution (7 defense).

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}} offers {{B}} a model of how to stay with depth, tolerate emotional ambiguity, and build a rich inner life — qualities {{B}}'s 7 tends to race past in pursuit of the next thing.
- {{B}} offers {{A}} a genuine invitation out of the 4-5 withdrawal loop: {{B}}'s enthusiasm and engagement with the world can pull {{A}} toward participation, lightness, and forward movement.
- The shared 9 means both are capable of profound acceptance of each other's differences, which gives this pairing real staying power if both commit to voicing rather than suppressing needs.
- The highest growth edge for this pairing is learning that emotional depth ({{A}}'s gift) and emotional expansiveness ({{B}}'s gift) are not opposites — integrating both is what each is quietly working toward.

549-748.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share the same head center and a supporting 4, giving them an unexpected common ground in intellectual curiosity and a hunger for depth and authenticity. But their lead types pull in nearly opposite directions — {{A}}'s lead 5 contracts inward, conserving energy and knowledge, while {{B}}'s lead 7 expands outward, chasing stimulation and possibility. This is a pairing with genuine creative and intellectual chemistry, but one that requires real negotiation around pace, space, and emotional directness.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry a supporting 4, which means both genuinely crave meaning, authenticity, and depth — surface-level relating bores them equally.
- As head-center leads, both respect intellectual rigor and can spend hours in rich conceptual conversation without either getting restless or checked out.
- {{B}}'s 4 gives it access to emotional resonance that many 7s lack, and {{A}}'s 5 responds well to a partner who isn't just relentlessly cheerful — the depth feels real.
- {{A}}'s 9 brings a calm, non-judgmental presence that {{B}}'s 8 finds unexpectedly grounding rather than threatening.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 5 needs significant solitude and mental retreat to recharge; {{B}}'s lead 7 interprets withdrawal as disengagement or rejection and tends to escalate stimulation in response, which is exactly what {{A}} cannot tolerate.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 is direct, confrontational when challenged, and moves fast — {{A}}'s supporting 9 will quietly shut down or dissociate rather than match that energy, creating an invisible wall.
- {{A}} deliberates carefully and often needs time before committing to an idea or decision; {{B}}'s 7 lead finds this pace frustrating and may override it, which triggers {{A}}'s deeper 5 withdrawal.
- {{B}} avoids emotional pain by accelerating forward; {{A}} avoids depletion by going still — in crisis, they move in opposite directions.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s high energy and rapid topic-switching as shallowness or avoidance, not realizing that {{B}}'s 4 is doing genuine emotional processing underneath the movement. Meanwhile, {{B}} misreads {{A}}'s silence and withdrawal as coldness or withholding, not understanding that for a lead 5, quiet presence is often a form of intimacy. {{A}}'s 9 makes it conflict-averse, so real concerns often go unexpressed; {{B}}'s 8 then assumes everything is fine and pushes harder, which quietly exhausts {{A}}. Both can convince themselves they understand the other intellectually while missing the felt emotional reality entirely — a head-center trap they share.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should resist the urge to fill {{A}}'s silences — pauses are processing, not withdrawal, and crowding them will cost real access to {{A}}'s inner world.
- {{A}} needs to name needs explicitly; relying on {{B}} to intuit them won't work — {{B}}'s 7 lead is optimism-biased and will assume things are fine unless told otherwise.
- {{B}}'s 8 directness lands better with {{A}} when it's framed as curiosity rather than challenge — {{A}}'s 5 responds to questions, not pressure.
- {{A}} should practice voicing discomfort before it becomes full shutdown; the 9 pattern of going vague to avoid conflict will register as passive-aggression to {{B}}'s 8.
- Both benefit from scheduled, contained depth conversations — {{B}} needs a container that isn't all-day, and {{A}} needs to know there's an end point.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} challenges {{A}} to move — to act on ideas rather than endlessly refining them in isolation, and to engage with life's texture rather than only observing it from a safe distance. The lead 5's tendency toward hoarding experience is genuinely disrupted by {{B}}'s enthusiasm, in ways that can be liberating rather than just intrusive. In return, {{A}} offers {{B}} something rare: a steady, non-reactive presence that doesn't require {{B}} to perform or keep the energy up, giving the 7's underlying anxiety somewhere to quietly land. The shared 4 means that when both commit to authentic expression over their respective defense strategies — withdrawal for {{A}}, acceleration for {{B}} — they can access a surprisingly rare quality of mutual creative and emotional depth.

417-638.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both driven by a deep sense that the world ought to be better, but they pursue that conviction from very different psychological home bases — {{A}} leads with the heart's hunger for authentic self-expression, while {{B}} leads with the head's vigilance for safety, loyalty, and justice. This pairing can generate genuine passion and mutual respect, but it requires real work because {{A}}'s emotional individualism and {{B}}'s security-seeking collectivism pull in structurally opposite directions. When they align on shared values, they can be a formidable and inspiring team; when they don't, they risk a cycle of 4-driven withdrawal and 6-driven testing that erodes trust.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both share a gut-level moral seriousness: {{A}}'s supporting 1 brings a reformer's idealism, while {{B}}'s supporting 8 brings the protector's instinct for justice — they can feel immediately aligned on what matters.
- The 4 in {{A}} and the 6 in {{B}} both operate with high emotional intensity and a dislike of superficiality, so early conversations often feel rare and real.
- {{B}}'s 8 backing gives them a boldness that {{A}}'s lead 4 respects — this isn't someone who flinches from hard truths.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 and {{B}}'s supporting 3 both bring energy and forward momentum, keeping the relationship from stagnating in either anxiety or melancholy.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 4 needs to be recognized as singular and irreplaceable; {{B}}'s lead 6 tends to locate identity in alliances and shared commitments, which can feel to {{A}} like pressure to conform.
- {{B}}'s 6 tests loyalty through consistency and reliability — but {{A}}'s 4-driven emotional fluctuations and 7-supported restlessness read as instability, repeatedly triggering {{B}}'s anxiety.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 can become quietly critical when {{B}} doesn't meet an idealized standard, and {{B}}'s lead 6 is already primed to detect judgment — this combination can produce a low-grade, unspoken atmosphere of mutual evaluation.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 delivers feedback bluntly; {{A}}'s lead 4 is among the most sensitivity-prone types, and repeated directness without emotional attunement can feel like contempt rather than honesty.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s vigilance and coalition-building as a lack of trust in them specifically, when {{B}}'s 6 anxiety is usually generalized and not a personal verdict on {{A}}'s character.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s emotional withdrawal — a classic 4 move when feeling unseen — as rejection or disloyalty, when it's actually {{A}}'s way of self-regulating before they say something they'll regret.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 reframes pain into possibility as a coping mechanism; {{B}}'s lead 6 needs threats to be taken seriously first, so {{A}}'s optimism registers as dismissal rather than support.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 can shift into a performance mode that {{A}}'s authenticity-obsessed 4 finds hollow or even dishonest, misreading adaptive presentation as deception.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should lead with affirmation of {{A}}'s perspective before offering critique — the lead 4 opens up when they feel genuinely seen, and closes down entirely when they feel evaluated.
- {{A}} should offer {{B}} explicit, consistent reassurance rather than expecting trust to be assumed; the lead 6 needs behavioral evidence of reliability, not just feeling-based declarations of commitment.
- When conflict arises, {{A}} should name what they need emotionally before going quiet, and {{B}} should resist the 8-supported impulse to escalate in order to force resolution.
- Both benefit from agreeing on shared values explicitly — when {{A}}'s 1 and {{B}}'s 6 and 8 are all aimed at the same external cause, it redirects their moral energy outward rather than at each other.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} something genuinely useful: the lead 6's capacity for committed, sustained loyalty can show {{A}}'s 4 that belonging and uniqueness are not mutually exclusive — a real developmental gift for a type that chronically fears being ordinary if accepted.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} an equally important mirror: the lead 4's willingness to stand apart from the crowd and trust subjective inner knowing can help {{B}}'s 6 develop the self-authority it seeks from external sources.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 can help {{B}} move from scanning for threats to genuinely anticipating possibilities, softening the 6's catastrophizing without dismissing it.
- The deepest growth for this pairing happens when {{A}} lets {{B}}'s loyalty ground their restlessness, and {{B}} lets {{A}}'s individuality remind them that authentic conviction matters more than consensus.

368-613.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share two of their three types — the 3 and the 6 — but in reversed dominance, which creates a relationship that feels immediately familiar yet persistently misaligned in subtle ways. {{A}} leads with the 3's drive to achieve and project competence, while {{B}} leads with the 6's need for security, loyalty, and careful vetting of trust. This pairing has real potential for a committed, high-functioning alliance, but only if both people learn to see past the distortions their own lead type projects onto the other.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 3 and 6 energies give both {{A}} and {{B}} a mutual appreciation for hard work, reliability, and follow-through — this pairing rarely has to explain why loyalty matters.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 resonates strongly with {{B}}'s lead 6, meaning both understand vigilance and the weight of commitment in a way that feels validating.
- Both are oriented toward tangible results: {{A}}'s lead 3 pushes for visible wins, and {{B}}'s supporting 3 can match that drive once trust is established.
- The 8 in {{A}} and the 1 in {{B}} are both gut types with a strong sense of justice, giving them overlapping moral seriousness even if they express it differently.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is wired to manage image and adapt presentation strategically — exactly the kind of behavior that triggers {{B}}'s lead 6 alarm bells around authenticity and hidden agendas.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 brings bluntness and a push for power and control that can feel destabilizing to {{B}}'s 6, which craves a stable, predictable relational environment.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 introduces a moralizing, error-correcting energy that can feel like criticism of {{A}}'s competence — one of the deepest wounds for a lead 3.
- When stressed, {{A}} doubles down on image management and dominance (3 and 8 move to stress lines), while {{B}} becomes more suspicious and rigid (6 and 1 amplify doubt and rule-enforcement) — a combustible combination.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s 6-led caution and repeated questioning as a lack of confidence or an implicit accusation of untrustworthiness, when {{B}} is actually running standard loyalty protocols that apply to everyone. Conversely, {{B}} tends to interpret {{A}}'s 3-led image shaping and tactical framing as spin or evasion, when {{A}} is often just leading with their best face as a matter of habit, not deception. {{A}}'s 8 directness reads to {{B}} as aggression or a power grab; {{B}}'s 1 principled correction reads to {{A}} as a personal attack on their performance record. Both are convinced they are the more honest person in the room, which is the core misread.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should offer transparency proactively — naming their reasoning before {{B}}'s 6 has time to fill the gap with suspicion.
- {{B}} should surface doubts and concerns directly and early rather than holding them until they calcify into tests of loyalty that {{A}} doesn't know they're failing.
- When conflict arises, {{A}}'s supporting 8 should consciously dial back intensity; high-pressure delivery confirms {{B}}'s fear that something unsafe is happening.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 should be careful to separate factual feedback from moral judgment — {{A}}'s lead 3 hears criticism of their work as criticism of their worth.
- Both benefit from explicitly naming shared goals: grounding the conversation in outcomes rather than motives short-circuits their respective defense loops.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}} has a genuine developmental gift to offer {{B}}: the 3's capacity to project confidence and take decisive action can pull {{B}}'s lead 6 out of analysis paralysis and into effective forward motion. In return, {{B}}'s lead 6 offers {{A}} something the 3 quietly needs — a person who will not simply mirror back {{A}}'s projected image but will ask the harder questions about whether the goal is actually worth chasing. {{B}}'s supporting 1 can hold {{A}}'s 8 accountable without the relationship collapsing, and {{A}}'s 8 can model for {{B}} that confrontation doesn't always end in betrayal. Over time, this pairing can become one where {{A}} learns to lead with authenticity over performance, and {{B}} learns to lead with agency over anxiety.

136-315.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share the 1 and 3 as core types, creating a strong baseline of mutual respect for competence, standards, and results — but the order of dominance is nearly inverted, and that inversion is where most of the friction lives. {{A}} leads from principled gut-level correctness and uses achievement as a tool for doing good, while {{B}} leads from image-conscious heart-energy and uses the 1's standards as a quality-control mechanism rather than a moral identity. They can build a remarkably productive partnership, but they'll need to negotiate whose definition of 'right' governs shared work.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the 1 and 3 energies, so they share a language of high standards, diligence, and wanting to produce something genuinely excellent.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 appreciates {{B}}'s drive and polish; {{B}}'s supporting 1 respects {{A}}'s principled consistency.
- Both are doers who take quality seriously — they are unlikely to have to drag each other toward effort or accountability.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 and {{A}}'s supporting 6 both value information and preparation, so they tend to show up to conversations and projects ready.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 has a strong internalized sense of the 'right way,' and that rightness feels moral, not just strategic — {{B}}'s lead 3 is far more adaptable and will shift approach to achieve the outcome, which can read to {{A}} as cutting corners or lacking integrity.
- {{B}} may find {{A}}'s critiques relentless; where {{B}}'s supporting 1 activates selectively to maintain quality, {{A}}'s lead 1 is running a continuous internal audit.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 introduces a loyalty-and-risk-awareness lens that can slow decisions down; {{B}}'s supporting 5 prefers self-sufficient analysis and can find that anxiety-checking energy draining rather than prudent.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s image-awareness and adaptability as superficiality or pragmatic opportunism, missing that {{B}}'s lead 3 is genuinely invested in competence — the polish is not a substitute for substance.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s principled corrections as personal criticism or rigidity, not understanding that {{A}}'s lead 1 experiences moral standards as objective facts, not preferences.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 can create subtle loyalty-testing behavior — looking for signs of reliability and commitment — that {{B}}'s supporting 5 simply doesn't register as a relational signal, leading {{A}} to feel unseen and {{B}} to feel scrutinized without cause.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should distinguish between 'this violates a principle I hold' and 'this isn't how I would do it' before raising an objection with {{B}} — {{B}} responds to the former but tunes out the latter as perfectionism.
- {{B}} should make the standards and reasoning behind decisions visible to {{A}}, rather than just presenting polished outcomes; {{A}}'s lead 1 trusts the process, not just the result.
- When tension arises, both should name which type is driving the reaction — {{A}}'s 1 firing vs. {{A}}'s 6 anxiety vs. {{B}}'s 3 defensiveness vs. {{B}}'s 5 withdrawal are four very different conversations requiring different responses.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} a model of effective, adaptive action — the lead 3's ability to course-correct without guilt can loosen {{A}}'s 1-driven rigidity and help {{A}} separate self-worth from being right.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something the lead 3 genuinely needs but resists: a stable moral anchor that isn't contingent on outcomes or audience, which over time helps {{B}}'s supporting 1 deepen from quality-control into genuine integrity.
- The 5/6 head-center pairing is quietly complementary — {{A}}'s 6 brings relational vigilance and loyalty while {{B}}'s 5 brings detached analytical depth, and together they cover cognitive blind spots neither has alone.

514-827.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a head-meets-gut pairing — one leading with careful, internalized analysis and the other with raw, outward force. There is genuine intrigue here: {{A}}'s depth and unconventional inner world can captivate {{B}}, while {{B}}'s bold decisiveness can pull {{A}} out of endless deliberation. The relationship has real power, but it requires both people to consciously stretch toward the other's center of gravity.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 5 prizes competence and original thinking, and {{B}}'s 8-driven confidence and 7-fueled enthusiasm make for a genuinely stimulating intellectual partner.
- The shared gut energy between {{A}}'s supporting 1 and {{B}}'s lead 8 creates a quiet undercurrent of mutual respect for conviction — both know where they stand and why.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 genuinely wants to provide for people they care about, and {{A}}'s 5 — though private — responds warmly to loyalty that doesn't feel smothering.
- When {{A}}'s 4 opens up about its rich interior life, {{B}}'s appetite for intensity and authenticity means it will actually lean in rather than deflect.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 5 guards energy carefully and retreats to recharge; {{B}}'s lead 8 is expansive and instinctively fills space, which can register to {{A}} as an intrusion and to {{B}} as passive resistance.
- {{B}}'s 8 can be blunt to the point of bulldozing, which activates {{A}}'s supporting 1's inner critic and triggers a cold, withholding response rather than direct pushback.
- {{B}}'s supporting 7 craves novelty, momentum, and action, while {{A}}'s 5 needs to thoroughly map territory before moving — this mismatch in pacing can breed mutual frustration.
- {{A}}'s 4 experiences emotions as significant and meaning-laden; {{B}}'s 8 tends to distrust emotional display and may unconsciously dismiss what it reads as excessive sensitivity.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}}'s natural response under pressure is to withdraw and process silently — a 5-defense of detachment — but {{B}} reads this as stonewalling, withholding, or even passive aggression, which triggers {{B}}'s 8 combativeness. Conversely, {{B}}'s directness and high-volume presence is simply how the lead 8 operates, but {{A}} can mistake it for hostility or control, prompting further retreat. {{B}}'s supporting 2 expresses care through doing and giving, and when {{A}} quietly declines help or seems self-sufficient to a fault, {{B}} can feel rejected without understanding that {{A}}'s autonomy is about self-preservation, not rejection. {{A}}'s 4 communicates emotional truth through implication and atmosphere; {{B}}'s 8 needs things stated plainly or it simply won't register them.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should practice naming needs and reactions out loud in the moment — {{B}} is built for directness and actually responds best to plain statements, not signals.
- {{B}} should announce big energy before deploying it, and consciously create pauses after raising a topic so {{A}}'s 5 has time to process rather than shut down.
- When conflict arises, {{A}}'s 1 and {{B}}'s 8 share a genuine sense of fairness and integrity — anchoring disagreements to shared principles rather than personal wounds tends to defuse escalation.
- {{B}} should resist the 2's urge to solve or provide for {{A}} unsolicited; offering help as an option rather than an act works far better with a 5-led person.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} is one of the few people who can genuinely move {{A}} from the island of analysis into lived engagement — the lead 8's certainty and momentum creates external permission for {{A}}'s 5 to finally act on what it knows. In the other direction, {{A}}'s patient depth and the 4's insistence on emotional authenticity can slowly teach {{B}} that slowing down is not weakness, and that vulnerability doesn't compromise strength. {{A}}'s supporting 1 and {{B}}'s lead 8 can form a powerful ethical backbone in the relationship when both are healthy — a shared refusal to tolerate injustice or dishonesty. The core growth edge for this pairing is courage in different registers: {{A}} learning to be seen and confronted rather than disappearing, and {{B}} learning to be genuinely tender rather than just fiercely protective.

136-837.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both gut-center dominant, action-driven, and results-oriented, which creates an immediate sense of mutual respect and shared momentum. Their shared supporting 3 gives them common language around ambition and achievement. However, the 1-vs-8 lead difference is a significant fault line: {{A}} leads with principled correctness and restraint, while {{B}} leads with raw power and appetite for expansion, and those two orientations will collide regularly over how things should be done.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both gut-led, {{A}} by 1 and {{B}} by 8, means neither is afraid of hard decisions, confrontation, or putting in serious effort.
- The shared supporting 3 in the heart center creates genuine alignment around ambition, competence, and wanting to see tangible results.
- {{A}} respects {{B}}'s directness and capacity to get things done; {{B}} respects {{A}}'s integrity and reliability.
- When pointed at a shared mission, this pairing is one of the most productive imaginable — high standards meeting high drive.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 is fundamentally about doing things the *right* way — ethically and procedurally — while {{B}}'s lead 8 is about doing things *their* way, full stop, and may bypass rules when they feel like an obstacle.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 adds a layer of risk-awareness, loyalty to established structures, and concern for consequences, all of which {{B}}'s supporting 7 will routinely dismiss as excessive caution or pessimism.
- {{B}} will periodically cross {{A}}'s ethical lines and not understand why it matters; {{A}} will periodically pump the brakes on {{B}}'s momentum, which {{B}} experiences as obstruction.
- Both have strong inner critics in different modes — {{A}}'s is moralistic and internalized, {{B}}'s is externalizing — and neither adapts well to being told they're wrong.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} reads {{B}}'s boundary-pushing and rule-bending as recklessness or moral laziness, when {{B}} is simply operating from a gut confidence that power and results justify the path taken.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s corrections and standards-setting as nagging, rigidity, or timidity, when {{A}} is expressing genuine care about integrity and long-term trust.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 produces worry and a need to plan for risks; {{B}}'s supporting 7 reframes problems as opportunities and moves on fast — this gap makes {{A}} feel dismissed and {{B}} feel bogged down.
- Both use their shared supporting 3 to project competence, which can make it hard for either to admit uncertainty or error to the other.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} will land better with {{B}} by framing concerns in terms of outcomes and effectiveness rather than rules or ethics — {{B}} responds to 'this will blow up on us' far more than 'this isn't right.'
- {{B}} should resist the instinct to steamroll {{A}}'s objections; {{A}}'s supporting 6 is often scanning for real structural risks that {{B}}'s 7 optimism is filtering out.
- Both should watch for competitive dynamics activated by the shared 3 — image jockeying or credit disputes can poison an otherwise strong alliance.
- Direct, brief, and solution-focused communication works best for both; {{A}} should compress the moral framing and {{B}} should compress the bluster.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} a genuinely expansive model of what bold, unapologetic action looks like, which can help {{A}}'s lead 1 loosen its grip on perfectionistic restraint and move faster toward impact.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something rare: a principled accountability partner who won't be intimidated or co-opted, which helps {{B}}'s lead 8 develop the ethical grounding it genuinely needs for sustainable leadership.
- The stress and growth lines of 1 (stress to 4, growth to 7) and 8 (stress to 5, growth to 2) don't directly mirror each other, meaning each will grow in directions the other finds somewhat foreign — this is friction but also genuine broadening.
- At their best, {{A}} provides the conscience and {{B}} provides the engine; the pairing only reaches that potential when both trust the other's core intention.

269-748.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a study in complementary energy — one leads from the heart with warmth, loyalty, and a drive to nurture, while the other leads from the head with enthusiasm, vision, and a push toward experience. At their best, they balance each other beautifully: {{A}} grounds {{B}}'s restless forward motion, and {{B}} liberates {{A}} from over-cautious self-sacrifice. The real challenge lies in mismatched needs around security, reciprocity, and emotional pacing.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 is naturally generous and attuned to others' needs, which {{B}}'s supporting 4 genuinely receives and appreciates — depth meets warmth here.
- {{B}}'s lead 7 brings adventure and levity that {{A}}'s supporting 9 finds genuinely relaxing; {{A}} can follow {{B}}'s energy without needing to lead it.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 and {{B}}'s supporting 8 share a loyalty-and-protection instinct — once trust is established, both are fiercely committed.
- Both have a social generosity (2's giving, 7's enthusiasm for shared experience) that makes the relationship feel alive and outward-facing.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 needs to feel needed and appreciated; {{B}}'s lead 7 is self-referential by default and can glide past emotional reciprocity without noticing the gap it leaves.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 craves consistency and reassurance, while {{B}}'s lead 7 resists being pinned to commitments — this mismatch can quietly erode {{A}}'s sense of security.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 will be blunt and confrontational when pushed; {{A}}'s supporting 9 will absorb it in the moment and simmer, eventually either over-accommodating or erupting.
- {{A}} tends to accumulate unspoken grievances (2 and 9 pattern), while {{B}} moves on fast (7 pattern) and may never realize a wound was opened.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} often reads {{B}}'s enthusiasm as deep relational investment, when for a lead 7 it may simply be the energy of the present moment — this sets {{A}} up for repeated disappointment.
- {{B}} can misread {{A}}'s attentiveness and loyalty (lead 2, supporting 6) as clinginess or an attempt to control, when {{A}} is actually expressing care and seeking reassurance.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 anxiety about reliability can look like mistrust to {{B}}'s supporting 8, triggering a defensive or dismissive response that shuts down the very conversation {{A}} needs.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 sometimes wants raw emotional honesty, but {{A}}'s 9 tends to smooth things over — {{B}} may experience this as emotional shallowness rather than peace-keeping.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should name needs directly and early rather than hinting and hoping {{B}} notices — lead 7 is not wired to read between the lines, and waiting breeds resentment.
- {{B}} should offer explicit, specific appreciation to {{A}}; a lead 2 doesn't just want to be liked, they need to know their care lands and matters.
- When {{A}}'s supporting 6 raises a concern, {{B}} should resist the impulse (8 support) to steamroll it — slowing down to validate the worry costs little and builds the security {{A}} needs to stay open.
- {{A}} can help the conversation by distinguishing between 6-driven anxiety (hypothetical fears) and genuine relational feedback, so {{B}} knows when to reassure versus when to actually reckon with something.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} is a genuine catalyst for {{A}}: the lead 7's refusal to over-caretake, combined with the 8's directness, can push {{A}} to stop self-erasing and actually advocate for their own desires — a core growth edge for lead 2.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something rare: a steady, non-judgmental presence (9 support) that doesn't flinch at {{B}}'s intensity, and a loyalty (6 support) that anchors the relationship against the 7's tendency to always chase the next thing.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 benefits from {{A}}'s warmth in ways the 4 often struggles to ask for — {{A}} models that vulnerability can be met with care rather than rejection.
- Over time, if both mature, {{A}} learns to receive as well as give, and {{B}} learns to stay present long enough to build something lasting — each becoming more whole through the friction the other provides.

217-548.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} represent a classic heart-meets-head pairing — {{A}}'s lead 2 moves toward people with warmth, service, and relational energy, while {{B}}'s lead 5 moves away from people to preserve autonomy and mental space. The attraction is real: each offers what the other lacks. But the same asymmetry that creates chemistry also generates persistent friction around closeness, reciprocity, and emotional expression.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 brings intellectual curiosity and enthusiasm that genuinely engages {{B}}'s lead 5 — both enjoy the exchange of ideas, and {{B}} respects a mind that can keep up.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 carries an emotional depth and authenticity that {{A}}'s lead 2 finds compelling and worth nurturing — {{A}} loves having someone genuinely complex to care for.
- The gut-center pairing of {{A}}'s supporting 1 and {{B}}'s supporting 8 gives the relationship a shared instinct for integrity and directness — both dislike superficiality and value substance.
- {{B}}'s 4 quietly longs to be truly seen, and {{A}}'s lead 2 is exceptionally good at exactly that kind of attentive, personalized care.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 is fundamentally oriented toward relational closeness and needs to feel needed and appreciated; {{B}}'s lead 5 instinctively conserves energy and guards personal space, making the closeness {{A}} craves feel like a drain to {{B}}.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 can be blunt to the point of harshness, which triggers {{A}}'s underlying 1 into quiet moral indignation or wounded withdrawal rather than open confrontation.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 can moralize or express disappointment when standards aren't met; {{B}}'s lead 5 experiences this as intrusive judgment and may retreat further into detachment.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 wants lightness, future-planning, and social engagement — activities that {{B}}'s 5-4 combination often finds exhausting or superficial.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s helpfulness through the lead-5 lens: a 5 is alert to dependency dynamics and may interpret {{A}}'s giving as an implicit demand for reciprocity, feeling manipulated even when {{A}}'s motivation is genuinely generous.
- {{A}} reads {{B}}'s withdrawal as emotional rejection or indifference, when for a lead 5, pulling back is simply self-regulation — not a verdict on the relationship.
- {{A}}'s indirect communication style (hinting at needs, giving in order to receive) is opaque to {{B}}'s 5-8 combination, which values explicit, economical communication and has little patience for emotional subtext.
- {{B}}'s emotional restraint registers to {{A}}'s lead 2 as ingratitude or coldness, while {{B}} assumes that doing its own thing quietly is a perfectly respectful form of coexistence.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should name needs directly and specifically — the lead-2 habit of giving while hoping others intuit what's needed will consistently fail with a lead 5 who takes words at face value.
- {{B}} should make a practice of verbal acknowledgment: a brief, sincere expression of appreciation lands far more powerfully for {{A}}'s lead 2 than any amount of quietly valued presence.
- {{A}} should negotiate explicit "alone time" agreements rather than interpreting {{B}}'s withdrawal reactively — framing space as a gift rather than a withdrawal helps {{A}}'s 2 reframe the dynamic.
- {{B}} should run the supporting 8's directness through the 4's empathy filter before delivering feedback, especially on topics that touch {{A}}'s sense of worth or care.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} something the lead 2 rarely gets: a relationship where help is not the currency of connection, which can push {{A}} toward healthier self-differentiation and genuine self-care rather than compulsive giving.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} a consistent, warm relational presence that can slowly make emotional vulnerability feel safer — over time {{B}}'s supporting 4 may open more fully with someone who has demonstrated sustained care without agenda.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 and {{B}}'s supporting 4 share an idealistic streak and a hunger for authenticity that, when both are functioning well, creates a deeply principled and meaningful bond.
- The central developmental challenge is reciprocity: {{A}} must learn that not everyone expresses care through emotional attunement, and {{B}} must learn that connection requires giving something back — even when it costs energy.

259-369.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a heart-center dominance and a mutual 9 undercurrent, which creates genuine warmth, social ease, and a shared dislike of unnecessary conflict. However, their heart types express very differently — {{A}}'s lead 2 orients around giving and relational closeness, while {{B}}'s lead 3 orients around achieving and image — and this gap is the central tension of the pairing. With awareness, they offer each other meaningful growth: {{A}} can ground {{B}} in authentic connection, and {{B}} can push {{A}} toward self-worth that isn't contingent on being needed.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both share a supporting 9, which means neither person defaults to aggression; there's a natural ease and low-friction baseline in everyday interaction.
- {{A}}'s lead 2 loves to support and encourage, and {{B}}'s lead 3 genuinely thrives when someone believes in them — this dynamic can feel mutually energizing.
- {{B}}'s supporting 6 craves trustworthy allies, and {{A}}'s 2-led warmth and consistency reads as deeply reassuring to that part of {{B}}.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 brings analytical depth that can help {{B}}'s 6 think through anxieties more clearly rather than spinning in worst-case scenarios.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 3 is wired for efficiency, output, and forward momentum; {{A}}'s lead 2 is wired for emotional attunement and reciprocal care, and {{B}} can feel too task-focused to truly satisfy {{A}}'s relational hunger.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 periodically needs to withdraw and recharge in solitude, which can confuse or subtly sting {{B}}'s lead 3, who tends to read disengagement as a signal that something is wrong.
- Both suppress their own emotional needs — {{A}} by over-giving to avoid asking, {{B}} by performing competence to avoid vulnerability — which means genuine emotional honesty can be chronically deferred between them.
- {{B}}'s 3-driven image management may strike {{A}}'s 2 as shallow or self-serving, especially when {{A}} is quietly hoping for acknowledgment that never comes.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to interpret {{B}}'s achievement-focus as a sign of not caring enough about the relationship, when in reality {{B}}'s lead 3 is often expressing love through doing and succeeding — it just doesn't look like the emotional presence {{A}} needs. Conversely, {{B}} may read {{A}}'s indirect style of expressing needs — hinting through helpfulness rather than asking directly — as passive or manipulative, when {{A}} genuinely hasn't been taught that it's safe to simply ask. The shared 9 supporting type in both can compound this: both are conflict-avoidant enough to let these misreadings accumulate rather than address them head-on.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should practice naming needs explicitly rather than signaling them through acts of service; {{B}}'s lead 3 responds to clarity, not emotional subtext.
- {{B}} should build in intentional moments of undistracted presence with {{A}} — the lead 3's natural mode of multitasking and future-focus reads as dismissiveness to {{A}}'s 2.
- When {{B}}'s supporting 6 enters an anxious loop, {{A}}'s supporting 5 can be a genuinely calming resource — but {{A}} should offer analysis as a gift, not as a correction.
- Both should agree on a low-stakes signal for when {{A}}'s 5 needs withdrawal time, so {{B}}'s 3 doesn't interpret it as rejection.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}}'s lead 3 offers {{A}} something the lead 2 quietly needs but struggles to claim: a model of self-referential worth, where value isn't earned through service to others. Watching {{B}} pursue goals for their own sake can gradually loosen {{A}}'s core belief that lovability depends on usefulness. In the other direction, {{A}}'s 2-led relational attunement invites {{B}} into a depth of authentic connection that the lead 3 often bypasses in favor of performance — {{A}} is one of the rare people who may actually see behind {{B}}'s achieved image and not flinch. If both can tolerate the discomfort of being genuinely known rather than strategically presented, this pairing has real transformative potential.

146-845.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both gut-dominant types who lead with strong conviction and a deep need to act on their values — but they express that drive in nearly opposite ways. {{A}}'s 1 lead channels gut energy into self-correction, principled restraint, and a drive toward moral improvement, while {{B}}'s 8 lead channels it outward as power, confrontation, and command of their environment. The shared 4 supporting type gives both an undercurrent of emotional intensity and a hunger for authenticity that can create genuine intimacy — but the 1-vs-8 axis is one of the more combustible pairings in the enneagram, and this relationship will require real self-awareness from both.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the shared 4 supporting type, which means beneath the surface there is real emotional depth, a distaste for pretense, and a desire to be seen and known — this creates an unusual intimacy between two otherwise tough-edged types.
- Both are gut-led and action-oriented; neither is passive, and both respect people who have clear convictions and stand behind them.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 and {{A}}'s supporting 6 both value getting to the truth of things, so intellectually they can enjoy rigorous, unvarnished debate without needing to soften every edge.
- When aligned on a shared cause or project, this pairing can be formidable — {{A}}'s principled rigor and {{B}}'s forceful execution complement each other well.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- The core friction is structural: {{A}}'s lead 1 is self-monitoring and morally corrective, and it will almost inevitably try to hold {{B}}'s lead 8 accountable to a standard — which is exactly the dynamic an 8 resists most viscerally.
- {{A}} represses and redirects anger into criticism and perfectionism; {{B}} expresses anger directly and without much filtering, which {{A}}'s 1 is likely to experience as an assault on order and decency.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 needs loyalty, reliability, and some reassurance — {{B}}'s 8 lead reads dependency or anxiety-driven questioning as weakness and may respond with impatience or dismissiveness.
- Both types are stubborn in the gut center sense: neither yields easily, and when they lock horns over a matter of principle ({{A}}) or authority ({{B}}), standoffs can last.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to experience {{B}} as reckless, unprincipled, or domineering, not recognizing that {{B}}'s 8 lead operates from a deep personal code of loyalty and strength — it just doesn't look like {{A}}'s structured ethical framework.
- {{B}} is likely to experience {{A}} as rigid, preachy, or self-righteous, not recognizing that {{A}}'s 1-and-6 combination means the criticism comes from genuine anxiety about doing things right, not from a desire to control.
- When {{B}}'s supporting 5 causes them to withdraw and go quiet for processing, {{A}}'s supporting 6 interprets the silence as disengagement or broken trust — and may escalate precisely when {{B}} needs space.
- {{A}} may not see that {{B}}'s bluntness is a form of respect; {{B}} may not see that {{A}}'s correction is a form of care.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the urge to lead with what {{B}} is doing wrong — 8s do not open up under moral pressure; framing concerns in terms of shared values or direct impact works far better than implied critique.
- {{B}} should slow down enough to acknowledge {{A}}'s principles explicitly before pushing back; dismissing the framework outright will trigger {{A}}'s 1 defensiveness and shut down real dialogue.
- Both share the 4 supporting type — when conversations feel stuck, shifting toward honest emotional disclosure (what this actually means to each person, not just what is correct or who wins) can unlock the exchange.
- {{A}}'s 6 tendency to over-question and seek reassurance should be named rather than acted out; {{B}}'s 8 tendency toward ultimatums or volume should be reined in before it becomes the only thing {{A}} can hear.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} a model of owning gut instinct and anger directly rather than sublimating it into perfectionism — {{A}}'s 1 growth edge is learning that righteous anger can be expressed cleanly rather than managed into resentment.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} a model of self-restraint and ethical accountability — {{B}}'s 8 growth edge is recognizing that structures and principles are not threats to autonomy but can actually expand what's possible.
- The shared 4 supporting type means both are capable of genuine vulnerability when the defensive layers come down, and those moments can be the deepest points of contact in the relationship.
- This pairing won't be easy, but it's not shallow either — if both commit to the friction rather than fleeing it or winning it, each will become a more integrated version of themselves.

513-713.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a fascinating head-center pairing who share the same supporting types (3 and 1) but lead from opposite ends of the head triad — {{A}} through deep focused withdrawal and {{B}} through expansive outward engagement. Their shared 3 and 1 give them genuine common ground in ambition, competence, and high standards, but their lead types create a persistent tension between depth and breadth, conservation and expansion. This pairing has strong intellectual chemistry but requires real effort to bridge fundamentally different rhythms and information-processing styles.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both lead with head-center energy, so intellectual respect comes quickly — each recognizes the other as someone who thinks seriously.
- Supporting 3 in both means a shared drive for results, visible competence, and real-world output; neither is content to just theorize.
- Supporting 1 in both creates alignment around standards, quality, and doing things the right way — shared frustration with sloppiness bonds them.
- When a complex problem needs solving, this pair can be formidable: {{A}} provides depth and precision while {{B}} generates options and momentum.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 5 conserves energy, retreats to process, and resists overstimulation; {{B}}'s lead 7 generates stimulation, resists stillness, and keeps the pace relentlessly high — these rhythms directly clash.
- {{B}} experiences {{A}}'s withdrawal as withholding or passive disengagement; {{A}} experiences {{B}}'s rapid pivoting as an exhausting drain that prevents any topic from being fully resolved.
- Both have supporting 1, which means both can be quietly critical — but when directed at each other, their shared perfectionism can turn into mutual fault-finding with no easy off-ramp.
- {{A}}'s fear of depletion and {{B}}'s fear of being trapped or bored are structurally opposed: the situations that feel safe to one feel suffocating to the other.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} frequently reads {{B}}'s breadth-seeking as superficiality or lack of rigor, when in fact {{B}}'s lead 7 is genuinely synthesizing patterns across domains — just at a speed {{A}} finds uncomfortably incomplete.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s need for solitude and deliberate pace as aloofness or arrogance, missing that lead-5 withdrawal is how {{A}} actually prepares to contribute meaningfully.
- Shared supporting 3 means both care about how competence is perceived, but they signal it differently: {{A}} signals it through demonstrated mastery; {{B}} signals it through enthusiasm and vision — each can quietly dismiss the other's style as show.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should give {{A}} advance notice of topics before discussions — a lead 5 who arrives prepared is a fully present partner; one caught off guard tends to close down.
- {{A}} should practice naming when they're processing rather than just going quiet — {{B}}'s lead 7 fills silence with new ideas, which derails the depth {{A}} was working toward.
- When the shared supporting 1 surfaces as criticism, both should explicitly separate 'this standard matters to me' from 'you are failing' — the former invites collaboration, the latter triggers defensiveness in both directions.
- Agree on a working pace for projects: allow {{B}} to map wide first, then give {{A}} structured time to go deep before converging on decisions.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} genuine growth by modeling that engagement with the world doesn't have to be depleting — a healthy lead 7's enthusiasm can show {{A}} that staying in the room is worth it.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something harder but more valuable: the experience of slowing down long enough to actually finish a thought, which {{B}}'s lead 7 structurally avoids by moving toward the next stimulus.
- Their shared 1 is the most stable bridge — when both orient toward a principled shared goal rather than their own preferred style, the 5's depth and the 7's range become genuinely complementary rather than competitive.

258-835.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share the raw materials of 5 and 8, but their lead types place them in fundamentally different orientations: {{A}} leads with the heart's need for connection and meaning, while {{B}} leads with the gut's drive for control and impact. This creates a pairing with genuine chemistry — directness, intelligence, and competence are values both hold — but also real tension around emotional reciprocity and power dynamics. At their best they form a formidable team; at their worst, a quiet battle for leverage.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the 5's analytical mind as a supporting type, so intellectual respect comes easily — these two can trade sharp observations without needing to simplify for each other.
- The shared 8 energy means neither person flinches from bluntness; conflict doesn't destabilize the relationship the way it might in softer pairings.
- {{A}}'s 2-lead drives a genuine desire to support {{B}}'s ambitions, and {{B}}'s 8-lead deeply values loyalty and capability in a partner — {{A}} offers both.
- There is a shared disdain for pretense: {{A}}'s 5 wants truth, {{B}}'s 8 demands it.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 needs to feel needed and emotionally seen; {{B}}'s lead 8 is built around self-sufficiency and can unconsciously signal that emotional needs are burdens.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 introduces an achievement-and-image layer that can make {{A}} feel like a resource rather than a partner — the 2's core fear of being unloved for who they are, not what they do, gets activated here.
- {{A}}'s 2 can become quietly manipulative when its needs go unmet (using help as a lever), and {{B}}'s 8 has a hair-trigger for perceived control or coercion — this combination can escalate fast.
- {{B}} leads from the gut and acts first; {{A}}'s 5 support wants to analyze before committing, creating friction around pace and decision-making.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} expresses love through attentiveness and service, and reads emotional acknowledgment as the currency of care; {{B}} expresses care through protection, directness, and showing up in a crisis — and may genuinely not register that {{A}} is keeping score. Meanwhile, {{B}} can misread {{A}}'s helping behavior as conditional or transactional (because sometimes, with a 2, it is), which triggers {{B}}'s 8-lead suspicion of hidden agendas. {{A}} in turn may interpret {{B}}'s bluntness and self-reliance as coldness or rejection, when {{B}} is simply operating from a gut-center worldview where emotions are expressed through action, not words.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should lead with directness when expressing needs — {{B}}'s 8 responds to plain, strong asks and is genuinely put off by hinting or emotional indirection.
- {{B}} should build in explicit, specific appreciation for what {{A}} contributes; {{A}}'s lead 2 doesn't just want to feel useful, it wants to feel *valued*, and {{B}}'s 8 tends to assume competence is its own reward.
- When tension rises, {{A}} should resist the 2's move toward self-sacrifice as a manipulation strategy; {{B}} will call it out, and it will damage trust.
- {{B}} can invite {{A}}'s 5 into problem-solving conversations — this engages {{A}} on neutral intellectual ground and lowers the emotional temperature.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} offers {{A}} a model of leading from personal authority rather than approval — spending time with {{B}}'s unapologetic 8 energy can help {{A}} access their own supporting 8 more cleanly, asserting without needing to frame it as self-sacrifice. In the other direction, {{A}}'s lead 2, when healthy, models genuine attunement and relational intelligence that {{B}}'s supporting 3 often bypasses in favor of performance; {{A}} can draw {{B}} into authentic emotional connection rather than transactional efficiency. The growth edge for both is the same underneath: learning that vulnerability and strength are not opposites.

358-548.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share two of three tritype numbers — the 5 and the 8 — giving them a strong common foundation in intellectual rigor and assertive directness. However, their lead types pull in meaningfully different directions: {{A}}'s lead 3 is goal-oriented, adaptive, and image-aware, while {{B}}'s lead 5 is knowledge-driven, detached, and depth-seeking. This pairing has real collaborative power but requires both to resist the temptation to dismiss what the other values most.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 5 creates genuine intellectual chemistry — both respect competence, hate sloppy thinking, and can engage in substantive, high-level analysis together.
- The shared 8 means neither person flinches from directness or conflict; there is a refreshing lack of performance around politeness, and disagreements can be aired cleanly.
- Both are fundamentally independent and self-reliant, so neither will feel smothered or demand more from the other than they can give.
- When pointed at a common problem, {{A}}'s 3-driven execution combines powerfully with {{B}}'s 5-driven depth of research — a natural strategist-operator pairing.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is wired for speed, efficiency, and results, often prioritizing what works over what is fully understood; {{B}}'s lead 5 refuses to act before the picture is complete, which {{A}} can experience as paralysis.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 introduces a hunger for authenticity and emotional meaning that sits in direct tension with {{A}}'s 3-led image management — {{B}} will detect when {{A}} is performing rather than being genuine, and will withdraw.
- {{A}} tends to calibrate behavior to context (a 3 hallmark), which can read to {{B}} as inconsistency or even inauthenticity, triggering the 4's distrust of anything that seems constructed.
- The shared 8 can compound friction: when both are stressed, the confrontational edge of 8 amplifies rather than bridges the 3-vs-5 tension.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to misread {{B}}'s withdrawal and long processing times as aloofness, disinterest, or even passive resistance — when in reality {{B}}'s lead 5 genuinely needs solitude to think, and the 4 needs space to feel.
- {{B}} is likely to misread {{A}}'s adaptability and results-focus as superficiality or self-promotion, missing that for a lead 3, achieving outcomes *is* how care, competence, and value are expressed — it is not merely performance.
- {{A}} may not realize how much {{B}}'s supporting 4 needs to feel that the relationship has depth and meaning beyond utility, and may inadvertently signal that {{B}} is just a resource.
- {{B}} may not appreciate that {{A}}'s 3-led shape-shifting is a genuine strength, not dishonesty — context-sensitivity and {{A}} may experience {{B}}'s insistence on slow, principled depth as impractical rigidity.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should give {{B}} uninterrupted processing time before expecting a response — pinging or pushing for quick answers activates {{B}}'s 5-lead withdrawal reflex and shuts the conversation down.
- {{B}} should name needs explicitly rather than retreating: the shared 8 means {{A}} can handle directness, and vague emotional signals from the 4 will confuse or frustrate {{A}}'s 3.
- Both should lean on the 8 they share as a communication channel — frank, bottom-line conversation without excessive hedging suits both of them far better than diplomatic tip-toeing.
- {{A}} benefits from occasionally signaling genuine curiosity rather than just competence; {{B}} benefits from occasionally signaling commitment to a shared goal rather than just individual understanding.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}} in integration (3 moving toward 6) becomes more genuinely collaborative, loyal, and willing to question their own assumptions — qualities {{B}} naturally models through the 5's epistemically humble depth-seeking.
- {{B}} in integration (5 moving toward 8) becomes more decisive, embodied, and willing to act before all information is in — a quality {{A}}'s lead 3 and supporting 8 can actively demonstrate and invite.
- The shared 8 acts as a genuine growth meeting point: at their best, both are frank, capable, and willing to act on hard truths, and that mutual respect for strength can hold the relationship together through friction.
