- {{A}} carries a triple intensity: the moral urgency of 1, the emotional sensitivity of 4, and the anxious vigilance of 6; {{B}}'s 5 instinctively retreats when emotional temperature rises, which only escalates {{A}}'s anxiety.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 resists being pushed or reformed; {{A}}'s lead 1 will interpret this passive resistance as laziness or evasion rather than a genuine need for autonomy.
- {{B}}'s 5-led self-sufficiency can make {{A}}'s supporting 6 feel perpetually unsure of where they stand in the relationship.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} reads {{B}}'s withdrawal and emotional economy as indifference or hidden rejection — the supporting 6 scans for signs of disloyalty and {{B}}'s characteristic detachment supplies plenty of false positives.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s criticism and high standards as controlling rigidity rather than recognizing them as expressions of care rooted in the lead 1's core belief that improvement equals love.
- When {{A}}'s supporting 4 needs to feel deeply understood, {{B}}'s lead 5 responds with analysis and problem-solving — technically useful, emotionally deflating.
- {{B}} may not realize that {{A}}'s bluntness is not hostility; {{A}} may not realize that {{B}}'s silence is not passive aggression.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should signal intellectual respect before raising a criticism — {{B}}'s lead 5 is far more receptive when it doesn't feel evaluated or lectured at.
- {{B}} should offer small, explicit verbal confirmations of loyalty and regard; this costs {{B}} little but directly soothes {{A}}'s supporting 6 without requiring emotional performance.
- {{A}} can ask {{B}} for a specific amount of thinking time before expecting a response on charged topics — respecting {{B}}'s processing style reduces the shutdown spiral.
- {{B}} should resist the temptation to minimize {{A}}'s emotional concerns with pure logic; naming the feeling before the solution is the entry point for the supporting 4.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}} has the most to learn from {{B}}'s capacity for non-attachment — the supporting 9 in {{B}} models a groundedness that {{A}}'s lead 1 and anxious supporting 6 genuinely need, pointing toward loosening the grip on how things "should" be. {{B}} has the most to learn from {{A}}'s moral courage and willingness to take a stand, something {{B}}'s supporting 9 tends to avoid; {{A}} models that values are worth defending even at personal cost. The growth edge lives in the heart layer: {{A}}'s supporting 4 and {{B}}'s supporting 2 can build a quietly profound emotional intimacy, but only if both types resist their respective defaults — {{A}} resisting the urge to criticize, {{B}} resisting the urge to disappear.

528-738.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both head-center leads who share a gutsy, assertive 8 in the body center, giving this pairing real directness and mutual respect for competence. But where {{A}} pulls inward to think, conserve, and strategize, {{B}} pushes outward to explore, expand, and execute — creating a productive but sometimes exhausting tension between depth and breadth. The shared 8 energy is the relationship's strongest anchor; the 5-vs-7 head-center clash is its sharpest fault line.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared supporting 8 is the bedrock: both {{A}} and {{B}} value directness, dislike pretense, and respect people who hold their ground — conversations rarely devolve into passive-aggression.
- Both are intellectually driven and competence-oriented; {{A}}'s lead 5 and {{B}}'s supporting 3 both prize mastery, making them genuinely stimulating to each other.
- When a problem needs solving, this pair is formidable — {{A}} brings deep analytical rigor and {{B}} brings rapid pattern-recognition and momentum.
- Neither carries a 9 in their tritype, so conflict doesn't get buried; issues surface and get addressed, which builds trust over time.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 5 guards energy carefully and needs substantial alone time to process; {{B}}'s lead 7 is high-stimulus and interprets withdrawal as rejection or disinterest.
- {{B}} moves fast, pivots constantly, and hates feeling trapped in a single track — {{A}} finds this scattered and intellectually unsatisfying, preferring to go deep before moving on.
- Both carry 8 assertiveness, which is unifying in shared goals but combustible when they disagree: neither naturally yields, and power struggles can escalate quickly.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 wants visible wins and external validation; {{A}}'s supporting 2 gives care selectively and privately, leaving {{B}} sometimes feeling unseen rather than celebrated.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} reads {{B}}'s enthusiasm and fast-moving energy as superficiality or avoidance — the 5's core fear of being drained leads them to interpret {{B}}'s expansiveness as a drain rather than a contribution. {{B}}, meanwhile, reads {{A}}'s careful observation and silence as coldness or gatekeeping, not recognizing that {{A}}'s supporting 2 is quietly tracking {{B}}'s wellbeing even when it isn't announced. {{A}} may not understand that {{B}}'s 7-led reframing and optimism is a genuine coping structure, not intellectual dishonesty; {{B}} may not understand that {{A}}'s boundaries around time and information are self-protective, not controlling. Both can accidentally weaponize their 8 energy — {{A}} through blunt withholding, {{B}} through overwhelming confrontation — and each tends to attribute the other's defense style to bad intent.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should give {{A}} explicit processing time before expecting a response on anything significant — pressing for immediate answers activates {{A}}'s 5-withdrawal and shuts the conversation down.
- {{A}} should share more of the internal reasoning process out loud; {{B}}'s lead 7 connects through idea exchange, and silence feels like exclusion rather than respect.
- When conflict arises, both should name the shared 8 dynamic explicitly — agree on a "cool-down and return" norm before discussions hit the power-struggle threshold.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 genuinely wants to help; {{B}} should let that care land rather than deflecting it with 7-led humor or 3-led self-sufficiency.
- {{B}} can earn {{A}}'s deeper trust by demonstrating follow-through, not just enthusiasm — the 5 in {{A}} is watching to see if {{B}} can be relied upon, not just inspired by.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}} challenges {{B}} to slow down, go deeper, and tolerate the discomfort of sitting with a single idea long enough to truly understand it — a direct antidote to 7's avoidance of depth. {{B}} challenges {{A}} to take action before every variable is controlled for, to trust that imperfect engagement is more valuable than perfect preparation — a direct antidote to 5's hoarding of self. The shared 8 means neither will let the other coast in comfort, which is ultimately a gift: this relationship doesn't allow stagnation. If both can resist using their 8 assertiveness to dominate rather than to build, and if {{A}} can stay open rather than retreating and {{B}} can stay present rather than escaping, this pairing has serious potential to push both people into genuinely integrated versions of themselves.

147-315.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both high-standards, driven individuals who share the Type 1 energy — {{A}} as lead, {{B}} as a supporting anchor — giving them a genuine common language around quality and doing things right. However, {{A}}'s gut-led moral idealism and emotional depth (via the 4) frequently collides with {{B}}'s heart-led pragmatism and image-consciousness, creating tension between authenticity and effectiveness. This pairing has real productive potential, but only if both are willing to question their own blind spots rather than quietly resenting each other's approach.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared Type 1 undercurrent means both {{A}} and {{B}} hold high standards and feel internal pressure to do work correctly — they recognize this drive in each other instantly.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 brings infectious enthusiasm and future-oriented energy that fuels {{B}}'s lead 3 achievement momentum, making them a naturally generative pair when pointed at a goal.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 offers the analytical rigor and quiet competence that {{A}}'s idealism genuinely respects and benefits from.
- Both dislike sloppiness — whether in thinking, craft, or values — and that mutual intolerance for mediocrity creates a strong working bond.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 operates from fixed moral conviction; {{B}}'s lead 3 is adaptive and pragmatic, willing to shift approach to reach an outcome. {{A}} can read this as unprincipled; {{B}} can read {{A}} as self-righteous.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 craves emotional authenticity and meaning beneath the surface. {{B}}'s lead 3 curates a polished, competent image that the 4 finds suspect or hollow.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 adds its own critical voice, meaning when these two disagree on standards, neither is inclined to back down — it can become a quiet war of correctness.
- {{A}}'s 7 wants expansive possibility and experimentation; {{B}}'s 5 wants precision and mastery, creating friction around how broadly or deeply to invest energy.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to interpret {{B}}'s image-management and strategic adaptability as a lack of integrity or genuine conviction, when in reality {{B}}'s lead 3 uses persona as a tool for effectiveness, not as deception — it's a feature, not a character flaw. Conversely, {{B}} reads {{A}}'s principled rigidity and emotional intensity (especially from the 4) as impractical idealism or, worse, moral superiority, missing that {{A}}'s lead 1 feels a genuine, almost physical discomfort when standards or values are compromised. {{B}} also tends to underestimate how much {{A}}'s 4 needs to feel that the relationship or collaboration has genuine depth and meaning, not just smooth execution — and {{A}} underestimates how much {{B}}'s 3 needs recognition and forward movement to feel safe.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should frame critiques as shared standards rather than moral verdicts — "this doesn't meet what we both care about" lands far better with {{B}}'s lead 3 than an implied accusation of ethical failure.
- {{B}} should offer {{A}} glimpses of genuine conviction and personal investment, not just competence reports — the lead 1 needs to know {{B}} actually cares, not just performs caring.
- {{A}} needs to monitor 4-driven emotional escalation; when depth-seeking becomes intensity, {{B}}'s 5 support will disengage and {{B}}'s 3 will reframe it as a problem to manage.
- {{B}} should resist the 3 reflex to optimize or fix {{A}}'s concerns quickly — sometimes {{A}}'s lead 1 needs the concern acknowledged as valid before any solution is offered.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}}'s lead 3 is one of the most effective antidotes to {{A}}'s lead 1 paralysis — where {{A}} can get locked in the pursuit of a perfect standard, {{B}} models that imperfect action and iteration still produce real results, and this pragmatism genuinely stretches {{A}} toward healthier execution. In return, {{A}}'s supporting 4 pushes {{B}} toward a depth of self-examination that the lead 3 typically avoids; spending real time with {{A}} can help {{B}} distinguish between achievements that are genuinely meaningful and those that are just impressive. Over time, {{A}} can learn to hold principles more lightly and {{B}} can learn to hold identity more honestly — but this only happens if both resist the easier path of quietly judging each other from a distance.

145-749.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a study in principled depth meeting expansive freedom — a pairing with genuine warmth and real creative spark, but also significant friction at the level of core operating systems. The shared 4 gives both a hunger for authenticity and emotional resonance that can make the connection feel uniquely real. Yet {{A}}'s gut-led perfectionism and {{B}}'s head-led boundlessness pull in structurally opposite directions, requiring conscious navigation to avoid mutual frustration.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the supporting 4, meaning both value depth, originality, and honest emotional expression — this creates an unusual feeling of being *seen* rather than just liked.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 and {{B}}'s lead 7 share a genuine love of ideas, learning, and intellectual curiosity, making conversation feel alive and ranging.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 brings a warmth and accommodating ease that softens {{A}}'s sometimes rigid 1-led edge, helping {{A}} relax without feeling judged.
- When {{A}} is integrating toward 7 (their growth direction), they become noticeably more joyful and spontaneous — {{B}} naturally models and draws out exactly that quality.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 operates on internalized standards and a need for correctness; {{B}}'s lead 7 resists any frame that feels like a ceiling or criticism, so {{A}}'s principled corrections can land as suffocating to {{B}}.
- {{B}}'s planning style — enthusiasm-driven, loose, open to pivots — clashes with {{A}}'s 1/5 combination, which prefers precision, preparation, and follow-through.
- Under stress, {{B}}'s 7 moves toward 1, becoming uncharacteristically critical and reactive — mirroring {{A}}'s baseline in a way that can spark sharp, unexpected conflict.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 needs withdrawal and solitude to process; {{B}}'s 7 tends to process outward and may interpret {{A}}'s retreat as coldness or rejection.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} reads {{B}}'s optimism and topic-hopping as avoidance of what's real or important; {{B}} genuinely isn't avoiding — the 7-led mind is wired for possibility, not denial, but {{A}}'s 1 instinct is to see it as irresponsible.
- {{B}} reads {{A}}'s critiques and exacting standards as disapproval or joylessness; {{A}} isn't trying to diminish — the 1 simply perceives flaws the way others perceive color, and can't easily switch it off.
- Both have a supporting 4, but {{A}}'s 4 is filtered through a 1's moral lens (melancholy tied to what *should* be), while {{B}}'s 4 is softened by the 9 (longing held lightly) — so their emotional depths feel similar on the surface but operate very differently underneath.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should signal openness to feedback before {{A}} gives it — a simple "I want your honest read" disarms the dynamic where {{A}} feels compelled to correct and {{B}} feels ambushed.
- {{A}} should flag when they are processing (supporting 5 withdrawal) rather than going quiet, since {{B}}'s 9 will assume harmony and miss that something is unresolved.
- {{A}} benefits from leading with appreciation before critique; the supporting 4 in both of them means recognition lands deeply and opens the door to harder conversations.
- {{B}} should resist the 7's habit of reframing problems into positives prematurely — {{A}}'s 1 needs acknowledgment that something *is* a problem before moving toward solutions.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- The Enneagram stress/growth lines here are unusually direct: {{A}}'s growth direction is 7 ({{B}}'s lead type) and {{B}}'s stress direction is 1 ({{A}}'s lead type), meaning this relationship is a natural mirror for both people's development.
- {{B}} shows {{A}} what integrated, light-handed engagement with life looks like — {{A}} genuinely needs that modeling to loosen the grip of 1's inner critic.
- {{A}} shows {{B}} what committed follow-through, ethical seriousness, and intellectual focus look like — precisely the qualities {{B}}'s 7 avoids but needs to develop (the 7→5 growth line runs through {{A}}'s supporting type).
- The risk is that both can become the other's superego rather than their teacher — {{A}} moralizing at {{B}}, {{B}} escaping {{A}}'s structure — so the growth only flows when both enter it voluntarily rather than through pressure.

258-548.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share two of three tritype numbers (5 and 8), giving them a real foundation of intellectual seriousness and no-nonsense directness — but they approach the world from opposite dominant centers, with {{A}} leading from the heart (2) and {{B}} leading from the head (5). This creates a pairing of genuine complementarity that is also genuinely strained: {{A}} moves toward people to connect and give, while {{B}} moves inward to analyze and conserve. The shared 8 gut anchor keeps both honest and grounded, but the 2-versus-5 lead dynamic is where most of the friction and the growth will live.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 8 support in both tritypes creates immediate mutual respect — neither {{A}} nor {{B}} is fragile, and both can handle blunt honesty without crumbling.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 means they genuinely appreciate {{B}}'s intellectual depth and are not threatened by it; {{B}} senses this and relaxes their usual guardedness.
- Both carry a kind of strategic intensity — {{A}} through the 2/5/8 combination of relational intelligence and willpower, {{B}} through focused analysis backed by emotional depth (4) and force (8).
- When aligned on a common goal or problem, these two are formidable: {{A}} reads the human landscape, {{B}} maps the conceptual terrain, and the shared 8 drives execution.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 has a core need to feel needed and appreciated; {{B}}'s lead 5 is fundamentally self-sufficient and often forgets — or resists — expressing gratitude or reciprocal care.
- {{B}} requires significant private space to recharge; {{A}}'s 2 interprets withdrawal as a signal that something is wrong and may escalate attempts at connection, which pushes {{B}} further into retreat.
- Under stress, {{A}}'s 2 can become covertly controlling — giving with strings attached — while {{B}}'s 5 becomes even more withholding and detached; these stress moves are nearly perfectly incompatible.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 adds a layer of self-referential emotional intensity that can feel indulgent to {{A}}'s 2, who tends to orient emotions outward toward others rather than inward toward the self.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s emotional reserve as rejection or coldness, when it is more accurately {{B}}'s baseline operating mode — the lead 5 does not withhold to punish, it withholds to survive.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s warmth and attentiveness as neediness or even subtle manipulation (a 5's suspicion of motives), missing that the lead 2 genuinely orients toward others as a primary way of being in the world.
- {{B}}'s 4 support means they do have rich emotional inner life, but it flows inward; {{A}} expects emotional expressiveness to flow outward and toward them, so {{B}} can seem simultaneously intense and emotionally unavailable in a way {{A}} finds baffling.
- {{A}} may assume that because {{B}} shares their 5 number, {{B}} will respond to intellectual engagement as a form of closeness — but for {{B}}, intellectual exchange is not intimacy, it is simply normal functioning.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should lean on the shared 8 support and state needs directly and concretely rather than communicating through acts of giving and waiting for {{B}} to notice — {{B}} responds far better to explicit requests than to implicit bids.
- {{B}} should build in small but consistent rituals of acknowledgment for {{A}}: a specific compliment, a named appreciation. This costs {{B}} little but is high-value currency for the lead 2.
- Both should treat directness as a shared language — when the 8 in each of them is engaged, misreads drop sharply and the conversation becomes efficient and real.
- {{B}} should communicate space needs proactively and neutrally rather than simply disappearing; {{A}} can tolerate distance far more easily when given a reason and a timeline.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}} offers {{B}} a model of emotional generosity and relational attunement that the lead 5 genuinely needs to develop — {{B}} can learn, through this pairing, that interdependence is not a threat to autonomy.
- {{B}} offers {{A}} a model of self-sufficiency and inner authority that challenges the lead 2's tendency to locate identity in others' approval; proximity to {{B}}'s groundedness can help {{A}} access the fuller potential of their supporting 5.
- The shared 8 support means both have real capacity for accountability — when this relationship hits friction, neither has to hide behind passivity, and that makes repair genuinely possible.
- The highest version of this pairing looks like two people who are both strategically capable and emotionally honest: {{A}} learning to need less validation, {{B}} learning to offer more presence — both growing toward the integration their tritypes point at.

146-259.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a pairing of principled depth and warm service — both oriented toward doing good in the world, but through very different engines. {{A}} leads from the gut with an internal moral compass sharpened by 4's emotional intensity and 6's vigilance, while {{B}} leads from the heart with a relational generosity softened by 9's accommodation and grounded by 5's analysis. They can build something genuinely meaningful together, but the friction between {{A}}'s reforming critique and {{B}}'s need for appreciation is a real and recurring hazard.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both are fundamentally oriented toward goodness: {{A}}'s lead 1 wants to fix what's wrong with the world on principle; {{B}}'s lead 2 wants to alleviate suffering through direct care — these are complementary missions that feel mutually validating.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 prizes loyalty and reliability, which resonates deeply with {{B}}'s lead 2, whose core identity is built around committed, dependable relationships.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 brings analytical rigor that engages {{A}}'s 1-and-6 desire for precision and intellectual honesty; conversations between them can be unusually substantive.
- Both carry a quiet seriousness about their values and resist superficiality, giving the relationship a sense of shared depth and purpose.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 has an internalized critic that often externalizes — when {{A}} names what's wrong or imperfect, {{B}}'s lead 2 is liable to hear it as personal failure or ingratitude, triggering the 2's core fear of being unloved despite giving everything.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 defaults to conflict-avoidance and accommodation, which frustrates {{A}}'s 1-driven need to confront problems honestly and resolve them; {{A}} may experience {{B}} as evasive or conflict-averse to the point of dishonesty.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 adds emotional moodiness and a tendency toward withdrawal, leaving {{B}}'s lead 2 — who tracks relational warmth obsessively — feeling shut out or unimportant.
- {{B}}'s 2 can give in ways that quietly accumulate expectation; {{A}}'s 1 resists being obligated and may pull back when they sense emotional debt being accrued.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to see {{B}}'s warmth and accommodation as a lack of genuine standards or backbone — the 2-lead's fluid responsiveness to others reads to the 1-lead as unprincipled people-pleasing rather than an intentional relational strategy.
- {{B}} tends to misread {{A}}'s criticism as rejection: because {{B}}'s 2 equates love with service and approval, {{A}}'s 1-driven corrections feel like a verdict on {{B}}'s worth rather than an expression of investment in shared ideals.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 can produce anxious doubt and skepticism that {{B}}'s 2 interprets as distrust of {{B}} personally, when it is actually generalized vigilance.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 occasionally retreats into detachment for self-regulation, which {{A}}'s supporting 4 may amplify into a drama of abandonment rather than recognizing it as a neutral need for processing space.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} benefits from naming needs directly rather than signaling through increased giving; {{A}}'s lead 1 is not naturally attuned to indirect emotional cues and will not reliably pick up on escalating helpfulness as a cry for reciprocity.
- {{A}} should practice leading with acknowledgment before correction — the 1's default is to move straight to what's improvable, but {{B}}'s 2 genuinely needs to hear that their contribution is seen before any critique can land constructively.
- When {{B}}'s supporting 9 goes quiet to avoid conflict, {{A}} should resist escalating pressure; instead, naming the pattern calmly ('I notice we've stopped talking about this') gives {{B}}'s 9 a softer on-ramp back into honest dialogue.
- {{A}}'s supporting 4 tends toward intense, emotionally loaded language during stress; {{B}} can help by staying present without over-soothing, which {{A}}'s 1 experiences as being managed rather than heard.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 2 offers {{A}} a direct embodiment of unconditional positive regard — something {{A}}'s inner critic rarely provides internally — and over time this can loosen {{A}}'s perfectionism and soften the harshness of the 1's self-imposed standards.
- {{A}}'s lead 1 offers {{B}} a model of holding a position independent of approval, which is exactly the growth edge for a 2-lead who risks losing themselves in service to others' needs.
- The deeper mutual gift is this: {{A}} helps {{B}} develop self-respect grounded in principle rather than in being needed; {{B}} helps {{A}} experience that warmth and care are not compromises of integrity but expressions of it.
- This pairing is not effortless, but it carries genuine developmental potential — provided both resist their respective defaults of critique-and-withdraw ({{A}}) and give-and-resent ({{B}}).

278-714.summary: {{A}} leads with warmth, relational generosity, and an instinct to care deeply, while {{B}} leads with expansive enthusiasm, future-focus, and a restless need for novelty. The shared 7 energy creates genuine sparks of fun and adventure, but the lead-type gap — heart-first vs. head-first — means their core emotional needs and rhythms are oriented quite differently. This pairing has real chemistry and real friction in equal measure.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The 7 in both {{A}} and {{B}} creates an immediate sense of playfulness and shared appetite for experience — this is a pairing that can light up a room together.
- {{A}}'s lead 2 genuinely delights in making {{B}} feel special and energized, and {{B}}'s lead 7 responds warmly to that generosity of spirit.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 adds boldness and directness that {{B}}'s lead 7 actually respects — there's no passive-aggressive undercurrent here when things are working well.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 brings a depth and longing for authenticity that resonates with {{A}}'s heart-center orientation, creating moments of surprising emotional intimacy.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 needs reciprocal emotional investment and acknowledgment to feel secure; {{B}}'s lead 7 tends to keep moving and resist emotional weight, which can leave {{A}} feeling invisible or taken for granted.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 introduces a critical, reforming edge that can inadvertently wound {{A}}'s 2, which is acutely sensitive to judgment and rejection from those it cares about.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 can become confrontational when {{A}} feels undervalued, and {{B}}'s lead 7 — which instinctively reframes or exits discomfort — may avoid the accountability {{A}}'s 8 demands.
- {{B}}'s 4 support creates occasional swings into melancholy and a desire for solitude or uniqueness that can confuse {{A}}, whose 7 support prefers to keep the energy upbeat and external.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} equates love with attentiveness and giving; {{B}} equates love with shared adventure and stimulating ideas — so each can feel genuinely caring toward the other while still leaving the other feeling unmet.
- {{B}}'s lead 7 processes emotion by reframing and moving forward quickly; {{A}}'s lead 2 processes by talking through feelings and seeking reassurance, and {{B}} can mistake this as neediness rather than a bid for connection.
- When {{A}}'s supporting 8 surfaces in frustration, {{B}} may read it as an aggressive attack rather than the blunt-but-direct communication style it actually is, prompting {{B}} to deflect or rationalize rather than engage.
- {{B}}'s oscillation between 7's expansive optimism and 4's introspective longing can look inconsistent to {{A}}, who may try to 'fix' {{B}}'s mood with caretaking when {{B}} actually just needs space to feel both sides.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should name needs explicitly rather than giving more in hopes that {{B}} will notice — {{B}}'s lead 7 is genuinely future-focused and not wired to read emotional subtext reliably.
- {{B}} should build in regular, specific acknowledgment of {{A}}'s contributions and feelings; a single sincere 'I see what you do and it matters' goes a long way for a lead 2.
- When conflict arises, {{A}} should lead with the 2's relational warmth before the 8's confrontational directness — {{B}}'s 1 support will actually respond better to principled dialogue than to power challenges.
- {{B}} can invite {{A}} into deeper honesty by creating safety for {{A}} to stop performing generosity and admit frustration; {{A}}'s 2 often masks resentment until it erupts.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}} offers {{B}} a genuine model of emotional presence and investment — over time, {{B}}'s underdeveloped heart connection (secondary 4 aside) can deepen through sustained contact with {{A}}'s lead 2 warmth.
- {{B}} offers {{A}} an invitation to loosen the caretaking identity and simply enjoy life for its own sake — {{A}}'s supporting 7 is already there, but {{B}}'s lead 7 can coax it out more freely.
- The real growth edge for this pairing is {{A}} learning that withdrawing care isn't punitive — it's self-respecting — and {{B}} learning that staying present during discomfort, rather than reframing it away, builds the depth {{B}}'s supporting 4 actually craves.
- If both can honor the gap between {{A}}'s need for emotional rootedness and {{B}}'s need for freedom without pathologizing the other, this pairing becomes genuinely expansive for both.

217-528.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are drawn together by a shared 2 archetype — both understand the impulse to help and to matter to others — but they express that impulse from very different centers of gravity. {{A}} leads from the heart and organizes the world through warmth, moral purpose, and enthusiasm, while {{B}} leads from the head and approaches everything, including relationships, through analysis, strategy, and guarded autonomy. This pairing has genuine complementarity and real tension in almost equal measure.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 2 creates a rare mutual language: both {{A}} and {{B}} understand what it means to invest in people, and neither is purely self-focused.
- {{A}}'s lead 2 warmth tends to draw out {{B}}'s supporting 2, which is normally screened through the 5's caution — {{A}} is one of the few types that can genuinely coax {{B}} into emotional openness.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 and {{B}}'s lead 5 create lively intellectual rapport; they can spend hours in stimulating conversation where enthusiasm and depth feed each other.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 and {{B}}'s supporting 8 share a gut-level commitment to integrity and getting things right, giving the pair a shared moral seriousness beneath the surface differences.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 needs to feel needed and appreciated in real time; {{B}}'s lead 5 instinctively withdraws to process and conserve energy, and that withdrawal reads as rejection to {{A}} even when it isn't.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 communicates bluntly and values directness as a form of respect; {{A}}'s lead 2 personalizes criticism quickly and {{A}}'s supporting 1 can respond with moralistic counter-critique, turning small disagreements into ethical standoffs.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 can scatter energy and pivot away from depth just when {{B}}'s 5 wants sustained focus; {{B}} may experience {{A}} as breezy or avoidant of harder truths.
- {{B}}'s 5-led self-sufficiency can quietly signal "I don't need you," which is close to the core wound of {{A}}'s 2.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} reads {{B}}'s intellectual distance as emotional unavailability or indifference; {{B}} genuinely doesn't register this as a problem because the 5 experiences detachment as neutral, not cold.
- {{B}} can interpret {{A}}'s 2-led warmth and generous gestures as emotional maneuvering — the 5 is skeptical of emotional appeals and may wonder what {{A}} wants in return, while {{A}} is simply expressing care without an agenda.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 occasionally shifts into teacher or corrector mode, which {{B}}'s supporting 8 reads as a power play or condescension, when {{A}} experiences it as genuine helpfulness and standards-setting.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should offer {{B}} explicit low-pressure space: naming "I'm not looking for a response right now" can allow {{B}}'s supporting 2 to surface without the 5's defenses activating.
- {{B}} should practice naming appreciation out loud and specifically — {{A}}'s lead 2 doesn't infer it from logic or competence; it needs to hear it directly and often.
- When {{B}}'s supporting 8 goes blunt, {{A}} benefits from pausing before responding with the supporting 1's correction reflex; and {{B}} benefits from softening delivery when {{A}} has extended emotional effort.
- {{A}} should resist the 2's impulse to help {{B}} before being asked — the 5 experiences unsolicited help as an intrusion on autonomy, not a gift.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} challenges {{A}} at the deepest level: the 5's self-sufficiency holds up a mirror to the 2's conditional giving, inviting {{A}} to examine whether care is freely offered or quietly transactional.
- {{A}} challenges {{B}} equally: sustained warmth from {{A}}'s lead 2 and playful invitation from the supporting 7 create a rare relational safety that can pull {{B}}'s 5 toward the integration point of 8 — not as aggression but as genuine confident engagement with the world.
- Over time, {{A}} can learn to need less external validation and develop a more internally grounded sense of worth, while {{B}} can learn that emotional presence does not drain or compromise — it expands. This makes the pairing quietly transformative for both when there is enough mutual commitment to stay with the discomfort.

628-946.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are a pairing of vigilant loyalty and peaceful depth — connected by a shared 6 current running through both tritypes, but operating from very different dominant centers. {{A}}'s head-led anxiety and assertive gut energy can clash sharply with {{B}}'s gut-led conflict-avoidance and introverted heart. With enough mutual understanding, they can offer each other real complementarity, but the friction points are structural and require ongoing attention.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry 6 energy: {{A}} leads with it, {{B}} holds it as a supporting type, giving the pair a shared vocabulary of loyalty, commitment, and long-term reliability.
- {{A}}'s supporting 2 and {{B}}'s supporting 4 meet in the heart center — both value emotionally meaningful connection and will invest deeply in the relationship.
- {{B}}'s 9-led steadiness can feel like a safe harbor for {{A}}'s lead-6 anxiety, while {{A}}'s 2 warmth and attentiveness speaks directly to what {{B}}'s 4 quietly craves: being truly seen and cared for.
- Neither type is flighty or noncommittal by nature, so shared values around fidelity and showing up give this pairing a durable foundation.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 is the single biggest friction point: when {{A}} feels threatened or unheard, the 8 energy surfaces as confrontation, volume, and directness — exactly what {{B}}'s lead 9 is wired to flee from or shut down against.
- {{B}}'s 9-driven conflict avoidance can look like stonewalling, vague agreement, or drifting away emotionally, which triggers {{A}}'s lead-6 worst-case thinking and escalates the very conflict {{B}} was trying to avoid.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 has a need for authentic, individuated emotional space; {{A}}'s supporting 2 can inadvertently crowd that space by over-helping, fixing, or making {{B}}'s feelings about the relationship rather than about {{B}}.
- {{A}} wants resolution and reassurance; {{B}} wants peace and room to process — these are often incompatible timelines.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} frequently misreads {{B}}'s 9-style withdrawal as passive aggression, hidden resentment, or a lack of investment — when it is more often overwhelm and a genuinely slow processing speed. {{B}} in turn misreads {{A}}'s lead-6 questioning and supporting-8 bluntness as aggression or instability, when {{A}} is actually seeking security and connection through directness. {{B}}'s supporting 4 experiences emotion as identity and depth; {{A}}'s supporting 2 responds to emotion as a problem to solve, which can make {{B}} feel dismissed rather than supported. Both can end up feeling unloved by the other's coping mechanism — {{A}} feels abandoned by {{B}}'s silence, {{B}} feels invaded by {{A}}'s urgency.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should consciously lead with the 2's warmth before letting the 8's directness take over — stating vulnerability first lowers {{B}}'s defensive withdrawal significantly.
- {{B}} must resist the 9's reflex to give vague, peacekeeping agreements; {{A}}'s lead 6 needs honest, specific responses to feel genuinely reassured, not just soothed.
- {{A}} should give {{B}} explicit processing time before expecting closure on difficult conversations — the 9-led mind needs to settle before it can engage authentically.
- {{B}} can use the supporting 4's capacity for authentic emotional language to name what is actually happening internally, rather than defaulting to 9-style merging or deflection.
- Both share 6 energy: naming shared fears and commitments directly ('I'm anxious because I care about this') can reset a spiral before it escalates.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}} offers {{B}} a model of naming fears out loud, acting decisively, and confronting what is uncomfortable — capacities the 9-led {{B}} genuinely needs to develop, and that {{B}}'s supporting 4 is actually hungry for even if the lead 9 resists. {{B}} offers {{A}} something equally rare: the experience of being in a relationship where peace is not earned through vigilance, helping {{A}}'s lead 6 gradually loosen its scanning and trust the present moment. The risk is that {{A}} over-functions and {{B}} under-functions relationally — {{A}} driving all conflict-resolution while {{B}} accommodates without truly growing. The growth edge for both is learning that real security ({{A}}'s core need) and real peace ({{B}}'s core need) are only achieved by moving through discomfort together, not around it.

137-837.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both gut-led, action-oriented, high-achieving types who share identical supporting centers — heart-center 3 and head-center 7 — making them natural collaborators in drive and ambition. The critical difference is in how their gut energy expresses: {{A}} leads with principled correctness and an inner critic that demands integrity, while {{B}} leads with raw power and the need to dominate outcomes on their own terms. This pairing has enormous productive potential but carries a real risk of colliding head-on when both believe they are unambiguously right.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both are gut-dominant and decisive — there is no vagueness or passivity in this pairing; things get done.
- Shared supporting 3 means both are wired for achievement, efficiency, and visible results, and they speak the same language of success.
- Shared supporting 7 gives both an optimistic, future-oriented energy — they can dream big together and keep momentum alive in a project or relationship.
- Both are direct and confident, so neither has to tiptoe around the other, which builds a baseline of mutual respect.
- When aligned on a goal, this pairing is one of the most productive combinations possible.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 operates from a deeply internalized code of correctness — there is a right way and a wrong way, and {{A}} feels compelled to uphold it. {{B}}'s lead 8 believes rules are for other people and chafes immediately at being told what to do or how to do it.
- Both gut types carry enormous conviction, meaning neither naturally yields — standoffs can be prolonged and entrenched.
- {{A}}'s corrective impulse (a core 1 defense) will land on {{B}} as moralizing or micromanagement, which is perhaps the fastest way to trigger an 8's combativeness.
- The shared 3 support can become a competition for credit or recognition rather than a shared engine — both want to be seen as the architect of success.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s boundary-pushing and rule-bending as recklessness or ethical sloppiness, when in fact {{B}} is operating from a gut-level certainty that they know what's needed and that procedural constraints are obstacles to real results. {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s principled stances and corrections as controlling rigidity or even cowardice dressed up as virtue, when {{A}} is genuinely motivated by a sincere need for integrity and quality. Neither fully registers that the other's gut conviction is just as real and deeply felt as their own — they each assume the other is being willfully obstinate rather than authentically wired differently.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} will reach {{B}} far more effectively by framing concerns in terms of outcomes and impact ('this approach will cost us the result') rather than what is right or wrong — lead 8 responds to power arguments, not moral ones.
- {{B}} should consciously acknowledge {{A}}'s standards before pushing back; skipping that step turns every disagreement into a dominance contest that {{A}}'s 1 will dig into stubbornly.
- Both can leverage their shared 7 support as a reset button — when tension spikes, redirecting to shared vision and possibility defuses the standoff.
- Establish explicit lanes of authority early; both need domains where their gut instinct is the final word.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}} offers {{A}} a genuinely valuable push against over-perfectionism — the lead 8's willingness to act boldly without waiting for ideal conditions can help {{A}}'s 1 loosen its grip on control and trust that good enough, executed powerfully, often outperforms perfect. {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally real: a principled anchor that channels {{B}}'s force toward outcomes that are not only impactful but sustainable and ethical, counteracting the lead 8's tendency to break things in the name of getting things done. The growth edge for both is recognizing that the other's gut-center strength is a genuine complement rather than a challenge to their authority — when that shift happens, this pairing becomes unusually formidable.

714-926.summary: {{A}} leads with 7's expansive, pleasure-seeking drive and pairs it with 4's emotional depth and 1's inner critic, creating someone who is simultaneously excited about possibility, hungry for meaning, and quietly self-demanding. {{B}} leads with 9's gentle inertia and comfort-seeking, supported by 2's relational warmth and 6's loyal vigilance — someone who merges easily, keeps the peace, and shows up steadily for those they love. This pairing has real warmth and creative chemistry, but the 7's restless forward motion and the 9's grounding stillness will regularly pull in opposite directions.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 7 brings infectious enthusiasm that {{B}}'s lead 9 genuinely enjoys — 9 is one of the few types that can receive 7's energy without feeling overwhelmed by it.
- {{B}}'s accepting, non-judgmental presence gives {{A}} the rare gift of feeling free to be fully themselves, including the emotionally complex 4 side.
- The 2 in {{B}} and the 4 in {{A}} create a mutual undercurrent of emotional attunement — both care about being seen and seeing others.
- {{A}}'s 1 and {{B}}'s 9 share a quiet idealism about how the world should be, which can make them feel aligned on values even when their styles differ.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 7 craves novelty, momentum, and constant forward motion; {{B}}'s lead 9 defaults to inertia and is genuinely energized by sameness and routine — this is a structural tension, not just a preference gap.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 will occasionally surface as sharp criticism or impatience with {{B}}'s slow decision-making pace, which strikes directly at {{B}}'s need for a friction-free environment.
- {{B}}'s supporting 6 carries an undercurrent of anxiety and can become suspicious of {{A}}'s optimism or broad social reach, reading enthusiasm as unreliability.
- The 4 in {{A}} periodically demands emotional intensity and authentic confrontation that {{B}}'s 9 is structurally wired to sidestep.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s calm and agreeableness as disengagement or lack of ambition; {{B}} is not disengaged — the 9 lead processes deeply and slowly, and merger with the environment looks like passivity from the outside.
- {{B}} may read {{A}}'s restlessness and reframing of problems as emotional avoidance — and to be fair, the 7's defense mechanism (rationalization and future-orientation) does bypass pain — but {{A}} experiences this as genuine aliveness, not escape.
- {{A}}'s 4 brings episodic emotional intensity and a need for uniqueness; {{B}}'s supporting 2 responds to others' needs rather than its own, so when {{A}} wants deep mirroring, {{B}} may deflect by caretaking instead.
- {{B}}'s 6 values loyalty and consistency and may quietly track whether {{A}}'s commitments hold up over time — {{A}} may have no idea this scorekeeping is happening.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the urge to reframe or silver-line {{B}}'s concerns too quickly; {{B}}'s 6 and 2 both need to feel heard before solutions are introduced.
- {{B}} must practice naming wants and disagreements directly — leaning on 9's merge-and-accommodate pattern will eventually breed resentment, and {{A}}'s 7 and 4 both respond better to directness than to passive compliance.
- When {{A}}'s 1 gets critical about pace or execution, framing feedback as shared idealism ('I want this to be great for both of us') lands far better with {{B}} than correction alone.
- {{B}} can appeal to {{A}}'s 4 when wanting depth — inviting {{A}} into meaning and authenticity, not just logistics, will hold {{A}}'s attention far more reliably.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 9 offers {{A}} something the 7 genuinely struggles to find: a still, accepting presence that doesn't require performance or relentless forward momentum, which can help {{A}}'s 4 access real emotional depth rather than aestheticizing it.
- {{A}}'s lead 7 can pull {{B}} out of comfortable numbness and into actual engagement with life — 9 at growth moves toward 3's action orientation, and {{A}}'s enthusiasm models what energized participation looks like.
- The risk is codependency of avoidances: 7 avoids pain through distraction, 9 avoids conflict through accommodation, and together they can collude in never addressing what actually needs addressing.
- The healthiest version of this pairing requires {{A}} to slow down enough to be present and {{B}} to speak up enough to be real — both are counter to their default wiring, which means genuine growth is on the table if both are willing.

358-416.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both heart-center leads, which means identity, emotional resonance, and the need to feel seen are central to each of them — but they pursue these needs through almost opposite strategies. {{A}} leads with achievement, efficiency, and strategic self-presentation, while {{B}} leads with emotional depth, individuality, and the search for authentic meaning. This pairing has real creative and intellectual voltage, but the friction between a 3's image-consciousness and a 4's authenticity-hunger is one of the more genuinely challenging heart-type clashes in the enneagram.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both {{A}} and {{B}} are heart-center leads who quietly crave being deeply known, giving the relationship an underlying emotional seriousness neither will want to waste on surface-level connection.
- {{A}}'s supporting 5 brings intellectual depth and curiosity that {{B}}'s lead 4 genuinely respects — this pair can have rich, substantive conversations about ideas, systems, and meaning.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 and {{A}}'s supporting 8 share a gut-level conviction about doing things right and refusing to be pushed around, producing mutual respect for each other's backbone.
- When {{A}} drops the performance mode, their 8's directness and 5's insight can feel like exactly the grounded, no-nonsense presence {{B}}'s 6 secretly needs for reassurance.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- The 3-vs-4 core tension is real: {{A}}'s lead 3 adapts its presentation to achieve goals and win approval, which {{B}}'s lead 4 tends to read as inauthenticity or even dishonesty.
- {{B}}'s emotional intensity and need to sit with difficult feelings runs directly against {{A}}'s instinct — shaped by 3 and reinforced by 8 — to fix the problem, move on, and produce results.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 can be blunt to the point of wounding; {{B}}'s lead 4 is one of the most emotionally sensitive types, so carelessly delivered criticism can cause outsized damage.
- {{B}}'s supporting 1 carries a moralistic streak that may quietly judge {{A}}'s pragmatic willingness to bend rules or work around systems in pursuit of outcomes.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} often reads {{B}}'s emotional expressiveness and longing as drama, self-indulgence, or inefficiency — failing to recognize that for a 4 lead, processing feeling is not obstruction but the actual point.
- {{B}} frequently misreads {{A}}'s polished, adaptive presentation as a mask or a sign that {{A}} is hiding something, when it is actually just how a 3 lead naturally navigates the world.
- When {{A}}'s supporting 5 withdraws to process privately, {{B}}'s supporting 6 can spiral into anxious interpretations — assuming coldness, rejection, or betrayal where there is really just a need for internal space.
- {{A}} may genuinely not understand why {{B}} needs so much emotional attunement before being able to engage practically, and {{B}} may not understand why {{A}} keeps steering toward action before the emotional reality has been acknowledged.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the 3's reflex to jump straight to solutions when {{B}} is in a feeling-heavy state; a brief "that sounds really hard" goes further than a five-point plan.
- {{B}} should try to name emotional needs explicitly rather than expecting {{A}}'s 3 to intuit them — directness is a language {{A}}'s supporting 8 actually respects and responds well to.
- {{A}}'s 8 bluntness needs a deliberate pause before delivery when {{B}} is in a 4-lead vulnerable mode; the same honesty wrapped in even minimal warmth lands completely differently.
- {{B}}'s supporting 6 should actively work against catastrophizing during {{A}}'s quiet or withdrawn phases — checking in with a simple question beats building an anxious narrative in silence.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} something genuinely valuable: a mirror for the emotional and identity dimensions that {{A}}'s lead 3 tends to bypass in the drive to perform and produce.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally valuable: evidence that desire and longing can be channeled into concrete action, helping {{B}}'s 4 move out of idealized yearning and into the world.
- The shared heart-center lead means that if both commit to honesty over self-protection, this relationship can produce unusual depth — but it requires {{A}} to risk being seen without the achievement armor, and {{B}} to risk that intimacy won't be destroyed by {{A}}'s imperfections.
- The growth edge for this pair lives precisely in the discomfort: {{A}} learning that emotional truth is not inefficiency, and {{B}} learning that adaptation and achievement are not the same as betrayal of self.

258-947.summary: {{A}} leads with a warm but strategically driven heart — the 2's need to be needed is reinforced by the 5's analytical cool and the 8's directness and control. {{B}} leads with a gut-level pull toward harmony and merger, softened by the 4's emotional depth and brightened by the 7's optimism. This pairing has genuine warmth and complementary strengths, but the 2's assertive giving clashes meaningfully with the 9's passive receiving, and real tensions emerge around control, emotional visibility, and reciprocity.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 is oriented toward others' wellbeing, and {{B}}'s lead 9 is naturally receptive and non-threatening — this creates an easy initial warmth and sense of being welcome.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 carries real emotional depth that {{A}}'s supporting 5 finds genuinely interesting and worth exploring intellectually.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 provides decisive, grounding energy that {{B}}'s 9 often lacks internally and quietly appreciates in a partner.
- {{B}}'s supporting 7 brings lightness and enthusiasm that can cut through the heaviness that {{A}}'s 5 and 8 can create.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s 2-lead runs on a hidden economy of giving and receiving — when {{B}}'s 9 passively accepts care without overtly reflecting it back, {{A}} eventually feels invisible and resentful.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 prizes directness, confrontation, and decisiveness; {{B}}'s 9-lead handles conflict through diffusion and withdrawal, which the 8 reads as evasion or weakness.
- The 2+8 combination in {{A}} can become quietly controlling — framing direction as care — and {{B}}'s 9 will resist through passive non-compliance rather than open pushback, which frustrates {{A}} even more.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 periodically needs to be recognized as singular and emotionally complex; {{A}}'s 2 tends to generalize care rather than tailor it, which can make {{B}} feel like just another person being helped.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} consistently misreads {{B}}'s 9-style agreeableness as emotional contentment or mutual alignment, missing the 4 undercurrent of unmet longing that {{B}} rarely voices directly.
- {{B}} experiences {{A}}'s 8-backed directness as aggression or an attempt to dominate, when {{A}} is genuinely operating from the 2's impulse to fix, protect, and care.
- {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s 9 quietude as ingratitude or emotional unavailability; {{B}} is actually merging deeply but doesn't perform connection the way {{A}}'s 2 expects.
- {{B}} assumes {{A}}'s helpfulness is unconditional; it isn't — the 2 keeps an internal ledger, and {{B}} doesn't realize a debt is accumulating.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the 2's instinct to diagnose {{B}}'s needs and instead ask open questions — {{B}}'s 4 has specific, nuanced emotional needs that differ from what {{A}} would want in the same situation.
- {{B}} needs to practice naming what they actually feel and want, rather than relying on {{A}}'s 5 to analyze it or the 2 to intuit it — the 9's habit of merging into vagueness leaves {{A}} working with incomplete data.
- When {{A}}'s 8 comes out forcefully, {{B}} should name the impact directly rather than going quiet — the 8 responds to honest pushback far better than to silence or slow withdrawal.
- {{A}} should watch for the 2's tendency to interpret any act of care as a relational claim; {{B}}'s 9 gives space generously and doesn't mean disinterest by it.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2, at its best, can hold steady, non-transactional care for {{B}} — modeling that showing up for someone doesn't require reciprocal performance, which is actually a lesson {{A}}'s own 2 needs to learn.
- {{B}}'s 9-lead, when it functions well, creates an atmosphere of radical acceptance that gives {{A}}'s 5 permission to surface uncertainty and {{A}}'s 8 permission to be vulnerable — a rare combination.
- {{A}}'s 8 can be a genuine gift to {{B}}: a real-world model of holding ground and voicing needs without the world falling apart, which is the 9's core growth edge.
- Long-term, {{A}} is pushed toward genuine selflessness by {{B}}'s non-transactional warmth, and {{B}} is pulled toward authentic self-expression by {{A}}'s insistence that real presence is required in the relationship.

268-529.summary: {{A}} leads with warm, relational urgency — a heart-dominant 2 backed by anxious loyalty (6) and forceful protectiveness (8) — while {{B}} leads with cool, analytical detachment — a head-dominant 5 backed by quiet care (2) and conflict-averse calm (9). The shared 2 energy gives them a genuine point of mutual understanding, but the fundamental tension between {{A}}'s need for emotional reciprocity and {{B}}'s need for inner space is the defining challenge of this pairing. They can work well together if they learn to read each other's love languages accurately rather than projecting their own onto the other.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry a 2 in their tritype, giving them a shared orientation toward care and usefulness — they genuinely want to help each other and will feel that intention from the start.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 finds real comfort in {{B}}'s lead 5; having a knowledgeable, competent partner quiets {{A}}'s anxiety and provides the sense of security the 6 craves.
- {{B}}'s supporting 9 creates a non-threatening, steady presence that {{A}}'s 6 support relaxes into, since {{B}} rarely escalates or destabilizes the environment.
- {{A}}'s lead 2 warmth can activate {{B}}'s supporting 2, drawing out a relational softness that {{B}} often keeps buried beneath the 5's self-sufficiency.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 is wired to give and connect, and it measures love by emotional availability — {{B}}'s lead 5 withdraws to recharge and thinks clearly in solitude, which {{A}} experiences as coldness or rejection.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 is direct, confrontational, and willing to push hard when something matters; {{B}}'s supporting 9 instinctively mutes conflict and goes flat under pressure, which reads to {{A}}'s 8 as passive or evasive.
- {{A}}'s 6 support generates anxious, looping reassurance-seeking; {{B}}'s 5 lead finds this emotionally costly and may disengage further — creating exactly the cycle {{A}} fears.
- {{B}}'s 5 tendency to intellectualize emotional issues can feel dismissive to {{A}}, who experiences feelings as primary data rather than noise to be processed.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s withdrawal as a signal about the relationship — a withholding of affection or a sign of disapproval — when {{B}} is simply doing what a lead 5 requires: retreating to restore capacity.
- {{B}} interprets {{A}}'s emotional intensity and bids for connection as intrusive or overwhelming, not recognizing that {{A}}'s lead 2 expresses care by closing distance, not by granting it.
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 can come across as controlling or aggressive to {{B}}'s supporting 9, but {{A}} is not trying to dominate — the 8 activates when {{A}} feels unheard or when someone they love is at risk.
- {{B}}'s sparse emotional expression can make {{A}} feel like they are doing all the emotional labor, when in reality {{B}}'s supporting 2 does care — it's just quieter, more practical, and less visible.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should name their need for connection explicitly rather than through indirect emotional pressure — {{B}}'s lead 5 responds to clear, non-guilt-laden requests far better than to emotional subtext.
- {{B}} should practice verbal affirmation on a predictable basis, not only when prompted; {{A}}'s lead 2 and supporting 6 together create a real need to feel valued and secure, and small consistent signals matter enormously.
- When {{A}}'s supporting 8 wants to push an issue, flagging it as important rather than escalating tone gives {{B}}'s supporting 9 room to engage rather than shut down.
- {{B}} can buy real goodwill with {{A}} by occasionally initiating care — even analytical or practical help counts as love to {{B}}'s supporting 2, and {{A}} will receive it warmly.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{B}}'s lead 5 offers {{A}} something genuinely valuable: a calm, non-reactive anchor that can help {{A}}'s supporting 6 break out of anxious spiral thinking and evaluate situations more clearly. In turn, {{A}}'s lead 2 warmth and emotional courage can gently challenge {{B}} to move toward the integration direction of the 5 — toward presence, engagement, and trusting that connection won't deplete them. The risk is that without mutual effort, {{A}} over-functions emotionally while {{B}} under-functions, reinforcing codependent patterns the lead 2 already tends toward. At their best, {{A}} teaches {{B}} that intimacy is sustainable, and {{B}} teaches {{A}} that love doesn't require constant vigilance to survive.

748-927.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a strand of 7 energy that creates an immediate sense of fun and mutual enthusiasm, but their lead types pull in genuinely different directions: {{A}} charges forward with head-led urgency and emotional intensity, while {{B}} anchors in gut-led stillness and harmony. This pairing has real warmth and spark, but will repeatedly bump into a tension between {{A}}'s need for bold engagement and {{B}}'s deep aversion to friction and disruption.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 7 thread means both {{A}} and {{B}} gravitate toward optimism, novelty, and adventure — trips, ideas, and spontaneous plans come easily.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 offers genuine warmth and attentiveness that feels nourishing to {{A}}'s 4, which craves being seen and appreciated.
- {{A}}'s lead 7 enthusiasm can cut through {{B}}'s 9-driven inertia in the best way, pulling {{B}} into experiences they'd never initiate alone.
- {{B}}'s 9 groundedness provides a rare pocket of calm that {{A}}'s restless 7 actually benefits from, even if {{A}} doesn't always recognize it.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 8 is direct, confrontational, and has no patience for passivity — {{B}}'s lead 9 experiences this as aggression and will shut down or stonewall rather than engage.
- {{B}}'s 9-led tendency to numb out and go along creates a slow-building resentment that never surfaces cleanly, which {{A}}'s 4 eventually reads as emotional unavailability.
- {{A}}'s lead 7 avoids sitting with pain, but the supporting 4 generates real emotional depth and intensity; {{B}} can be caught off guard by {{A}}'s mood swings between high energy and brooding.
- {{B}}'s supporting 2 can enable {{A}}'s avoidance patterns by accommodating rather than gently challenging, which helps neither person grow.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s 9 quiet or withdrawal as passive aggression or disengagement; {{B}} is usually just self-regulating, not punishing.
- {{B}} interprets {{A}}'s 8-inflected directness as an attack that demands a winner and a loser; {{A}} often just wants a real conversation and moves on quickly after.
- {{A}}'s 4 needs to feel uniquely understood and chosen, but {{B}}'s 9 merges and accommodates broadly — {{A}} can feel like just another person {{B}} is keeping the peace with, rather than someone truly seen.
- {{B}} may assume {{A}}'s big enthusiasm signals reliability and follow-through; {{A}}'s lead 7 often means the excitement *is* the point, and execution is secondary.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should consciously dial back the 8 directness with {{B}} — not to suppress truth, but to invite rather than confront, since {{B}}'s 9 genuinely cannot engage when it feels like a fight.
- {{B}} must practice naming needs and disagreements in real time instead of absorbing them; {{A}}'s 7+8 respects directness far more than quiet compliance followed by slow withdrawal.
- When {{A}}'s 4 surfaces — melancholy, longing, a need for depth — {{B}} should resist the 9 impulse to smooth it over with reassurance; sitting with it and reflecting it back is what {{A}} actually needs.
- {{B}} can use the supporting 7 energy to match {{A}}'s pace in conversation, signaling engagement rather than letting 9 flatness read as indifference.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} carries something {{A}} genuinely needs: the 9's capacity to be fully present without an agenda, which can teach {{A}}'s lead 7 that staying in one place — emotionally or physically — isn't the same as being trapped.
- {{A}} carries something {{B}} genuinely needs: the combined force of 7's vision and 8's will models that desire is worth pursuing and conflict doesn't have to mean collapse.
- The real growth edge for this pair is mutual tolerance of discomfort — {{A}} learning to stay rather than escape when things get heavy, and {{B}} learning to speak rather than disappear when things get tense.
- If both can develop those capacities, the relationship becomes unusually rich: {{A}}'s depth and drive lands in {{B}}'s genuine warmth and stillness, and neither has to perform a version of themselves they aren't.

217-415.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are both heart-center leads who share a supporting 1, giving them a surprising ethical bedrock in common — but their emotional orientations pull in nearly opposite directions. {{A}} leads with outward warmth and a drive to nurture and improve others, while {{B}} leads with inward depth, longing, and a fierce need for authentic selfhood. This pairing can be profoundly enriching if both respect the difference between giving love and inhabiting it.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared supporting 1 gives both {{A}} and {{B}} a genuine commitment to integrity, quality, and doing things right — they can bond quickly over principled stances and mutual standards.
- Both are heart-center leads, meaning emotional depth and meaning-making are central to how they navigate the world; neither will be satisfied with shallow connection.
- {{A}}'s natural warmth and attentiveness meets something real in {{B}}, whose lead 4 quietly hungers to be seen as uniquely significant — {{A}} is often very good at making people feel exactly that.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 adds levity and enthusiasm that can genuinely lift {{B}} out of 4-led rumination when {{B}} is open to it.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 is wired to connect, give, and stay in relationship; {{B}}'s lead 4 periodically needs to retreat into interior space, and that withdrawal can feel like rejection to {{A}}.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 actively sidesteps pain and keeps energy forward-moving, while {{B}}'s lead 4 often moves toward melancholy and sits with it — this mismatch in emotional tempo creates real friction.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 adds a cool, analytical layer that can read as cold indifference to {{A}}, who leads with warmth and expects some emotional reciprocity.
- Both have supporting 1, which means both can be quietly critical — when this energy turns toward each other, the criticism feels especially stinging because it comes from someone who cares.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to interpret {{B}}'s emotional withdrawal or self-focus as ingratitude or rejection, when {{B}} is simply doing what lead 4 does: turning inward to locate an authentic sense of self.
- {{B}} may experience {{A}}'s helping instincts as subtly controlling or emotionally transactional — the classic 4 suspicion that love comes with strings — when {{A}} is, more often than not, genuinely motivated by care.
- {{A}}'s 7-supported optimism can feel emotionally dismissive to {{B}}; what {{A}} intends as encouragement, {{B}}'s lead 4 can receive as a refusal to take their inner life seriously.
- {{B}} may appear self-absorbed to {{A}}, while {{A}} may appear emotionally performative or approval-seeking to {{B}} — both attributions are partially accurate but missing crucial context.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the urge to fix or brighten {{B}}'s emotional states; the lead 4 needs to feel that their depths are tolerable to others, not redirected.
- {{B}} should name explicitly when they need solitude — {{A}}'s lead 2 does not assume withdrawal is neutral, so a direct "I need space, this isn't about you" matters enormously.
- Both can anchor difficult conversations in their shared supporting 1 values — framing things in terms of fairness, integrity, or doing things right tends to be mutually legible ground.
- {{A}} should practice asking for their own needs rather than hinting through giving; {{B}}'s supporting 5 responds far better to direct, specific requests than to emotional pressure.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} has the potential to teach {{A}} something essential: that emotional authenticity sometimes means sitting with discomfort rather than resolving it, helping {{A}}'s lead 2 stop outsourcing its emotional needs through service.
- {{A}} has the potential to show {{B}} that care can be offered freely without an agenda, slowly eroding the lead 4's default assumption that love is conditional or will eventually disappoint.
- The shared supporting 1 is the structural backbone of long-term growth here — both can use their principled instincts to hold each other accountable with compassion rather than judgment.
- At their best, {{A}} and {{B}} model for each other what it looks like to lead with the heart honestly: {{A}} learning depth, {{B}} learning generosity.

629-925.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a warm, other-oriented core — both carry the 2 Helper and the 9 Peacemaker in their tritypes, creating an instinctively harmonious and supportive bond. However, {{A}}'s lead 6 introduces an undercurrent of vigilance and anxiety that can unsettle {{B}}'s 9-led need for undisturbed calm, while {{B}}'s easy drift toward inertia and emotional merger can inadvertently trigger {{A}}'s deepest fear of being unsupported or abandoned. This is a relationship of genuine care and comfort that carries real risks of enabling each other's avoidance patterns.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both carry the supporting 2, making mutual care, generosity, and attentiveness feel completely natural — neither has to explain the impulse to show up for people.
- The shared 9 energy means both prize harmony and low-conflict environments; a shared evening or shared project feels easy and unforced.
- {{A}}'s loyalty (lead 6) and {{B}}'s steady, undemanding presence (lead 9) create a sense of reliable safety that both quietly crave.
- {{B}}'s supporting 5 can provide thoughtful, calm analysis that actually soothes {{A}}'s 6-driven worry rather than inflaming it.
- Neither is ego-driven or showy, so there's little competition for status or dominance in the relationship.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 6 generates anticipatory anxiety and a need to test trustworthiness; {{B}}'s lead 9 finds repeated loyalty-checks destabilizing to the settled peace they require.
- {{B}}'s 9-led inertia and tendency to merge with ambient mood can read to {{A}}'s 6 as evasiveness or hidden withdrawal — precisely the ambiguity that 6 finds most threatening.
- When stressed, {{B}}'s supporting 5 causes a cold, retreating detachment; this can feel like abandonment to {{A}}, activating 6 catastrophizing rather than patient waiting.
- Both suppress personal needs through the shared supporting 2, meaning resentments can quietly accumulate on both sides with neither person naming them directly.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s calm and slowness to react as indifference or hidden discontent, when {{B}} is almost always genuinely content in the moment — the lead 9 doesn't register as "fine" the way {{A}}'s 6 expects fine to look. Conversely, {{B}} reads {{A}}'s questioning, preparation for worst-case scenarios, and periodic reassurance-seeking as evidence of distrust or instability, when for {{A}} this vigilance is simply how love and commitment are expressed. Because both have 9 energy, both may assume the other is equally conflict-averse and hold back feedback — then be surprised when minor frictions have compounded into something larger.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should name anxiety explicitly rather than letting it surface as indirect questioning or loyalty tests; {{B}} responds far better to a direct "I'm feeling unsettled about X" than to a series of probing questions.
- {{B}} needs to resist the 9-lead habit of going vague or agreeable when actually uncomfortable; {{A}}'s 6 reads ambiguity as threat, so a clear "I'm okay, I just need quiet" is genuinely reassuring.
- Both should resist the shared 2 tendency to prioritize the other's comfort at the expense of honest self-disclosure — naming a need is not a burden in this pairing, it's necessary maintenance.
- Scheduling intentional check-ins (rather than waiting until a problem erupts) plays to {{A}}'s 6 desire for structure and {{B}}'s 9 preference for gradual, low-stakes conversation.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body: {{A}} can genuinely help {{B}} grow by modeling that naming problems and sitting with uncertainty does not destroy a relationship — the 6's willingness to raise concerns, when done without accusation, slowly erodes the 9's fear that conflict means dissolution. {{B}} in turn offers {{A}} something no amount of preparation can manufacture: a steady, non-anxious presence that demonstrates the world does not require constant monitoring to remain safe. The shared risk is collusion — both 6 and 9 can rationalize avoidance as keeping the peace, and the supporting 9 in {{A}} amplifies this pull. Real growth happens when both resist the comfortable harmony long enough to say what is actually true.

368-368.summary: When two 368 Justice Fighters meet, the connection is immediate and electric — they share the same drive for achievement, the same vigilance about loyalty and threat, and the same willingness to confront. The mirror dynamic is both a source of deep recognition and a source of real friction, because every strength each brings is also the exact blindspot the other carries. This pairing thrives when they channel their shared energy outward toward a common cause, and struggles when they turn that same combative clarity on each other.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both {{A}} and {{B}} lead with type 3, meaning they immediately recognize each other's ambition, efficiency, and results-orientation — there's no need to explain why winning matters.
- The shared 6 support means both value loyalty deeply; trust, once built, feels unusually solid and mutual between them.
- The shared 8 gut gives both a blunt, cut-through-the-noise communication style — neither has to soften language or tiptoe, which creates refreshing directness.
- Both are energized by standing up for a cause or fighting injustice together, and in a shared mission they can become a formidable, almost unstoppable team.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- Two lead-3s in the same relationship means two people competing — consciously or not — for the role of the most capable, most respected, most accomplished person in the room.
- The 8 support in both amplifies this into overt power struggles: neither {{A}} nor {{B}} backs down easily, and neither is particularly skilled at yielding without feeling diminished.
- The shared 6 vigilance can turn toxic in conflict, as both become suspicious of each other's motives and start scanning for betrayal or disloyalty where none exists.
- Image management (core 3) means both may refuse to show vulnerability to the other precisely because the other is the person who would see it most clearly.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} may read {{B}}'s drive as one-upmanship rather than genuine passion, and vice versa — because both know how a 3's ambition can shade into performance, they project that suspicion onto each other.
- When the 6 support is activated under stress, both can become anxious and reactive simultaneously, leaving no one in the pairing with the bandwidth to de-escalate — each interprets the other's anxiety as aggression.
- The 8 in both causes them to mistake bluntness for disrespect: what {{A}} means as honest feedback, {{B}} receives as a challenge to their competence, and the cycle escalates quickly because neither reads the other's intent charitably under pressure.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- Agree explicitly on who takes the lead in specific domains — without that structure, both will default to leading, and collisions are inevitable.
- When conflict heats up, name what's happening: "I think we're both in 8-mode right now" is more useful than escalating; shared self-awareness of the tritype pattern is a genuine asset here.
- {{A}} and {{B}} both need to practice asking before advising — the 3/8 combo in each makes them solution-oriented to a fault, and the other person frequently just needs to be heard, not fixed.
- Loyalty acknowledgments matter: both have a 6 underneath that craves reassurance that the relationship is solid, even when — especially when — things are tense.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
