- {{A}}'s supporting 3 and {{B}}'s lead 2 share a desire to contribute meaningfully and be recognized for their efforts, creating mutual admiration when healthy.
- {{B}}'s warmth and loyalty (2 lead, 6 support) can feel genuinely grounding for {{A}}, whose lead 1 often carries a heavy internal critic that {{B}}'s acceptance can soften.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 brings enthusiasm and forward momentum that {{B}}'s 6 anxiety finds reassuring rather than threatening.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 1 issues corrections and holds high standards naturally; {{B}}'s lead 2 experiences this as personal rejection rather than principled feedback, and the wound is real.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 can be confrontational and boundary-testing; {{A}}'s lead 1 responds to perceived pushiness with rigidity and quiet resentment rather than engagement.
- {{B}}'s 2 giving pattern often carries unconscious expectation of reciprocity — when {{A}}'s 3 is in achievement mode and doesn't notice, {{B}} accumulates hurt that can erupt through the 8.
- {{A}}'s supporting 7 avoids emotional discomfort and pivots to optimism; {{B}}'s 2/6 combination needs to process relational tension, not skip past it.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} tends to read {{B}}'s emotional intensity and care as manipulation or boundary violation — the 2's merging and the 8's directness together can feel like a pincer to {{A}}'s principled independence.
- {{B}} tends to read {{A}}'s critique and task-focus as coldness or ingratitude, when {{A}} is actually expressing care through quality and standards, not indifference.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 is image-aware and can appear performative; {{B}}'s lead 2 values authentic emotional connection and may distrust what looks like a polished front.
- {{B}}'s supporting 6 scans for reliability and consistency; {{A}}'s supporting 7 can drift toward new ideas and options in ways that trigger {{B}}'s loyalty-testing anxiety.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should name appreciation explicitly before offering any correction — {{B}}'s lead 2 genuinely cannot hear critique until it knows the relationship is safe.
- {{B}} should state needs and wants directly rather than through giving; {{A}}'s lead 1 values fairness and honesty and will respond far better to directness than to unspoken expectation.
- When conflict escalates, {{B}}'s 8 and {{A}}'s 1 can both harden into righteousness — both should watch for the moment they stop listening and start defending a position.
- {{A}} can use the 7's lightness to create emotional ease; {{B}} can use the 6's loyalty to remind {{A}} that the relationship itself is the point, not just the project.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} invites {{A}} toward the relational and emotional dimensions that the lead 1 tends to subordinate to principle — learning to value connection as an end rather than a means is real growth for {{A}}.
- {{A}} models for {{B}} that self-worth does not have to be earned through service; the lead 1's integrity-based identity can inspire {{B}}'s lead 2 to develop a more internally grounded sense of value.
- {{A}}'s supporting 3 in stress can slip into image management and cutting corners on honesty; {{B}}'s directness (via the 8) is genuinely useful here as a reality check.
- Together, they have the raw material to build something purposeful and deeply human — but only if {{A}} loosens the grip of the inner critic and {{B}} learns to ask rather than give its way into belonging.

316-927.summary: {{A}} leads with the Achiever's relentless drive for results, sharpened by a Reformer's standards and a Loyalist's vigilance — a combination that is productive, principled, and quietly anxious. {{B}} leads with the Peacemaker's deep need for harmony and merger, softened further by a Helper's warmth and an Enthusiast's optimistic reframing. These two can build a genuinely complementary bond, but the pairing carries a real risk: {{A}} pushes the agenda while {{B}} quietly absorbs it, until one day {{B}}'s 9-led passive resistance surfaces and neither person fully understands why.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 craves loyalty and a reliable "home base" — {{B}}'s 9+2 combination radiates exactly that kind of steady, accepting warmth.
- {{B}}'s supporting 7 brings levity and possibility-thinking that can cut through the tension {{A}}'s lead 3 and supporting 1 generate around performance.
- Both carry an other-oriented orientation: {{A}} through image-awareness and loyalty, {{B}} through merging and helping, so neither tends toward callousness.
- There's a shared gut-center thread — {{A}}'s supporting 1 and {{B}}'s lead 9 both have a deep, if differently expressed, sense of right order in the world.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 measures progress and worth through achievement; {{B}}'s lead 9 measures wellbeing through stillness and lack of pressure — these are fundamentally opposed metrics.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 will flag errors, inefficiencies, and moral lapses and feel compelled to correct them; {{B}}'s 9 experiences this as relentless criticism and will disengage rather than fight back.
- {{B}}'s supporting 7 can scatter energy and avoid follow-through, which is nearly intolerable for {{A}}'s 1-driven need for completion and correctness.
- When {{A}}'s supporting 6 anxiety spikes, it produces urgency and worst-case scanning; {{B}}'s 9 responds to urgency by going flat and slow, which reads to {{A}} as dangerous indifference.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} frequently reads {{B}}'s 9-led calm as passivity or lack of ambition, not recognizing it as a deeply held value of inner peace rather than an absence of direction.
- {{B}} often reads {{A}}'s 3-led drive as ego or status-chasing, missing the genuine fear underneath — the supporting 6's need for security and the 1's need to do things right.
- {{B}}'s 9 goes quiet or vague during tension as a self-protective move; {{A}}'s supporting 6 interprets silence as a threat to the relationship's reliability and escalates, which drives {{B}} further inward.
- {{A}} may genuinely not register how much {{B}}'s 2 and 9 are accommodating and contributing relationally, because it doesn't show up as visible output — which leaves {{B}} feeling invisible.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the 3's instinct to table-set agendas for every interaction; {{B}}'s 9 needs unstructured space to arrive at its own preferences, and pressure produces stonewalling, not agreement.
- {{B}} must practice naming wants and disagreements in the moment rather than deferring — the 9's habit of going along ensures short-term harmony but generates long-term resentment that surfaces as withdrawal.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 needs explicit verbal reassurance that the relationship is stable; {{B}}'s supporting 2 is well-equipped to offer this, but the 9 lead can forget to initiate it without a direct ask.
- When {{A}}'s 1 feels compelled to critique, framing it as "this is a standard I care about" rather than an evaluation of {{B}} personally will help {{B}}'s 2 not collapse into shame.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}}'s lead 9 offers {{A}} something rare and genuinely needed: a relationship where worth is not contingent on output, which is the core unmet need of the lead 3.
- {{A}}'s lead 3, in turn, can help {{B}}'s 9 activate — moving from potential to actual, from going-along to genuinely choosing — which is the core growth edge for 9.
- The risk in this pairing is a codependent groove where {{A}} sets all direction and {{B}} accommodates indefinitely; both must periodically audit whether {{B}} is genuinely present or just absent of conflict.
- At their best, {{A}} learns that rest is not failure and {{B}} learns that assertion is not aggression — and the 3's drive combined with the 9's groundedness produces a partnership that is both effective and human.

215-548.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share a genuine intellectual thread — the 5 appears in both tritypes — but they lead from opposite centers: {{A}} leads with heart-driven care and relational purpose, while {{B}} leads with head-driven detachment and sovereign autonomy. This creates a pairing with real depth potential and equally real friction, particularly around emotional need versus emotional distance.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:

- {{B}}'s supporting 4 and {{A}}'s lead 2 both value depth and authenticity in relationships — neither is satisfied with superficiality.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 and {{B}}'s supporting 4 share a strong internal compass around integrity, which builds mutual respect over time.
- {{A}} naturally attunes to what others need, which can feel quietly sustaining to {{B}}, who rarely gets that kind of attentive care without having to ask for it.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 2 is oriented toward closeness, reciprocity, and being needed; {{B}}'s lead 5 is oriented toward autonomy, conservation of energy, and minimal obligation — these are structurally opposing relational styles.
- {{A}} may interpret {{B}}'s habitual withdrawal as coldness or rejection, triggering the 2's core fear of being unwanted.
- {{B}}'s supporting 8 can be blunt and confrontational; {{A}}'s lead 2 tends to suppress direct conflict, which means tension builds invisibly until {{A}} overreacts or collapses.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 may critique or try to improve things around {{B}}, and {{B}}'s supporting 4 — already sensitive to being misunderstood — can take this personally even when it isn't meant that way.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} reads {{B}}'s detachment as emotional unavailability or ingratitude; {{B}} reads {{A}}'s attentiveness as an implicit demand for emotional reciprocity they didn't agree to.
- {{B}}'s lead 5 experiences {{A}}'s helpfulness as a subtle encroachment on autonomy — a form of obligation-creation — while {{A}} genuinely experiences it as love with no strings attached.
- When {{B}}'s supporting 4 surfaces with unexpected emotional intensity, {{A}} is often caught off guard, having assumed {{B}} was always the cool, contained 5; {{B}} may then feel exposed and retreat further.
- {{A}}'s 1 framing of problems in terms of right and wrong can feel moralistic to {{B}}, who prefers to operate from logic and personal sovereignty rather than ethical prescription.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should state needs directly rather than hoping {{B}} will notice and respond — {{B}}'s 5 does not passively scan for relational cues the way {{A}}'s 2 does.
- {{B}} should offer explicit verbal appreciation when {{A}} gives care; a single acknowledged 'thank you, that mattered' does more for {{A}}'s 2 than hours of implicit goodwill.
- {{A}} should resist the urge to fill {{B}}'s silences or solitude — the 5's withdrawal is about energy management, not a verdict on the relationship.
- {{B}} should flag when they're hitting a capacity limit before going cold, so {{A}} doesn't spiral into self-doubt; even a brief 'I need space to think' lands far better than disappearance.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} models something {{A}} deeply needs: the capacity to hold boundaries without guilt, to prioritize one's own inner life without needing approval — {{A}}'s underdeveloped self-care can mature through this pairing.
- {{A}} models something {{B}} quietly longs for: the ability to move toward people, to offer and receive warmth without it feeling like a loss of self — {{B}}'s supporting 4 is hungry for this even when the lead 5 resists it.
- The shared 5 energy provides a crucial 'safe zone' — intellectual engagement where both can be present without the vulnerability of emotional exposure, and from which deeper trust can grow.
- At their best, {{A}} becomes more autonomous and boundaried, and {{B}} becomes more relationally open; the growth is asymmetric but genuinely mutual.

368-468.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} share two of three tritype numbers — the supporting 6 and supporting 8 — which gives them a remarkable baseline of loyalty, directness, and shared intensity. The critical divergence is in the heart center: {{A}}'s lead 3 is image-aware, adaptive, and action-driven, while {{B}}'s lead 4 is authenticity-driven, emotionally deep, and identity-protective. This makes for a relationship that is simultaneously magnetic and combustible, with real potential for growth if both are willing to examine their core defenses.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared supporting 6 creates a powerful bond of loyalty — both {{A}} and {{B}} are deeply committed once trust is established and will show up for each other in adversity.
- The shared supporting 8 means both are direct, confrontational when provoked, and genuinely protective; neither will gaslight the other or play passive games.
- Both carry a strong sense of justice and dislike of hypocrisy, so they can align powerfully around shared causes, moral convictions, or mutual enemies.
- The combined 6-and-8 energy gives this pairing a reliable, street-smart solidarity — they both understand what it means to fight for something real.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 is fundamentally adaptive and image-conscious; {{A}} adjusts presentation to achieve goals, which {{B}}'s lead 4 instinctively reads as inauthenticity or even manipulation.
- {{B}}'s lead 4 lingers in emotional experience and needs to process feelings as real in themselves; {{A}} tends to treat emotion as either fuel for achievement or noise to be managed, which can make {{B}} feel dismissed.
- When conflict erupts, both the supporting 8 in {{A}} and the supporting 8 in {{B}} kick in simultaneously — neither will easily back down, and the shared 6 anxiety can escalate a disagreement into a perceived betrayal.
- {{A}} may silently judge {{B}} as self-indulgent; {{B}} may silently judge {{A}} as hollow — and with 8 support on both sides, these judgments rarely stay silent for long.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} interprets {{B}}'s emotional depth as a delay or obstacle: from a lead-3 perspective, feelings are meant to be processed quickly so action can resume, so {{B}}'s need to sit with pain reads as stalling.
- {{B}} interprets {{A}}'s goal-orientation and image-management as a mask: the lead-4 core fear is being without significance or authentic identity, so watching {{A}} shift tone or style strategically triggers suspicion about who {{A}} really is.
- {{A}}'s supporting 6 makes them loyal and anxious about the relationship's security, but they express this through doing and proving; {{B}}'s supporting 6 expresses it through questioning and testing — so both are anxious but their anxiety looks accusatory to the other.
- Neither realizes that both are, at root, seeking the same thing through different means: to be seen as genuinely valuable, not just useful.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist the reflex to reframe {{B}}'s emotional pain as a problem to be solved; naming the feeling out loud — even briefly — before moving to action signals to {{B}}'s lead 4 that the relationship is a safe place.
- {{B}} should recognize that {{A}}'s acts of loyalty, effort, and follow-through are real emotional expression, not substitutes for it; demanding verbal depth on {{A}}'s lead-3 timeline often produces performance rather than truth.
- When the shared 8 energy escalates a conflict, the one who steps back first is not losing — both should agree in advance on a pause signal before either has fully activated, because neither will de-escalate gracefully mid-confrontation.
- The shared supporting 6 means both respond well to explicit reassurance of commitment; stating "I'm not going anywhere" directly can interrupt a spiral that might otherwise be driven entirely by 6-based doubt.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} something genuinely difficult: the invitation to stop performing and encounter their own emotional interior, which the lead 3 habitually bypasses in pursuit of results — exposure to {{B}}'s emotional honesty can, over time, help {{A}} access real feeling rather than a curated version of it.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally valuable: the lead-3 capacity to move, execute, and convert inner intensity into visible external impact — {{B}}'s lead 4 can get marooned in longing and idealization, and {{A}}'s momentum can pull that energy into the world.
- Both grow by leaning into their shared supporting 8's courage: the willingness to be honest not just in confrontation but in vulnerability, which is harder for both than any fight they will ever have.

417-739.summary: {{A}} and {{B}} are drawn together by a shared streak of visionary idealism — both carry the 7's appetite for meaning and possibility — but they approach life from fundamentally different emotional altitudes. {{A}} leads from the heart with a 4's need for depth, authenticity, and emotional truth, while {{B}} leads from the head with a 7's drive toward momentum, reframing, and forward motion. This pairing has real creative spark but requires deliberate navigation of the gap between depth and breadth.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- Both share the 7 archetype: {{A}}'s supporting 7 and {{B}}'s lead 7 generate a mutual love of ideas, novelty, and expansive conversation that can feel electric.
- {{A}}'s 4 and {{B}}'s supporting 3 both care about making something meaningful — there's a shared orientation toward creative output and leaving a mark.
- {{B}}'s gut-supporting 9 brings a relaxed acceptance that can genuinely soothe {{A}}'s 4-driven self-doubt and inner tension.
- When {{A}} and {{B}} are both inspired, they can co-create boldly — {{A}} supplying emotional resonance and {{B}} supplying enthusiasm and execution energy.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 4 needs to sit inside difficult feelings and be witnessed there; {{B}}'s lead 7 instinctively reframes, fast-forwards, or brightens the room, which {{A}} experiences as dismissal.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 is exacting, critical, and morally serious — {{B}}'s supporting 9 hates confrontation and will disengage or go flat rather than engage with {{A}}'s critiques.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 prizes image, productivity, and visible success in ways that can feel performative or hollow to {{A}}'s 4, who is allergic to inauthenticity.
- {{A}} tends toward sustained depth and {{B}} toward stimulating breadth — over time this can leave {{A}} feeling emotionally unmet and {{B}} feeling dragged into heaviness.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body:
- {{A}} is likely to read {{B}}'s 7-led optimism and reframing as emotional avoidance or superficiality, when {{B}} is genuinely trying to move toward life rather than away from it.
- {{B}} is likely to read {{A}}'s emotional intensity and melancholic honesty as self-indulgence or drama, when {{A}} is actually doing serious internal work that is core to their identity.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 can deliver feedback with a precision that feels like judgment; {{B}}'s 9 will absorb it silently and build quiet resentment rather than push back, leaving {{A}} unaware any damage was done.
- {{B}}'s supporting 3 can shift into performance mode under stress, and {{A}}'s 4 will sense the inauthenticity immediately — often withdrawing before {{B}} even knows something shifted.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{B}} should resist the 7 reflex to fix or reframe {{A}}'s emotional states; simply naming "I hear that this matters deeply to you" lands far better than redirection.
- {{A}} should signal explicitly when they need depth versus when they're open to levity — {{B}}'s 7 will default to lightness without malice and benefits from a clear cue.
- When {{A}}'s supporting 1 has a critique, framing it as a shared standard rather than a personal judgment helps {{B}}'s 9 stay present instead of shutting down.
- {{B}} should watch for the 3-supporting pattern of glossing over conflict to protect image — {{A}}'s 4 will always prefer a harder truth to a polished non-answer.

sections.heading: Growth dynamic
sections.body:
- {{B}} offers {{A}} genuine medicine: the 7's capacity to hold possibility and move forward can loosen the 4's grip on suffering and idealized longing, nudging {{A}} toward the healthier spaciousness that 7 energy provides.
- {{A}} offers {{B}} something equally valuable: the 4's insistence on emotional truth and depth pushes {{B}} past the 7's habitual gloss, supporting the kind of self-knowledge that {{B}}'s lead type tends to outrun.
- The shared 7 in both tritypes acts as a genuine bridge — when {{A}} and {{B}} meet in that register, there is real mutual recognition that can anchor the relationship through harder passages.
- Long-term, {{A}} grows by trusting that joy and depth are not opposites, and {{B}} grows by discovering that slowing down to feel something fully does not mean losing forward motion — lessons this pairing is uniquely positioned to teach each other.

315-945.summary: {{A}}'s lead 3 drives toward measurable achievement and polished competence, while {{B}}'s lead 9 orients toward harmony, integration, and unhurried presence — a pairing that can be genuinely complementary but requires real effort to bridge different paces and emotional registers. Their shared supporting 5 gives them a valuable intellectual meeting ground, but the contrast between {{A}}'s heart-center ambition and {{B}}'s gut-center stillness will surface repeatedly. This relationship has real potential, but only if both people are willing to name the tension rather than let it quietly accumulate.

sections.heading: Where you click
sections.body:
- The shared 5 in both tritypes creates immediate intellectual rapport — both value expertise, depth of knowledge, and getting things right.
- {{B}}'s 9-led calm offers {{A}} a rare reprieve from the performance treadmill that the lead 3 sustains, and {{A}} often experiences {{B}} as unusually non-threatening.

- {{B}}'s 4 can genuinely appreciate the craft and precision that {{A}}'s 1 brings to their work, recognizing a kind of quiet artistry in it.

sections.heading: Where you grate
sections.body:
- {{A}}'s lead 3 sets a pace — goal-oriented, efficient, results-focused — that {{B}}'s lead 9 experiences as relentless and exhausting.
- {{A}}'s supporting 1 introduces a critical, improvement-oriented edge that can feel like constant low-grade judgment to {{B}}, whose 9 is hypervigilant to any sense of being corrected or found lacking.
- {{B}}'s supporting 4 hungers for raw emotional authenticity, and {{A}}'s lead 3 tends to package emotions for external palatability — {{B}} will sense this gap even when they can't name it.
- {{B}}'s 9-led tendency to avoid conflict and merge with the dominant agenda can frustrate {{A}}'s 1, which actually respects directness and principled pushback.

sections.heading: How you misunderstand each other
sections.body: {{A}} is likely to misread {{B}}'s 9-led stillness and lack of urgency as passivity, disengagement, or wasted potential — particularly when {{A}}'s 3 is in a high-output phase and needs a partner who matches the energy. Meanwhile, {{B}} can misread {{A}}'s polished efficiency as emotional superficiality or inauthenticity, which {{B}}'s supporting 4 finds quietly alienating. {{A}} packages feelings into performance-ready form; {{B}} wants feelings presented raw and unedited — they are often speaking different emotional dialects without realizing it. {{B}} also tends to say yes when they mean maybe, and {{A}} takes that yes at face value, leading to unspoken resentment on {{B}}'s side that {{A}} never saw coming.

sections.heading: Communication tips
sections.body:
- {{A}} should resist presenting polished conclusions and instead open a genuine question to {{B}} — the lead 9 needs space to form and voice an opinion rather than simply react to one.
